title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣東鄉試錄序
聖天子統御天下之十年
德化流洽民用康阜乃益稽古右文
誕敷詩書禮樂之教以惠幸天下
天下之士莫不爭先淬濯樂於自
新期以仰荅
休恩康誥有云作新民今之所以鼓
舞歆動乎其自新之民者既有徳
===
以為本有詩書禮樂以為輔亦惟
置選舉爵賞之階以為勸如是而
已廣東為嶺南大藩士之沾沭
德化以從事乎詩書禮樂盖百有餘
年其起而登高科縻好爵者亦已
彬彬其盛况有總鎮太監陳瑄平
蠻將軍平鄉伯陳政耀兵出銳以
廓清奸氛有足以佐文教贊治功
punctuated:
廣東鄉試錄序
聖天子統御天下之十年，德化流洽，民用康阜，乃益稽古右文，誕敷《詩》《書》禮樂之教，以惠幸天下。天下之士，莫不爭先淬濯，樂於自新，期以仰荅休恩。《康誥》有云：「作新民。」今之所以鼓舞歆動乎其自新之民者，既有徳以為本，有《詩》《書》禮樂以為輔，亦惟置選舉爵賞之階以為勸，如是而已。廣東為嶺南大藩，士之沾沭德化、以從事乎《詩》《書》禮樂，盖百有餘年；其起而登高科、縻好爵者，亦已彬彬其盛。况有總鎮太監陳瑄、平蠻將軍平鄉伯陳政，耀兵出銳，以廓清奸氛，有足以佐文教、贊治功，
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

In the tenth year of the Sacred Son of Heaven's rule over the realm, his virtuous transformation has flowed forth and permeated everywhere, and the people accordingly enjoy peace and abundance. He has therefore all the more examined antiquity and championed civil culture, broadly extending the teachings of the Odes, the Documents, rites, and music so as to favor and bless the world. Among the scholars of the realm, there are none who do not vie to be the first to cleanse and polish themselves, delighting in self-renewal and hoping to look up and repay this gracious benevolence. The "Announcement to Kang" (Kang gao) says: "To stir up the new people." Today, the means by which those self-renewing people are inspired and moved—having already virtue as the foundation and the Odes, the Documents, rites, and music as the support—consists simply in establishing the steps of selection, noble rank, and reward as an encouragement, and nothing more.

Guangdong is a great province South of the Ranges. For well over a hundred years, its scholars have been steeped in virtuous transformation and have devoted themselves to the Odes, the Documents, rites, and music; those who have risen to attain high examination degrees and hold fine offices are already refined and flourishing in their abundance. Moreover, there are the Grand Defender Eunuch Chen Xuan 陳瑄 and the General Who Pacifies the Man, Earl of Pingxiang, Chen Zheng 陳政, who display military might and lead forth elite troops to sweep away the noxious miasma of rebels, which suffices to assist civil education and aid the achievements of governance; …

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而都察院右副都御史吳琛又新
受
簡命加總督兩廣諸軍事舉庶政而
一新之於
朝廷之所以鼓舞歆動乎其自新之
民者必求其所為本與其所為輔
表明倡導使勉就選舉爵賞之階
士學為自新而欲推以新民者顧
===
不繼奮於是哉時監察御史江泝
建節来巡適當選舉之期因慨然
言曰吾将於此驗士所以自新之
效不可以不慎遂勤日夜嚴規程
而防範斥故常之弊文藝戒陳腐
之習務以新嶺南士俗之聞見乃
與布政使周鐸袁凱按察使呂洪
叅政劉昌謝燫卓天錫副使章格
punctuated: 而都察院右副都御史吳琛又新受簡命，加總督兩廣諸軍事，舉庶政而一新之。於朝廷之所以鼓舞歆動乎其自新之民者，必求其所為本與其所為輔，表明倡導，使勉就選舉爵賞之階。士學為自新而欲推以新民者，顧不繼奮於是哉！時監察御史江泝建節来巡，適當選舉之期，因慨然言曰：「吾将於此驗士所以自新之效，不可以不慎。」遂勤日夜，嚴規程而防範，斥故常之弊；文藝戒陳腐之習，務以新嶺南士俗之聞見。乃與布政使周鐸、袁凱，按察使呂洪，叅政劉昌、謝燫、卓天錫，副使章格、
translation_en:
…and Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate Wu Chen 吳琛 has also newly received an imperial commission, with the added title of Supreme Commander of Military Affairs in Liangguang, taking up the manifold affairs of administration and renewing them all at once. As for the means by which the Court rouses and inspires its self-renewing people, he surely seeks out what serves as the foundation and what serves as the auxiliary, making them manifest and leading the way so as to encourage them to strive toward the steps of selection, noble rank, and reward. How then could scholars who learn for the sake of self-renewal, and who wish to extend this to renew the people, fail to rouse themselves in succession at this time?

At this time, Investigating Censor Jiang Su 江泝 came bearing his credentials on a tour of inspection. It happened to be the period of the examinations and selection, and so he declared with deep feeling: "In this I shall test the efficacy of how the scholars renew themselves; I cannot fail to be cautious." Thereupon he toiled day and night, tightened the regulations and took strict precautions to cast out routine abuses, and in literary compositions warned against stale and hackneyed habits, striving to renew the outlook and experience of the scholars and customs of Lingnan. He then consulted with Administration Commissioners Zhou Duo 周鐸 and Yuan Kai 袁凱, Surveillance Commissioner Lü Hong 呂洪, Administration Vice Commissioners Liu Chang 劉昌, Xie Lian 謝燫, and Zhuo Tianxi 卓天錫, Surveillance Vice Commissioners Zhang Ge 章格,…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
馮定孔鏞涂棐參議傅實僉事俞
俊陶魯林錦陳𤇍諸正陳昭提學
僉事胡榮謀聘儒紳集羣職且獎
飭其士之就選舉者革其舊而新
是圖士亦以聞見之新相與堅其
志作其氣試之日洪親蒞之而凱
與昌司提調格與俊任監巡合試
者千五百人得士七十有五實精
選也孜叨典文衡僭因小錄之成
而序之曰夫士之欲有用於天下
必先有以治其心心之所具者充
之可以配天地一蔽於私則銷鑠
殆盡近而無以立其身况及於人
乎是故貴自新也能加之淬濯而
日新焉則其可以配天地者將復
具於我推之而無不準用之而無
punctuated:
馮定、孔鏞、涂棐，參議傅實，僉事俞俊、陶魯、林錦、陳𤇍、諸正、陳昭，提學僉事胡榮，謀聘儒紳，集羣職，且獎飭其士之就選舉者，革其舊而新是圖。士亦以聞見之新，相與堅其志、作其氣。試之日，洪親蒞之，而凱與昌司提調，格與俊任監巡。合試者千五百人，得士七十有五，實精選也。

孜叨典文衡，僭因小錄之成而序之曰：夫士之欲有用於天下，必先有以治其心。心之所具者，充之可以配天地；一蔽於私，則銷鑠殆盡，近而無以立其身，况及於人乎？是故貴自新也。能加之淬濯而日新焉，則其可以配天地者將復具於我，推之而無不準，用之而無
translation_en:
… Feng Ding 馮定, Kong Yong 孔鏞, and Tu Fei 涂棐; Administration Vice Commissioner Fu Shi 傅實; Surveillance Assistant Commissioners Yu Jun 俞俊, Tao Lu 陶魯, Lin Jin 林錦, Chen Ying 陳𤇍, Zhu Zheng 諸正, and Chen Zhao 陳昭; and Education-Intendant Surveillance Assistant Commissioner Hu Rong 胡榮—consulted on inviting Confucian gentry, assembling the various officials, and furthermore encouraging and admonishing the scholars who were presenting themselves for selection, so that they might cast off the old and strive for the new. The scholars likewise, through the renewal of what they heard and saw, mutually strengthened their resolve and roused their spirit. On the day of the examination, [Surveillance Commissioner] Lü Hong 呂洪 personally attended it, while [Administration Commissioner] Yuan Kai 袁凱 and [Administration Vice Commissioner] Liu Chang 劉昌 served as Proctors, and [Surveillance Vice Commissioner] Zhang Ge 章格 and [Surveillance Assistant Commissioner] Yu Jun assumed charge of surveillance and inspection. In all, one thousand five hundred candidates were examined, and seventy-five scholars were obtained—truly a refined selection.

I, Zi 孜, having had the undeserved honor of presiding over the literary balance [as Examiner], have presumed upon the completion of this brief record to write its preface, saying: Now, if a scholar wishes to be of use to the world, he must first have the means to govern his mind. When that with which the mind is endowed is fully developed, it can become the counterpart of Heaven and Earth; yet once it is obscured by selfishness, it is melted away almost completely—near at hand, one has no means to establish oneself, much less extend it to others! For this reason, self-renewal is prized. If one is able to subject it to tempering and cleansing so as to renew it daily, then that which can be the counterpart of Heaven and Earth will again be complete within oneself; when extended, there will be nothing it does not measure up to, and when put to use, there will be nothing…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
不化於事業之著夫孰得而禦士
之登是錄者既嘗樂育乎
德化之中以從事詩書禮樂而學為
自新尚思今日大臣表明倡導之
功與憲臣及藩臬諸重臣獎飭期
待之意皆所以宣
聖天子惠幸之恩以自致於新而欲以
新士俗者也其可不推其自新以
===
新乎民而無負乎哉惟無所負斯
然後身名光榮有以新嶺南之聞
見又將以新天下之聞見矣爾多
士勉之孜日望之是歲八月既望
江西吉安府萬安縣儒學教諭吳孜
謹序
punctuated:
不化，於事業之著，夫孰得而禦？士之登是錄者，既嘗樂育乎德化之中，以從事《詩》《書》禮樂而學為自新，尚思今日大臣表明倡導之功，與憲臣及藩臬諸重臣獎飭期待之意，皆所以宣聖天子惠幸之恩，以自致於新，而欲以新士俗者也。其可不推其自新以新乎民，而無負乎哉？惟無所負斯，然後身名光榮，有以新嶺南之聞見，又將以新天下之聞見矣。爾多士勉之！孜日望之。

是歲八月既望，江西吉安府萬安縣儒學教諭吳孜謹序。
translation_en:
…not be transformed; as for the manifestation of their achievements in public affairs, who then could hinder them? The scholars whose names are entered in this record have already rejoiced in being nurtured within our dynasty's moral transformation, devoting themselves to the Odes, the Documents, rites, and music in learning to renew themselves. May they reflect upon the merit of the grand ministers today in making clear and leading the way, as well as the intentions of the censorial officials and the senior provincial administrative and judicial officials in encouraging, admonishing, and holding high expectations for them—all of which serve to proclaim the grace and favor of the Sacred Son of Heaven, so as to attain self-renewal themselves while desiring thereby to renew the customs of the scholars. How could they fail to extend their own self-renewal to renew the people, and thus not prove ungrateful? Only when they fail not in these expectations will their persons and reputations attain glory, having the means to renew what is heard and seen in Lingnan, and going on to renew what is heard and seen throughout the realm. Exert yourselves, all you scholars! I, Zi, look forward to this day by day.

On the sixteenth day of the eighth month of this year [September 26, 1474], respectfully written as a preface by Wu Zi 吳孜, Instructor of the Confucian School of Wan'an County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi.

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第一塲
四書
斯民也三代之所以直道而行也
衣錦尚絅惡其文之著也故君子之道
闇然而日章
觀水有術必觀其瀾日月有明容光必
照焉
易
===
后以財成天地之道輔相天地之宜以
左右民初九拔茅茹以其彙征吉
利見大人亨利貞
易與天地準故能彌綸天地之道仰以
觀於天文俯以察於地理是故知幽
明之故原始反終故知死生之說精
氣為物游魂為變是故知鬼神之情
狀與天地相似故不違知周乎萬物
punctuated:
第一塲

四書
斯民也，三代之所以直道而行也。
衣錦尚絅，惡其文之著也。故君子之道，闇然而日章。
觀水有術，必觀其瀾。日月有明，容光必照焉。

易
后以財成天地之道，輔相天地之宜，以左右民。初九，拔茅茹，以其彙，征吉。
利見大人，亨，利貞。
易與天地準，故能彌綸天地之道。仰以觀於天文，俯以察於地理，是故知幽明之故。原始反終，故知死生之說。精氣為物，游魂為變，是故知鬼神之情狀。與天地相似，故不違；知周乎萬物，
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books
"These people are the same people with whom the Three Dynasties pursued the straightforward way."
"Over a brocade robe she wears a plain single garment, disliking the display of its elegance. Thus the Way of the noble person is unobtrusive, yet it grows more illustrious day by day."
"There is an art to contemplating water: one must look at its foaming waves. The sun and moon have their brilliance, and wherever a ray of light can enter, they never fail to illuminate it."

Classic of Changes (Yi)
"Thus the sovereign regulates and completes the Way of heaven and earth, and furthers and regulates the adaptations of heaven and earth, in order to aid the people. Nine at the beginning: Pulling up thatch grass with its tangled roots, each according to its kind. Going forward brings good fortune."
"It is advantageous to see the great man. Success. It is advantageous to be steadfast and upright."
"The Changes are on a par with heaven and earth, and therefore can wholly encompass and order the Way of heaven and earth. Looking up, by means of it one contemplates the patterns of heaven; looking down, one examines the lines and veins of earth; thus one knows the causes of the obscure and the manifest. One traces things to their beginnings and follows them to their ends; thus one knows the explanation of life and death. Refined qi forms things, and the wandering soul produces change; thus one knows the conditions and characteristics of ghosts and spirits. Because he resembles heaven and earth, he does not go contrary to them. His wisdom encompasses all things, …"

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而道濟天下故不過旁行而不流樂
天知命故不憂安土敦乎仁故能愛
範圍天地之化而不過曲成萬物而
而不遺通乎晝夜之道而知故神无
方而易无體
其旨遠其辭文
書
至誠感神矧茲有苗禹拜昌言曰俞班
===
師振旅
人惟求舊器非求舊惟新古我先王暨
乃祖乃父胥及逸勤予敢動用非罰
世選爾勞予不掩爾善
越三日庚戌太保乃以庶殷攻位于洛
汭越五日甲寅位成若翼日乙卯周
公朝至于洛則達觀于新邑營越三
日丁巳用牲于郊牛二越翼日戊午
punctuated:
而道濟天下，故不過。旁行而不流，樂天知命，故不憂。安土敦乎仁，故能愛。範圍天地之化而不過，曲成萬物而而不遺，通乎晝夜之道而知，故神无方而易无體。
其旨遠，其辭文。
《書》：
「至誠感神，矧茲有苗。」禹拜昌言，曰：「俞。」班師振旅。
「人惟求舊，器非求舊，惟新。古我先王暨乃祖乃父，胥及逸勤，予敢動用非罰？世選爾勞，予不掩爾善。」
越三日庚戌，太保乃以庶殷攻位于洛汭。越五日甲寅，位成。若翼日乙卯，周公朝至于洛，則達觀于新邑營。越三日丁巳，用牲于郊，牛二。越翼日戊午，
translation_en:
…and his Way brings aid to all under Heaven, so he does not err. He acts extensively yet is not swept away; he rejoices in Heaven and knows its decree, so he is free from anxiety. Content in his abode and earnest in benevolence, he is therefore able to love. He encompasses the transformations of Heaven and Earth without erring, and brings the myriad things to completion in all their intricacies without leaving anything out. He comprehends the Way of day and night and understands it. Therefore, spirit has no fixed direction and the Changes have no corporeal form."
"Its import is far-reaching, its wording refined."
Book of Documents (Shu):
"'Utmost sincerity moves the spirits; how much more so this ruler of Miao!' Yu bowed to these admirable words and said, 'Yes!' Thereupon he led back the army and marshaled the troops."
"'In men, one seeks only the old; in vessels, one does not seek the old, but only the new. Of old, our former kings, together with your grandfathers and fathers, shared in both ease and toil; how could I dare to lightly inflict undeserved punishments? For generations your labors have been recorded, and I do not conceal your goodness.'"
"Three days later, on the gengxu day, the Grand Guardian (Taibao) led the multitude of Yin to prepare the altar sites at the bend of the Luo River. Five days later, on the jiayin day, the sites were completed. On the following day, yimao, the Duke of Zhou (Zhougong) arrived at Luo in the morning and thoroughly inspected the layout of the new city. Three days later, on the dingsi day, he offered victims at the suburban sacrifice: two bulls. On the following day, wuwu,…"

天齊于民，俾我一日。非終惟終，在人。
《詩》：

工祝致告，徂賚孝孫。苾芬孝祀，神嗜飮食，卜爾百福，如幾如式。旣齊旣稷，旣匡旣敕，永錫爾極，時萬時億。禮儀旣備，鍾鼓旣戒，孝孫徂位，工祝致告。

translation_en:
…and then offered sacrifice to the altars of soil and grain in the new city: one bull, one sheep, and one pig."
"Heaven regulates the people, granting me a single day's charge. Whether a man comes to an untimely end or lives out his allotted span rests with men."
Classic of Poetry (Shi):
"Now let us prepare for the change of the year, and enter this house to dwell."
"The skillful invocators convey the message, going to bestow it upon the filial descendant: 'Fragrant has been your filial sacrifice; the spirits have enjoyed the drink and food. They confer on you a hundred blessings, right on time and in due measure. You have been reverent and prompt, you have been upright and cautious; forever will they grant you the highest blessings, in tens of thousands and in hundreds of millions.' Every ceremony has been completed, the bells and drums have given the signal; the filial descendant goes to his place, and the skillful invocator conveys the announcement."
"The male and female phoenixes fly about, their wings rustling as they settle down at their resting place.Numerous are the king's fine officers; it is the lord who employs them, and they are devoted to the Son of Heaven. The male and female phoenixes fly about, their wings rustling as they soar up to heaven. Numerous are the king's fine men; it is the lord who commands them, and they show affection toward the common people. The male and female phoenixes sing on that high ridge; the parasol trees grow on that eastern slope."

translation_en:
… and the men of Cao attacked Song. [14th year of Duke Zhuang] Shusun Zhouqiu led an army and dismantled the walls of Hou; Jisun Si and Zhongsun Heji led an army and dismantled the walls of Bi; the Duke laid siege to Cheng. [12th year of Duke Ding]

They thereupon attacked Chu. [4th year of Duke Xi] The Marquis of Jin, the army of Qi, the army of Song, and the army of Qin fought with the men of Chu at Chengpu. [28th year of Duke Xi] The Duke met Viscount Liu, the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Cai, the Marquis of Wei, the Viscount of Chen, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Dun, the Viscount of Hu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, the Viscount of Little Zhu, and Guo Xia of Qi at Shaoling, and made an incursion into Chu. [4th year of Duke Ding]

The Duke met the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Cai, the Earl of Zheng, the Viscount of Wei, and the Viscount of Ju, and made a covenant at Jiantu; the Duke had an audience at the King's residence. [28th year of Duke Xi] The Duke met the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, the Earl of Cao, and Zhao Dun of Jin, and on the guiyou day, they made a joint covenant at Xincheng; the Duke arrived back from the meeting; the men of Jin sought to install Jiezai in Zhu. [14th year of Duke Wen]

They made a joint covenant at Xi. [9th year of Duke Xiang] The Duke arrived back from attacking Zheng. [10th year of Duke Xiang] They made a joint covenant north of the city of Bo; the Duke arrived back from attacking Zheng; they met at Xiaoyu; the Duke arrived back from the meeting. [11th year of Duke Xiang]

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
禮記
毋失經紀以初為常
樂所以脩內也禮所以脩外也禮樂交
錯於中發形於外
故玄酒在室醴醆在戶粢醍在堂澄酒
在下陳其犧牲備其鼎俎列其琴瑟
管磬鐘鼓脩其祝嘏以降上神與其
先祖以正君臣以篤父子以睦兄弟
===
以齊上下夫婦有所是謂承天之祐
金石絲竹樂之器也詩言其志也歌咏
其聲也舞動其容也三者本於心然
後樂器從之
第二場
論
治天下以正風俗得賢才為本
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
punctuated:
《禮記》
毋失經紀，以初為常。
樂所以脩內也，禮所以脩外也。禮樂交錯於中，發形於外。
故玄酒在室，醴醆在戶，粢醍在堂，澄酒在下。陳其犧牲，備其鼎俎，列其琴瑟管磬鐘鼓，脩其祝嘏，以降上神與其先祖。以正君臣，以篤父子，以睦兄弟，以齊上下，夫婦有所。是謂承天之祐。
金石絲竹，樂之器也。詩，言其志也；歌，咏其聲也；舞，動其容也。三者本於心，然後樂器從之。

第二場
論
治天下以正風俗得賢才為本
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
translation_en:
Record of Rites (Liji):
"Do not lose the guiding principles, taking the beginning as the constant standard."
"Music is that by which the interior is cultivated; rites are that by which the exterior is cultivated. Rites and music interweave within and manifest in form without."
"Therefore, the dark water is in the inner chamber, the sweet wine and clarified wine are at the door, the reddish wine is in the hall, and the clear wine is below. They set forth the sacrificial victims, prepare the tripods and stands, array the zithers, pipes, chime-stones, bells, and drums, and order the prayers and benedictions, so as to bring down the spirits above and their ancestors; to rectify the relation between ruler and minister, to deepen the affection between father and son, to harmonize elder and younger brothers, to regulate superior and inferior, and to ensure that husband and wife have their proper places. This is called receiving the blessings of Heaven."
"Metal, stone, silk, and bamboo are the instruments of music. Poetry expresses the intent; song prolongs the voice; dance moves the bearing. These three originate in the mind, and only afterward do the musical instruments follow them."

Second Session
Discourse:
"Governing All Under Heaven Takes Rectifying Customs and Obtaining Worthy Talents as Its Foundation"
Imperial Edict, Mandate, and Memorial [Tested on one topic from among these]:

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
擬漢高帝定元功位次詔
擬唐以韓愈為國子祭酒誥
擬宋以劉珙同知樞密院事謝表
判語
官文書稽程
立嫡子違法
良賤為婚姻
主將不固守
===
屏去人服食
第三場
策
問古先聖王之治天下必旌別淑慝示
之勸懲書云董正治官詩云式序在
位盖先正百官而後及萬民也舜有
天下選於眾舉皐陶不仁者遠矣湯
有天下選於眾舉伊尹不仁者遠矣
punctuated:
擬漢高帝定元功位次詔。
擬唐以韓愈為國子祭酒誥。
擬宋以劉珙同知樞密院事謝表。
判語
官文書稽程。
立嫡子違法。
良賤為婚姻。
主將不固守。
屏去人服食。
第三場
策
問：古先聖王之治天下，必旌別淑慝，示之勸懲。《書》云：「董正治官。」《詩》云：「式序在位。」盖先正百官，而後及萬民也。舜有天下，選於眾，舉皐陶，不仁者遠矣；湯有天下，選於眾，舉伊尹，不仁者遠矣。
translation_en:
Imitation of an Imperial Edict by Emperor Gao of Han Determining the Order of Precedence for Those of Foremost Merit.
Imitation of an Imperial Mandate of the Tang Appointing Han Yu 韓愈 as Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.
Imitation of a Memorial of Thanks of the Song upon the Appointment of Liu Gong 劉珙 as Co-Administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

Legal Judgments
Delay in the Transmission of Official Documents.
Illegally Establishing an Heir Apparent.
Marriage between Commoners and Base Persons.
Commanding Generals Failing to Hold Their Posts Firmly.
Depriving a Person of Clothing and Food.

Third Session
Policy Questions
Question: When the ancient sage-kings governed all under Heaven, they necessarily distinguished between the good and the wicked in order to demonstrate encouragement and warning. The Book of Documents (Shu 書) says: "Strictly regulate the governing officials." The Book of Odes (Shi 詩) says: "Ordering those in office according to their merits." This is because one first rectifies the hundred officials, and only afterward extends this to the myriad people. When Shun 舜 possessed all under Heaven, he selected from among the multitude and raised up Gao Yao 皐陶, and those who were inhumane were kept afar; when Tang 湯 possessed all under Heaven, he selected from among the multitude and raised up Yi Yin 伊尹, and those who were inhumane were kept afar. …

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
豈亦勸懲明而淑慝分歟我
朝
太祖高皇帝大誥三編
太宗文皇帝為善陰騭孝順事實二書
宣宗章皇帝五倫書皆以訓戒天下敦勸懲
別淑慝於詩書所云固同一揆而視
舜湯所舉抑亦有可考者歟且所載
有剛斷嫉惡不容奸偽者又有交不
===
變色德優於才者其與斷獄四百人
無怨言深厚不伐絕口舊恩果何優
劣有夙夜在公恪遵古道者又有超
出羣職進膺嘉勞者其與為政公忠
注當貴顯教化大行政有三異果何
得失有禁戢士卒市肆不移者又有
發廩賑饑民多來歸者其與申令戢
下所至悅服救灾有法從如歸市果
punctuated: 豈亦勸懲明而淑慝分歟？我朝太祖高皇帝《大誥三編》、太宗文皇帝《為善陰騭》、《孝順事實》二書、宣宗章皇帝《五倫書》，皆以訓戒天下，敦勸懲、別淑慝，於《詩》、《書》所云固同一揆，而視舜、湯所舉抑亦有可考者歟？且所載有剛斷嫉惡、不容奸偽者，又有交不變色、德優於才者，其與斷獄四百、人無怨言，深厚不伐、絕口舊恩，果何優劣？有夙夜在公、恪遵古道者，又有超出羣職、進膺嘉勞者，其與為政公忠、注當貴顯，教化大行、政有三異，果何得失？有禁戢士卒、市肆不移者，又有發廩賑饑、民多來歸者，其與申令戢下、所至悅服，救灾有法、從如歸市，果
translation_en: Is this not also because encouragement and punishment were clear, and the good and the wicked were distinguished? In our dynasty, the Three Compilations of Grand Pronouncements (Dagao sanbian) by Grand Progenitor Emperor Gao (Taizu, the Hongwu Emperor), the two books Secret Rewards for Doing Good (Weishan yinzhi) and True Examples of Filial Piety (Xiaoshun shishi) by Grand Ancestor Emperor Wen (Taizong, the Yongle Emperor), and the Book of the Five Human Relationships (Wulun shu) by Ancestor of Announcements Emperor Zhang (Xuanzong, the Xuande Emperor) all serve to instruct and admonish the realm, reinforcing encouragement and punishment and distinguishing the good from the wicked. They are certainly grounded in the same principle as what is said in the Book of Odes (Shi) and the Book of Documents (Shu); yet compared with those raised up by Shun and Tang, are there also matters in them that can be examined? Furthermore, among the accounts recorded therein, there is one who was resolute and decisive, hated evil, and tolerated no treachery or falsehood, and another whose countenance never changed in his dealings with others and whose virtue surpassed his talent—how do they compare in superiority or inferiority with him who decided four hundred criminal cases without anyone uttering a word of resentment, and him who was deep and magnanimous without boasting and never spoke of past favors? There is one who attended to public duty early and late and reverently followed the ancient way, and another who stood out above the multitude of officials and was advanced to receive commendation for his labors—how do their merits and shortcomings compare with him who governed with public-spirited loyalty and was noted down as destined for noble prominence, and him under whom moral transformation greatly prevailed and whose administration produced three marvels? There is one who restrained his soldiers so that the market stalls did not even shift, and another who opened the granaries to relieve the starving so that the people came in great numbers to submit—how do their similarities and differences compare with him who reiterated orders to restrain his subordinates so that wherever he went people gladly submitted, and him who had a method for disaster relief so that people followed him as if flocking to a market …

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
何同異有思母不置悲戚而卒者又
有齧蛆刲股姑獲賜葬者其與不許
歸養毀不勝哀悲慟嘔血聞者泣下
果何甄別此諸生素所誦習而講求
者今欲舉一賢者則使不賢者勸進
一能者則使不能者戒何道以致之
歟願詳對毋讓
問朱子著小學家禮二書以為脩身齊
===
家治國平天下之本今天下所通習
者請舉其槩從諸生論之夫立教明
倫敬身小學一書之大綱也立教篇
載教非一端而先於母教至稽古始
言父教而亦後於母教何歟其亦有
可考歟明倫之目五敬身之目四可
得而詳歟然既立為大綱而又稽古
以證之矣何又取嘉言以廣之而善
punctuated:
何同異？有思母不置、悲戚而卒者，又有齧蛆刲股、姑獲賜葬者，其與不許歸養、毀不勝哀、悲慟嘔血、聞者泣下，果何甄別？此諸生素所誦習而講求者。今欲舉一賢者則使不賢者勸，進一能者則使不能者戒，何道以致之歟？願詳對毋讓。

問：朱子著《小學》、《家禮》二書，以為脩身、齊家、治國、平天下之本，今天下所通習者。請舉其槩，從諸生論之。夫立教、明倫、敬身，《小學》一書之大綱也。〈立教〉篇載教非一端，而先於母教；至〈稽古〉始言父教，而亦後於母教，何歟？其亦有可考歟？〈明倫〉之目五，〈敬身〉之目四，可得而詳歟？然既立為大綱，而又〈稽古〉以證之矣，何又取〈嘉言〉以廣之，而〈善
translation_en:
… how are they the same or different? There was one who longed for his mother incessantly and died of grief, and another who bit out maggots and cut flesh from her thigh so that her mother-in-law was granted an imperial burial; how should they really be distinguished from those who, denied permission to return home to care for their parents, wasted away from unbearable sorrow, or who wept bitterly and vomited blood so that all who heard of it were moved to tears? These are things that you students have long recited, studied, and investigated. Now, if one wishes to promote a single worthy person so as to encourage the unworthy, and advance a single capable person so as to admonish the incapable, by what way can this be brought about? Please reply in detail and do not hold back.

Question: Master Zhu [Zhu Xi 朱熹] compiled the two books Elementary Learning (Xiaoxue 小學) and Family Rituals (Jiali 家禮) as the foundation for cultivating the self, regulating the family, governing the state, and bringing peace to the world, and today they are universally studied throughout the empire. Allow me to raise their general outlines and discuss them with you students. "Establishing Instruction" (Lijiao 立教), "Clarifying Human Relations" (Minglun 明倫), and "Revering the Self" (Jingshen 敬身) are the main principles of the Elementary Learning. The chapter "Establishing Instruction" records more than one kind of instruction, yet it begins with maternal instruction; only when we reach "Examining Antiquity" (Jigu 稽古) does it first speak of paternal instruction, and even there it places it after maternal instruction—why is this? Can this also be investigated and verified? The subheadings of "Clarifying Human Relations" are five, and the subheadings of "Revering the Self" are four; can you explain them in detail? Moreover, having already established these as the main principles and further "Examining Antiquity" to substantiate them, why did he also select "Fine Words" (Jiayan 嘉言) to broaden them and "Good …

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
行以實之歟所謂內篇外篇何所指
歟而又著為通論以介乎其間其故
何歟或者謂其所以申明立教明倫
敬身之畧而獨致意於曰寵祿曰威
儀何歟諸家之說有可舉其優劣歟
冠婚喪祭家禮一書之大綱也冠禮
載冠非一節而極於三加至笄禮不
用三加而又獨服背子何歟其亦有
===
可考歟婚禮之目七喪禮之目四十
有六祭禮之目三可得而詳歟然既
立為大綱而又酌古以準之矣何又
取雜儀以附之而袒禰以辨之歟所
謂古禮俗禮何所別歟而又摘為通
禮以列乎其前其故何歟或者謂其
表明家居日用之常而獨致意於曰
祠堂曰深衣何歟諸家之說有可言
punctuated: 行以實之歟？所謂「內篇」、「外篇」，何所指歟？而又著為《通論》以介乎其間，其故何歟？或者謂其所以申明立教、明倫、敬身之畧，而獨致意於曰寵祿、曰威儀，何歟？諸家之說，有可舉其優劣歟？冠、婚、喪、祭，《家禮》一書之大綱也。《冠禮》載冠非一節，而極於三加，至笄禮不用三加，而又獨服背子，何歟？其亦有可考歟？《婚禮》之目七，《喪禮》之目四十有六，《祭禮》之目三，可得而詳歟？然既立為大綱，而又酌古以準之矣，何又取雜儀以附之，而袒禰以辨之歟？所謂「古禮」、「俗禮」，何所別歟？而又摘為《通禮》以列乎其前，其故何歟？或者謂其表明家居日用之常，而獨致意於曰祠堂、曰深衣，何歟？諸家之說，有可言
translation_en:
… and "Good Deeds" (Shanxing) to substantiate them? What do the so-called "Inner Chapters" (Neipian) and "Outer Chapters" (Waipian) refer to? And why did he further compose the "General Discussion" (Tonglun) and place it between them? Some say that it serves to reiterate the general outline of "Establishing Teaching," "Clarifying Human Relationships," and "Revering the Self," yet why does it focus specifically on "favor and emolument" and "stateliness and decorum"? Among the explanations of various commentators, can their relative merits and flaws be cited?

Capping, marriage, funerals, and sacrifices are the overarching principles of the book Family Rituals (Jiali). The chapter "Capping Rituals" (Guanli) records that capping is not a single step, culminating in the "three cappings" (sanjia); yet when it comes to the hairpinning ceremony (jili) for women, it does not use the three cappings, and the initiate wears only a sleeveless jacket (beizi)—why is this? Can the reasons for this also be examined? There are seven subheadings under "Marriage Rituals" (Hunli), forty-six under "Funeral Rituals" (Sangli), and three under "Sacrificial Rituals" (Jili)—can these be explained in detail? Moreover, having already established these as the overarching principles and adapted antiquity to set their standards, why did he also select miscellaneous ceremonies to append to them, and distinguish between the distant ancestor (zu) and the father's shrine (ni) [? 袒禰 for 祖禰]? What is the distinction between the so-called "ancient rituals" and "popular rituals"? And why did he extract a section on "General Rituals" (Tongli) and place it at the beginning? Some say that it sets forth the regular norms of daily life at home, yet why does it focus specifically on the "ancestral hall" (citang) and the "deep garment" (shenyi)? Among the explanations of various commentators, can one speak of …

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
其得失歟諸生行將出以用世其明
以告我以觀脩身齊家之學
問窮經將以致用觀理所以應事天下
之事小可以喻大近可以該遠姑舉
二廣言之武衛防禦寇亂也往年蠻
夷弗靖或遇戰則潰以守則失矣今
雖邊塵已息然武事不可不脩何以
使將皆智勇兵皆精銳而戰無不克
===
守無不固歟有司牧養斯民也比年
軍旅屢興或斂財以供費勞民以餽
餉矣今雖閭閻不擾然治政不可不
飭何以使吏皆循廉民皆安乂而賦
惟正供力無重困歟流移之民雖曰
附籍然爭奪田產小則興詞訟大則
相攻殺團結嘯聚意外之虞可憂也
何以使永建乃家而各安生業歟頑
punctuated:
其得失歟？諸生行將出以用世，其明以告我，以觀脩身齊家之學。

問：窮經將以致用，觀理所以應事。天下之事，小可以喻大，近可以該遠。姑舉二廣言之：武衛，防禦寇亂也。往年蠻夷弗靖，或遇戰則潰，以守則失矣。今雖邊塵已息，然武事不可不脩。何以使將皆智勇、兵皆精銳，而戰無不克、守無不固歟？有司，牧養斯民也。比年軍旅屢興，或斂財以供費，勞民以餽餉矣。今雖閭閻不擾，然治政不可不飭。何以使吏皆循廉、民皆安乂，而賦惟正供、力無重困歟？流移之民，雖曰附籍，然爭奪田產，小則興詞訟，大則相攻殺，團結嘯聚，意外之虞可憂也。何以使永建乃家，而各安生業歟？頑…
translation_en:
…their merits and shortcomings? You students are soon to go forth to be of service to the world; explain this clearly to me, so that I may observe your learning in cultivating the person and regulating the family.

Question: Exhausting the meaning of the Classics is meant for practical application, and observing principle is the means to respond to affairs. Among the affairs of the world, the small can illustrate the great, and the near can encompass the distant. Let us tentatively take the Two Guang provinces [Guangdong and Guangxi] to speak of this: The military guards exist to defend against banditry and rebellion. In past years, when the native tribes were unrestful, sometimes when our forces met them in battle they were routed, and when holding fortifications they lost them. Now, although the dust on the frontiers has settled, military preparedness must not go uncultivated. How can we cause the commanders all to be wise and brave, and the soldiers all to be well-trained and sharp, so that in attack they never fail to conquer and in defense they never fail to hold fast? The local authorities exist to shepherd and nourish this people. In recent years, military campaigns have been repeatedly launched, at times exacting wealth to supply expenses and exhausting the people in transporting provisions. Now, although the villages are unmolested, civil governance must not go unrectified. How can we cause the officials all to be law-abiding and incorruptible, and the people all to be peaceful and well-governed, so that taxes consist solely of the regular quotas and corvée labor does not impose a heavy burden? As for the vagrant and displaced people, although they are said to have been entered into the household registers, they fight over fields and property—on a small scale instigating lawsuits, and on a large scale attacking and killing one another, banding together and gathering in mobs—so that unforeseen dangers are cause for worry. How can we cause them to permanently establish their homes and each be content in his livelihood? The recalcitrant…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
梗之徒雖曰向化然田耕而賦不入
於公廩丁壮而力不役於有司窺覘
侮慢率服之意未誠也何以使畏威
懷德而格其非心歟諸士子生長是
邦凡此數者觸目經心有年矣幸酌
古準今以陳久安長治之策
問君子之事
上也莫急於忠愛忠愛之發莫先於諫諍古
===
有諷諫有直諫其何所取義歟吁咈
致儆與矢詩遂歌者孰為諷而孰為
直告歸陳戒與稽首對揚者孰為直
而孰為諷天人之策治安之疏其詞
之所及者或為諷或為直均一忠愛
也何誼獨見斥大寶之箴金鑑之錄
其意之所主者或為直或為諷同一
忠愛也何蘊古獨見疑他如械繫不
punctuated:
梗之徒，雖曰向化，然田耕而賦不入於公廩，丁壮而力不役於有司，窺覘侮慢，率服之意未誠也。何以使畏威懷德，而格其非心歟？諸士子生長是邦，凡此數者，觸目經心有年矣，幸酌古準今，以陳久安長治之策。

問：君子之事上也，莫急於忠愛；忠愛之發，莫先於諫諍。古有諷諫，有直諫，其何所取義歟？吁咈致儆與矢詩遂歌者，孰為諷而孰為直？告歸陳戒與稽首對揚者，孰為直而孰為諷？天人之策、治安之疏，其詞之所及者，或為諷，或為直，均一忠愛也，何誼獨見斥？《大寶》之箴、《金鑑》之錄，其意之所主者，或為直，或為諷，同一忠愛也，何蘊古獨見疑？他如械繫不
translation_en:
…and recalcitrant elements, though said to have turned toward civilization, till their fields without paying taxes into the public granaries, and have able-bodied men who do not perform labor service for the authorities. Watching for opportunities and acting with insolence, their intention to submit is not yet sincere. How can they be made to fear authority and cherish virtue, thereby rectifying their errant hearts? You gentlemen were born and raised in this region; all of these matters have met your eyes and occupied your minds for years. Please weigh antiquity and measure the present to set forth a policy for lasting peace and enduring order.

Question: In a gentleman's service to his sovereign, nothing is more urgent than loyal affection; in the manifestation of loyal affection, nothing comes before remonstrance. In antiquity there was indirect remonstrance (fengjian) and direct remonstrance (zhijian); from what do these derive their meanings? Between uttering cries of "Alas!" and "Not so!" to convey warnings, and presenting poems and singing songs in response, which is indirect and which is direct? Between stating admonitions upon requesting leave to retire, and bowing one's head to the ground to extol the ruler's grace, which is direct and which is indirect? In the policy essays on Heaven and Man (by Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒) and the Memorial on Peace and Order (by Jia Yi 賈誼), what their words touched upon was in one case indirect and in the other direct; both were equally motivated by loyal affection, so why was Jia Yi alone rejected? In the Admonition on the Great Treasure (by Zhang蘊古 Zhang Yungu) and the Record of the Golden Mirror (by Zhang Jiuling 張九齡), what their intentions centered upon was in one case direct and in the other indirect; both shared the same loyal affection, so why was Zhang Yungu alone suspected? As for other cases—such as one who, undeterred by fetters,…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
恤而終受褒美投笏求退而上至斂
容與越職抗議事若慷慨刓墀死爭
節若高亢是其諫皆以直自許者也
其視伏閤奏事叩環呼聲挽衣苦諍
叩榻抗論寧為英州之行而必奪寵
臣之命寧為雪堂之游而力沮新法
之行果孰優而孰劣至如子虛之作
鋪張景物羽獵之賦偽言車騎通西
===
南有書得寶鼎有對是其諫皆以諷
自名者也其視侍從規諫不諍口舌
經筵開陳色溫氣和辨錫王勇智之
語論酣酒嗜音之句果孰是而孰非
方今
朝廷清明政事脩舉固無可言之事設臨
大政闗大計欲一言之不訐以為直
不媚以取容必欲
punctuated: 恤而終受褒美，投笏求退而上至斂容，與越職抗議、事若慷慨，刓墀死爭、節若高亢，是其諫皆以直自許者也。其視伏閤奏事、叩環呼聲、挽衣苦諍、叩榻抗論，寧為英州之行而必奪寵臣之命，寧為雪堂之游而力沮新法之行，果孰優而孰劣？至如《子虛》之作，鋪張景物；《羽獵》之賦，偽言車騎；通西南有書，得寶鼎有對，是其諫皆以諷自名者也。其視侍從規諫、不諍口舌，經筵開陳、色溫氣和，辨「錫王勇智」之語，論「酣酒嗜音」之句，果孰是而孰非？方今朝廷清明，政事脩舉，固無可言之事；設臨大政、闗大計，欲一言之，不訐以為直，不媚以取容，必欲
translation_en: …disregarding being put in fetters and yet ultimately receiving praise, or throwing down one's tablet to request retirement so that the sovereign even composed his countenance; along with overstepping one's office to protest—an act appearing impassioned—or breaking the palace balustrade in a fight to the death—a moral integrity appearing lofty: all of these are remonstrances that prided themselves on being forthright. Compared with prostrating oneself at the palace gates to present matters, knocking on the door-ring and crying out aloud, pulling at the emperor's robe in bitter contention, or striking the couch in defiant argument; or preferring banishment to Yingzhou if only to revoke the appointment of a favored minister, or preferring exile to Xuetang (Snow Hall) while striving to block the implementation of the New Policies—which of these are superior and which inferior? As for the composition of "Sir Fantasy" (Zixu), which elaborately describes scenery, or the rhapsody on the "Plume Hunt" (Yulie), which speaks allegorically of chariots and cavalry; the letter on opening communications with the Southwest, and the reply upon the discovery of the precious tripod: all of these are remonstrances that gained their name through indirect admonition. Compared with offering corrective advice while in attendance without verbal wrangling, or setting forth explanations at the Classics Colloquium with a gentle countenance and harmonious air—distinguishing the phrase "endowing the king with courage and wisdom" or discussing the line "addicted to wine and fond of music"—which of these are right and which wrong? At present, the imperial court is pure and enlightened, and governmental affairs are well-ordered and flourishing, so there is assuredly nothing that requires speaking out on. Yet suppose one is faced with a major policy or a matter of great consequence and wishes to speak a word on it: neither exposing faults in order to appear forthright, nor flattering in order to curry favor, if one necessarily desires that…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
朝廷信之而無疑天下聞之而致慕其道
安在此諸生之所當勉以待用者幸
相與講之
問孔子言禮云禮云玉帛云乎哉樂云
樂云鐘鼓云乎哉盖以其有本也今
姑就其文言之五玉三帛見于書矣
然經禮三百曲禮三千其多有如此
者何以獨言玉帛歟賁鼓維鏞見于
===
詩矣然八音克諧無相奪倫其義有
如此者何以獨言鐘鼓歟且古今禮
不相襲樂不相沿自伏羲時禮樂之
端已萌繼之者黃帝堯舜也其制作
之大有可舉者歟至成王時禮樂之
文已極前之者禹湯文武也其參酌
之妙有可詳者歟漢初用叔孫通朝
儀樂制大抵皆秦舊也河間獻王以
punctuated:
朝廷信之而無疑，天下聞之而致慕，其道安在？此諸生之所當勉以待用者，幸相與講之。

問：孔子言「禮云禮云，玉帛云乎哉？樂云樂云，鐘鼓云乎哉？」盖以其有本也。今姑就其文言之：五玉、三帛見于《書》矣，然經禮三百、曲禮三千，其多有如此者，何以獨言玉帛歟？「賁鼓維鏞」見于《詩》矣，然「八音克諧，無相奪倫」，其義有如此者，何以獨言鐘鼓歟？且古今禮不相襲，樂不相沿。自伏羲時，禮樂之端已萌，繼之者黃帝、堯、舜也，其制作之大有可舉者歟？至成王時，禮樂之文已極，前之者禹、湯、文、武也，其參酌之妙有可詳者歟？漢初用叔孫通朝儀，樂制大抵皆秦舊也。河間獻王以
translation_en:
… the imperial court trust it without doubt and the realm hear of it with admiration—where does the way to achieve this lie? This is what you students ought to strive after as you await employment; I hope that we may discuss it together.

Question: Confucius said, "Rites, they say, rites! Does it mean no more than jade and silk? Music, they say, music! Does it mean no more than bells and drums?" This is because they have a fundamental basis. For now, let us speak simply of their outward forms: the five jades and three silks appear in the Book of Documents (Shu), yet the cardinal rites number three hundred and the detailed ceremonies three thousand; when there are so many as this, why did he speak solely of jade and silk? "Large drums and great bells" appear in the Book of Odes (Shi), yet "the eight timbres can be harmonized without encroaching upon one another's order"; when their meaning is such as this, why did he speak solely of bells and drums? Moreover, across antiquity and the present, rites have not duplicated one another and music has not simply followed what came before. From the time of Fuxi, the beginnings of rites and music had already sprouted, and those who succeeded him were the Yellow Emperor (Huangdi), Yao, and Shun—can the greatness of their institutions be enumerated? By the time of King Cheng, the outward forms of rites and music had reached their peak, and those who preceded him were Yu, Tang, King Wen, and King Wu—can the subtlety of their adaptations and deliberations be recounted in detail? At the beginning of the Han, the court ceremonial of Shusun Tong was used, and the musical system mostly followed the old practices of the Qin. King Xian of Hejian (Hejian Xianwang) held that …

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
為治道非禮樂不成獻禮五百餘篇
復獻所集雅樂其有合於古歟博士
曹充請興禮樂有可考者歟唐用房
玄齡等貞觀禮雅樂大槩因隋舊也
李銳與諸學士刊定五禮其亦有合
於古歟起居舍人王仲丘又請脩明
堂祀禮有可言者歟宋以三禮圖閲
定為十五卷者誰歟改周樂章十二
===
順為十二安者其何所取義歟元起
朝儀稽古典而參以時宜者誰歟新
製大成雅樂其何所推本歟我
朝
太祖高皇帝命禮部取儀禮及采周官屬民
讀法之旨為鄉飲酒禮又謂尚書牛
諒定著禮儀宜與諸儒參詳考議甚
盛心也可言其節目歟且厭前代樂章用
punctuated: 為治道非禮樂不成，獻禮五百餘篇，復獻所集雅樂，其有合於古歟？博士曹充請興禮樂，有可考者歟？唐用房玄齡等《貞觀禮》，雅樂大槩因隋舊也。李銳與諸學士刊定五禮，其亦有合於古歟？起居舍人王仲丘又請脩明堂祀禮，有可言者歟？宋以《三禮圖》閲定為十五卷者誰歟？改周樂章十二順為十二安者，其何所取義歟？元起朝儀，稽古典而參以時宜者誰歟？新製大成雅樂，其何所推本歟？我朝太祖高皇帝命禮部取《儀禮》及采《周官》屬民讀法之旨為鄉飲酒禮，又謂尚書牛諒定著禮儀宜與諸儒參詳考議，甚盛心也，可言其節目歟？且厭前代樂章用…
translation_en: …held that the Way of governance cannot be accomplished without rites and music. He presented more than five hundred chapters on rites and further presented the court music (yayue) he had collected; did these accord with antiquity? Erudite (Boshi) Cao Chong 曹充 requested the revival of rites and music; is there anything in this that can be examined? The Tang employed the Zhenguan Rites (Zhenguan li) compiled by Fang Xuanling 房玄齡 and others, while its court music largely followed the old practices of the Sui. Li Rui 李銳 [?] and various Scholars (Xueshi) edited and fixed the Five Rites (Wuli); did these also accord with antiquity? Imperial Diarist (Qiju sheren) Wang Zhongqiu 王仲丘 further requested the revision of the sacrificial rites of the Hall of Light (Mingtang); is there anything that can be said of this? In the Song, who was it that reviewed and finalized the Illustrations to the Three Ritual Classics (Sanli tu) into fifteen scrolls (juan)? And in changing the twelve "Shun" (Harmony) musical pieces of the Later Zhou into the twelve "An" (Peace) pieces, what meaning was drawn upon? In the Yuan, who was it that established the court ceremonial by investigating ancient canons and adapting them to the needs of the time? And in newly instituting the court music of Great Completion (Dacheng yayue), what was taken as its fundamental basis? In our own dynasty, Emperor Taizu Gaohuangdi 太祖高皇帝 ordered the Ministry of Rites (Libu) to draw upon the Etiquette and Ceremonial (Yili) and adopt the purport of assembling the people to read the laws from the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan) to establish the District Symposium Rites (xiang yinjiu li). He also told Minister (Shangshu) Niu Liang 牛諒 that in fixing and codifying the ritual ceremonies, he ought to consult and deliberate carefully with the various Confucian scholars. This was a most magnificent intention; can you state its detailed articles? Moreover, disliking the musical pieces of former dynasties for their use of…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
諛鄙陋命尚書陶凱更製新詞又諭
禮部臣曰大成樂器以祀孔子此宜
究心甚
盛典也可舉其名義歟夫禮樂不可斯須
去身諸生尚原其本備其文以對毋
泛毋畧
punctuated: 諛鄙陋，命尚書陶凱更製新詞，又諭禮部臣曰：「大成樂器以祀孔子，此宜究心。」甚盛典也，可舉其名義歟？夫禮樂不可斯須去身，諸生尚原其本、備其文以對，毋泛毋畧。
translation_en: …flattering, vulgar, and crude, he commanded Minister Tao Kai 陶凱 to compose new lyrics; and he further instructed the officials of the Ministry of Rites, saying: "The musical instruments of Great Perfection (Dacheng) are used in sacrificing to Confucius; to this one ought to devote thorough attention." This was truly a grand institution! Can you cite their names and meanings? Now, rites and music may not be set aside from one's person even for a moment. May you students trace their origins and set forth their details in full in your replies; do not be vague or cursory.

text:
四書義
斯民也三代之所以直道而行也
劉實
