title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
至自會〔襄公十一年〕
陳政
同考試官訓導陳批此題塲中雖知春秋以變
文為褒貶之說然皆昧於分截貫串而以同盟
于戲有致伐故失之遠此篇辭旨俱優殆雞群
野鶴歟
同考試官教諭張批經旨明白而辭足以發之
本房之翹楚也敬羡敬羡
考試官教諭劉批得變文為褒貶之旨允宜
===
錄出以示後學
考試官教諭吴批晋悼服貳得失聖人書法
精妙此篇得之
屢盟而不信故貳國之歸心卒在於推誠屡伐而無
功故望國之策功卒在於致會此悼公服鄭之事春
秋於二同盟之後書會于蕭魚兩致伐之後書公至
自會其以變文為褒貶歟且鄭之従晉春秋著其或
叛或服以為伯事之盛衰久矣今也五會之後鄭復
従楚悼公於是伐鄭而有于戲之盟虎牢之後鄭又
punctuated:
至自會〔襄公十一年〕。
陳政
同考試官訓導陳批：此題塲中雖知《春秋》以變文為褒貶之說，然皆昧於分截貫串，而以「同盟于戲」有致伐，故失之遠。此篇辭旨俱優，殆雞群野鶴歟！
同考試官教諭張批：經旨明白，而辭足以發之，本房之翹楚也。敬羡，敬羡！
考試官教諭劉批：得變文為褒貶之旨，允宜錄出以示後學。
考試官教諭吴批：晋悼服貳得失，聖人書法精妙，此篇得之。
屢盟而不信，故貳國之歸心，卒在於推誠；屡伐而無功，故望國之策功，卒在於致會。此悼公服鄭之事，《春秋》於二「同盟」之後書「會于蕭魚」，兩「致伐」之後書「公至自會」，其以變文為褒貶歟！且鄭之従晉，《春秋》著其或叛或服，以為伯事之盛衰久矣。今也五會之後，鄭復従楚，悼公於是伐鄭，而有于戲之盟；虎牢之後，鄭又
translation_en:
… arrived from the meeting [Eleventh Year of Duke Xiang].

Chen Zheng

Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Chen: On this topic, although the candidates in the examination hall knew the theory that the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) uses changes in wording to express praise and blame, they were all confused about how to divide the sections and link them together coherently; and because "jointly covenanted at Xi" is followed by a report of returning from the campaign, they missed the mark by far. This essay excels in both diction and meaning—is it not like a wild crane among a flock of chickens!

Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Zhang: The meaning of the Classic is clear and the words suffice to bring it out; it is the finest of this ward. Full of admiration, full of admiration!

Comment by Examiner and Instructor Liu: It grasps the purport of changing the wording to express praise and blame; it is truly fitting to copy it out to show to later students.

Comment by Examiner and Instructor Wu: The successes and failures of Duke Dao of Jin in subduing a wavering state, and the subtle perfection of the Sage's historiographical method—this essay has grasped them.

When covenants are made repeatedly yet without good faith, a wavering state's submission of heart ultimately rests upon extending sincerity; when punitive campaigns are launched repeatedly yet without success, a prestigious state's recording of merit in the ancestral temple ultimately rests upon reporting arrival from a meeting. Regarding this affair of Duke Dao subduing Zheng, after two "joint covenants" the Spring and Autumn Annals records "met at Xiaoyu," and after two reports of "arrival from attacking," it records "the Duke arrived from the meeting"—is this not using changes in wording to express praise and blame? Moreover, as for Zheng's following Jin, the Spring and Autumn Annals has long set forth its alternating rebellion and submission as the measure of the rise and decline of the hegemonic enterprise. Now, after the five meetings, Zheng again followed Chu, whereupon Duke Dao attacked Zheng and there was the covenant at Xi; after Hulao, Zheng again…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
即楚悼公於是伐鄭而為亳城北之歃然盟戲鄭非
不聽命也未幾有中分之改慮盟亳北鄭非不行成
也無何有逆楚之異圖是屢書盟而不信也悼公乃
於三駕之終而講蕭魚之會舍其盟誓待以至誠鄭
無晉詐晉無鄭虞故春秋於于戲亳北屢書同盟者
所以譏其强人以信也至是而變文書會者非以鄭
感於推誠自是歸心中國之好乎若乃魯之従晉春
秋托其致會致伐以為伯事之得失舊矣今也初駕
伐鄭會于牛首我公既親帥師旅以在其列再駕伐
===
鄭盟于亳北我公復身親金革而預其行然初駕之
師諸侯非無會也而鄭即叛故班師之日止以伐鄭
致再駕之師諸侯非不盟也而鄭尋背故旋旆之時
亦以伐鄭書是屢書伐而無功也於是當我公於蕭
魚之後復有従晉之返告廟飲至舍爵策勲雖晉得
鄭我實有榮故春秋於初駕再駕致公以伐者所以
譏其恃力以逞也至是而變文致會者非以魯自是
亦得以息肩諸侯之事乎抑嘗觀晉景五書同盟而
終於强人以信而春秋譏之則悼公於二盟之後而
punctuated: 即楚，悼公於是伐鄭而為亳城北之歃。然盟戲，鄭非不聽命也，未幾有中分之改慮；盟亳北，鄭非不行成也，無何有逆楚之異圖。是屢書盟而不信也。悼公乃於三駕之終而講蕭魚之會，舍其盟誓，待以至誠，鄭無晉詐，晉無鄭虞。故《春秋》於于戲、亳北屢書同盟者，所以譏其强人以信也；至是而變文書「會」者，非以鄭感於推誠，自是歸心中國之好乎？若乃魯之従晉，《春秋》托其致會、致伐以為伯事之得失舊矣。今也，初駕伐鄭，會于牛首，我公既親帥師旅以在其列；再駕伐鄭，盟于亳北，我公復身親金革而預其行。然初駕之師，諸侯非無會也，而鄭即叛，故班師之日，止以伐鄭致；再駕之師，諸侯非不盟也，而鄭尋背，故旋旆之時，亦以伐鄭書。是屢書伐而無功也。於是當我公於蕭魚之後，復有従晉之返，告廟飲至，舍爵策勲，雖晉得鄭，我實有榮。故《春秋》於初駕、再駕致公以伐者，所以譏其恃力以逞也；至是而變文致「會」者，非以魯自是亦得以息肩諸侯之事乎？抑嘗觀晉景五書同盟而終於强人以信，而《春秋》譏之，則悼公於二盟之後而
translation_en: …turned to Chu, and thereupon Duke Dao attacked Zheng and held the blood-smearing covenant north of Bocheng. Yet in the covenant at Xi, it was not that Zheng did not obey orders, for before long there was the change of heart to divide the state's allegiance in half; and in the covenant north of Bo, it was not that Zheng did not make peace, for shortly afterward it harbored ulterior plans to welcome Chu. This is why covenants were repeatedly recorded without producing good faith. At the end of the three expeditions, Duke Dao therefore held the meeting at Xiaoyu, setting aside oaths and covenants and treating Zheng with utmost sincerity; Zheng no longer suspected Jin of deceit, and Jin no longer worried about Zheng. Thus, when the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) repeatedly records "joint covenants" at Xi and north of Bo, it is to criticize him for forcing others into good faith; when at this point it changes the wording to record a "meeting," is it not because Zheng was moved by his extension of sincerity and from then on turned its heart toward amity with the Central States? As for Lu's following Jin, the Spring and Autumn Annals had long used the reporting of our duke's return from a meeting or return from an attack as a vehicle to show the successes and failures of hegemonic endeavors. Now, in the first expedition to attack Zheng, when they met at Niushou, our duke personally led troops to take his place in the ranks; in the second expedition to attack Zheng, when they covenanted north of Bo, our duke again personally donned armor and weapons to take part in the campaign. Yet in the campaign of the first expedition, it was not that the feudal lords held no meeting, but Zheng immediately rebelled, and so on the day the army was withdrawn, the return was reported only as having "attacked Zheng"; in the campaign of the second expedition, it was not that the feudal lords made no covenant, but Zheng soon turned its back, and so when the banners were turned homeward, it was likewise recorded by reference to "attacking Zheng." This is why attacks were repeatedly recorded without achieving merit. Thereupon, when our duke returned from following Jin after Xiaoyu, announcing it to the ancestral temple, drinking to celebrate the return, setting down the goblets, and recording merits on bamboo slips, although it was Jin that won over Zheng, our state truly shared in the glory. Thus, when the Spring and Autumn Annals reports the duke's return from the first and second expeditions in terms of an "attack," it is to criticize relying on force to get one's way; when at this point it changes the wording to report his return from a "meeting," is it not because Lu from then on was also able to rest its shoulders from the affairs of the feudal lords? Moreover, if we observe how Duke Jing of Jin had five "joint covenants" recorded and ended by forcing others into good faith, for which the Spring and Autumn Annals criticized him, then after two covenants Duke Dao's…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
推誠者善可知矣晉厲三舉伐鄭致伐於兩伐致會
之後而春秋責之則悼於兩致伐之後而致會者美
可見焉惜乎鄭役既息委政大夫伯事不逮於初君
子為之扼腕
禮記義
毋失經紀以初為常
陳廣
同考試官教諭許批此題所謂經紀者天文
進退遲速之度數而初者曆家推步之舊法
===
以為占候之常者也場中紛紛異說殊為可厭
此作一破既隹通篇明潔當為本房之冠
考試官教諭劉批月令一題講理不綮遣詞
有文亦是作手
考試官教諭吳批禮記義如此者頗少物色
取以為一經之冠得之
先王之命太史既欲其司正乎天文必欲其循用乎
曆法盖用曆法為占候之常則天文之度數可無失
也先王以是而告太史欲其敬脩其職之意為何如
punctuated:
推誠者，善可知矣；晉厲三舉伐鄭，致伐於兩伐致會之後，而《春秋》責之，則悼於兩致伐之後而致會者，美可見焉。惜乎鄭役既息，委政大夫，伯事不逮於初，君子為之扼腕。

禮記義
毋失經紀，以初為常。
陳廣
同考試官教諭許批：此題所謂經紀者，天文進退遲速之度數，而初者，曆家推步之舊法，以為占候之常者也。場中紛紛異說，殊為可厭。此作一破既隹，通篇明潔，當為本房之冠。
考試官教諭劉批：《月令》一題，講理不綮，遣詞有文，亦是作手。
考試官教諭吳批：《禮記》義如此者頗少，物色取以為一經之冠，得之。

先王之命太史，既欲其司正乎天文，必欲其循用乎曆法。盖用曆法為占候之常，則天文之度數可無失也。先王以是而告太史，欲其敬脩其職之意為何如
translation_en:
… extended sincerity, its excellence can be known; and since Duke Li of Jin (Jin Li 晉厲) thrice launched campaigns to attack Zheng, recording the return from an attack after two attacks that had been recorded as returns from assemblies, for which the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu 春秋) censured him, then when Duke Dao (Dao 悼) recorded the return from an assembly after two returns recorded from attacks, its admirability can be seen. Alas! Once the campaigns against Zheng had ceased, he delegated governance to his Grand Masters, and his霸 (hegemonic) achievements did not measure up to his beginning—for which the gentleman wrings his hands in regret.

Exposition on the Record of Rites (Liji 禮記)
"Do not lose the regularities and cycles; take the original method as the constant rule."
By Chen Guang 陳廣

Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Xu 許: What this topic calls "regularities and cycles" (jingji 經紀) refers to the degrees and numbers of the advance, retreat, slowness, and swiftness of celestial phenomena, while "the original" (chu 初) refers to the established methods of calculation used by calendrical specialists, taken as the constant standard for astronomical observation. In the examination compound there was a tangle of divergent interpretations, which was truly tiresome. The opening analysis of this essay is already fine, and the entire piece is clear and lucid; it should rank first in this examination ward.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Liu 劉: On a topic from the "Monthly Ordinances" (Yueling 月令), expounding the principles does not lend itself to intricate junctures, yet the phrasing is literary—this too is the work of a skilled hand.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Wu 吳: Expositions on the Record of Rites such as this are quite rare. In seeking out talent, selecting it to head the list for this classic is well deserved.

When the former kings charged the Grand Scribe (Taishi 太史), since they wished him to preside over and rectify the celestial phenomena, they necessarily wished him to follow and employ the calendrical methods. For if one uses the calendrical methods as the constant standard for astronomical observation, then the degrees and numbers of the celestial phenomena will not be lost. When the former kings instructed the Grand Scribe with this, how profound was their intention that he reverently cultivate his duties…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
哉昔先王曆天象以授人時故於歲首而命太史若
曰日月之行天有進退遲速之度數如孟春會於營
室仲春會於奎宿之類是謂天之經紀所以明乎時
者也不可使有或失焉星辰之麗天亦有進退遲速
之度數如孟春參尾中於昏旦仲春弧建中於昏旦
之類是亦天之經紀所以明乎時者也不可使有或
忒焉然天文之經紀曆家推步之舊法備矣苟以此
求之則日月雖高其進退遲速可坐而致汝太史其
以此法為占候之常可也天象之經紀曆家推步之
===
故法詳矣苟用是求之則星辰雖遠其進退遲速可
坐而得汝太史其用是法為占候之常可也吁先王
命太史如此其敬天之意何其至哉大抵曆象日月
星辰以授人時自堯以来未之有改也舜齊七政周
用五紀其究一耳盖日月星辰之度數天以是而命
萬物而人奉之以為令者也故司之不可無其人占
之不可失其候月令記此於孟春之初豈以人君一
歲之首務莫大於此歟
樂所以脩内也禮所以脩外也禮樂交錯於中
punctuated:
哉！昔先王曆天象以授人時，故於歲首而命太史，若曰：日月之行天，有進退遲速之度數，如孟春會於營室、仲春會於奎宿之類，是謂天之經紀，所以明乎時者也，不可使有或失焉。星辰之麗天，亦有進退遲速之度數，如孟春參、尾中於昏旦，仲春弧、建中於昏旦之類，是亦天之經紀，所以明乎時者也，不可使有或忒焉。然天文之經紀，曆家推步之舊法備矣；苟以此求之，則日月雖高，其進退遲速可坐而致。汝太史其以此法為占候之常可也。天象之經紀，曆家推步之故法詳矣；苟用是求之，則星辰雖遠，其進退遲速可坐而得。汝太史其用是法為占候之常可也。吁！先王命太史如此，其敬天之意何其至哉！大抵曆象日月星辰以授人時，自堯以来未之有改也。舜齊七政，周用五紀，其究一耳。盖日月星辰之度數，天以是而命萬物，而人奉之以為令者也。故司之不可無其人，占之不可失其候。《月令》記此於孟春之初，豈以人君一歲之首務莫大於此歟？
樂所以脩内也，禮所以脩外也。禮樂交錯於中，
translation_en:
… ! In antiquity, the former kings calculated the celestial phenomena in order to grant the seasons to the people; therefore, at the beginning of the year, they commanded the Grand Astrologer (Taishi), as if to say: "As the sun and moon travel through the heavens, they have their degrees and numbers of advance and retreat, of slowness and speed—such as their conjunction in the Align-the-Hall (Yingshi) lodge in the first month of spring, and their conjunction in the Legs (Kui) lodge in the second month of spring. These are called the regularities of Heaven, by which the seasons are made clear; you must not allow any error in them. As the stars and celestial markers are arrayed in the heavens, they too have their degrees and numbers of advance and retreat, of slowness and speed—such as the Three Stars (Shen) and the Tail (Wei) lodges culminating at dusk and dawn in the first month of spring, and the Bow (Hu) and the Establishment (Jian) stars culminating at dusk and dawn in the second month of spring. These too are the regularities of Heaven, by which the seasons are made clear; you must not allow any discrepancy in them. Now, for the regularities of the celestial patterns, the old methods of calculation used by calendar-makers are already complete; if you seek them by these means, then lofty though the sun and moon may be, their advance and retreat, slowness and speed can be determined while sitting still. You, the Grand Astrologer, should take these methods as your constant rule for observation and divination. For the regularities of the celestial phenomena, the established methods of calculation used by calendar-makers are already detailed; if you seek them by these means, then distant though the stars and celestial markers may be, their advance and retreat, slowness and speed can be ascertained while sitting still. You, the Grand Astrologer, should use these methods as your constant rule for observation and divination." Ah! For the former kings to command the Grand Astrologer in this manner—how utmost was their reverence for Heaven! On the whole, calculating and observing the sun, moon, stars, and celestial markers in order to grant the seasons to the people has never changed since the time of Yao. Shun brought into harmony the Seven Directors, and the Zhou employed the Five Regulators; ultimately they are one and the same. For the degrees and numbers of the sun, moon, stars, and celestial markers are that by which Heaven gives its mandate to the myriad things, and that which human beings reverently receive as their ordinances. Therefore, in taking charge of them there must not be a lack of the proper officials, and in observing them there must be no missing of the proper signs. When the "Monthly Ordinances" (Yueling) records this at the beginning of the first month of spring, is it not because no primary duty of a ruler for the entire year is greater than this?

"Music is that by which the interior is cultivated; ritual is that by which the exterior is cultivated. When ritual and music intermingle within, …"

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
發形於外
甯詵
同考試官教諭許批此題本平易然禮樂交
錯發形於外處正欲觀學者筆力盖講貫不
明則措辭易昧此作其庶幾擺脫塵冗而碩
濯清飈者歟
考試官教諭劉批此篇講禮樂分合處不冗
不釋可謂佳作
考試官教諭吳批禮記義佳盖詞不奪理
===
當是朴學之士
先王教世子有禮樂分治之功致禮樂合成之美夫
禮樂所以治身心而身心一體也然有分治之功豈
無合成之美乎昔三王之於世子教之必以禮樂如
干戈羽籥弦誦之教樂也樂由中出所以脩乎內盖
消融其邪慝之蘊所謂不和不樂而鄙詐入之者無
有焉其脩內為何如若祭與養老合語之教禮也禮
自外作所以脩乎外盖陶成其恭肅之儀所謂不莊
不敬而慢易入之者無有焉其脩外為何如然禮之
punctuated:
發形於外。
甯詵
同考試官教諭許批：此題本平易，然禮樂交錯、發形於外處，正欲觀學者筆力。盖講貫不明，則措辭易昧。此作其庶幾擺脫塵冗而碩濯清飈者歟！
考試官教諭劉批：此篇講禮樂分合處，不冗不釋，可謂佳作。
考試官教諭吳批：禮記義佳，盖詞不奪理，當是朴學之士。
先王教世子，有禮樂分治之功，致禮樂合成之美。夫禮樂所以治身心，而身心一體也；然有分治之功，豈無合成之美乎？昔三王之於世子，教之必以禮樂。如干戈、羽籥、弦誦之教，樂也。樂由中出，所以脩乎內，盖消融其邪慝之蘊，所謂不和不樂而鄙詐入之者，無有焉，其脩內為何如？若祭與養老、合語之教，禮也。禮自外作，所以脩乎外，盖陶成其恭肅之儀，所謂不莊不敬而慢易入之者，無有焉，其脩外為何如？然禮之
translation_en:
… and manifests outwardly in form.”

Ning Shen 甯詵

Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Xu 許: This topic is inherently straightforward, yet the part concerning how ritual and music intermingle and manifest outwardly in form is precisely where one seeks to observe the scholar's literary vigor. Indeed, if one's comprehension is unclear, one's phrasing easily becomes obscure. Does this essay not come close to shaking off dusty verbosity and bathing grandly [?] in a pure breeze?

Comment by Examiner and Instructor Liu 劉: Where this piece expounds upon the separation and integration of ritual and music, it is neither verbose nor slack [?]; it may be called a fine composition.

Comment by Examiner and Instructor Wu 吳: This exposition on the Record of Rites (Liji) is fine. Because the rhetoric does not overwhelm the principle, the author must be a scholar of unadorned, solid learning.

In instructing the heir apparent, the former kings employed the efficacy of ritual and music governing separately to achieve the perfection of ritual and music blending together. Now, ritual and music are the means by which body and mind are governed, and body and mind are a single whole; since there is the efficacy of governing them separately, how could there not be the perfection of blending them together? In antiquity, when the Three Kings instructed the heir apparent, they invariably taught him through ritual and music. For instance, instruction in shields and axes, feather-wands and flutes, and stringed instruments and chanting pertained to music. Music arises from within and is the means to cultivate the interior. It melts away accumulated evil and depravity, so that what is described as “being neither harmonious nor joyful, whereby vulgarity and deceit enter into him” does not occur—how great is such cultivation of the interior! As for instruction in sacrifices, nourishing the aged, and conversing together, this pertained to ritual. Ritual is enacted from the outside and is the means to cultivate the exterior. It molds a reverent and solemn demeanor, so that what is described as “being neither dignified nor respectful, whereby negligence and carelessness enter into him” does not occur—how great is such cultivation of the exterior! Yet the [cultivation] of ritual …

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
脩達於內樂之脩達於外而嚴敬有以制其心和順
有以充其體則相合而不離相雜而無間所謂交錯
於中也夫既交錯於其中以至充積於其內則動與
禮樂俱行與禮樂會蔚然恭敬温文之可觀粹然中
正和樂之可羨又非發形於外乎故曰有禮樂分治
之功致禮樂合成之美以此吁世子德成而教尊良
有以夫抑考君之於世子親則父也尊則君也有父
之親有君之尊然後兼天下而有之是以養世子不
可不慎故三王之於世子既教以禮樂下文又教以
===
父子君臣長幼之道此三代所以繼體得人而享國
長久也不可不知
論
治天下以正風俗得賢才為本
梁儲
同考試官教諭張批〔論推正風俗得賢才為治天下之本得賢才又為正風俗之本脩身尤為得賢才之本而講貫無遺必一有識之士〕
考試官教諭劉批〔論不難於作而難於得體措〕
punctuated:
脩達於內，樂之脩達於外，而嚴敬有以制其心，和順有以充其體，則相合而不離，相雜而無間，所謂交錯於中也。夫既交錯於其中，以至充積於其內，則動與禮樂俱，行與禮樂會，蔚然恭敬温文之可觀，粹然中正和樂之可羨，又非發形於外乎？故曰：有禮樂分治之功，致禮樂合成之美，以此。吁！世子德成而教尊，良有以夫！抑考君之於世子，親則父也，尊則君也；有父之親，有君之尊，然後兼天下而有之，是以養世子不可不慎。故三王之於世子，既教以禮樂，下文又教以父子、君臣、長幼之道，此三代所以繼體得人而享國長久也，不可不知。

論
治天下以正風俗得賢才為本
梁儲
同考試官教諭張批：〔論推正風俗、得賢才為治天下之本，得賢才又為正風俗之本，脩身尤為得賢才之本，而講貫無遺，必一有識之士。〕
考試官教諭劉批：〔論不難於作，而難於得體。措〕
translation_en:
…cultivation of ritual reaches within, and the cultivation of music reaches without. When strict reverence regulates his mind and harmonious compliance fills his body, they unite without separating and intermingle without gap; this is what is meant by "intertwining within." Once they are intertwined within to the point of being fully accumulated inside, then his movements are together with ritual and music, and his conduct meets with ritual and music. Richly observable in his respectful, reverent, gentle, and refined demeanor, and purely admirable in his central, correct, harmonious, and joyful state—is this not "manifesting in form on the outside"? Therefore, it is said that having the efficacy of separate cultivation through ritual and music brings about the beauty of combined completion through ritual and music, for this very reason. Ah! That the Heir Apparent's virtue is perfected and education is revered truly has its cause in this! Moreover, if we examine the ruler's relation to the Heir Apparent: in affection, he is a father; in reverence, he is a ruler. Only when there is the affection of a father and the reverence of a ruler can one encompass and possess all under Heaven; therefore, the nurturing of the Heir Apparent cannot but be done with caution. Thus, in dealing with the Heir Apparent, the Three Kings not only taught him ritual and music, but, as the text below states, also taught him the way of father and son, ruler and minister, and elder and younger. This is why the Three Dynasties obtained the right men to succeed to the throne and enjoyed the realm for a long time; this must be known.

Discourse
"Governing All Under Heaven Takes Rectifying Customs and Obtaining Worthy Talents as Its Foundation"
Liang Chu 梁儲
Associate Examiner Instructor Zhang comments: (This discourse deduces that rectifying customs and obtaining worthy talents are the foundation of governing all under Heaven, that obtaining worthy talents is in turn the foundation of rectifying customs, and that cultivating the self is especially the foundation of obtaining worthy talents. It explains and threads these ideas together without omission; he must be a scholar of insight.)

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
比堆積則類乎𤗿策步驟窘束則同乎經義此作
其所謂沛然莫禦而皆安流者歟
考試官教諭吳批論旨遠淵永詞氣豐縟
蓋亦學之知本者也
威武可以服天下而萬邦協和黎民於變則在
乎風俗之正而不在乎威武智慮可以制天下
而羣黎百姓徧爲爾德則係乎賢才之用而不
係乎智慮故明道先生言于朝曰治天下以正
風俗得賢才爲本愚請言風俗之所以當正者
===
自朝廷而達于天下茫茫禹方烟火萬里而人
非一人也利害交乎其前一人鼓之而十人繼
之遂至於風靡草偃而莫可止三代比屋可封
之俗既遠於是乎僭亂于春秋縱橫于戰國逐
客于秦夫子沒而微言絕風教弊陋而俗益下
矣何可以不正乎自中國以至于海隅四極棼
棼雞犬相聞而家非一家也好惡出乎其間一
人倡之十人和之遂至於波流淪胥而莫可救
三代四海仰德之風既邈於是乎黃老于炎漢
punctuated:
比堆積則類乎𤗿策，步驟窘束則同乎經義。此作其所謂沛然莫禦而皆安流者歟？
考試官教諭吳批：論旨遠淵永，詞氣豐縟，蓋亦學之知本者也。
威武可以服天下，而萬邦協和、黎民於變，則在乎風俗之正，而不在乎威武；智慮可以制天下，而羣黎百姓徧爲爾德，則係乎賢才之用，而不係乎智慮。故明道先生言于朝曰：「治天下以正風俗、得賢才爲本。」愚請言風俗之所以當正者。自朝廷而達于天下，茫茫禹方，烟火萬里，而人非一人也。利害交乎其前，一人鼓之而十人繼之，遂至於風靡草偃而莫可止。三代比屋可封之俗既遠，於是乎僭亂于春秋，縱橫于戰國，逐客于秦。夫子沒而微言絕，風教弊陋而俗益下矣，何可以不正乎？自中國以至于海隅四極，棼棼雞犬相聞，而家非一家也。好惡出乎其間，一人倡之，十人和之，遂至於波流淪胥而莫可救。三代四海仰德之風既邈，於是乎黃老于炎漢，
translation_en:
…when comparisons are piled up, it resembles a policy essay; when its pacing is cramped and constrained, it is no different from an explication of the Classics. Is this composition not what may be called a torrent that nothing can stem, yet flowing everywhere in tranquil channels?

Comment by Examiner Wu, Instructor: The purport of the discourse is far-reaching, deep, and enduring, and its diction and vigor are rich and luxuriant. Truly, this is also someone whose learning grasps the fundamentals.

Military might can subjugate the empire, yet bringing harmony to the myriad states and transforming the black-haired people lies in the rectification of customs, not in military might.Resourceful calculation can control the empire, yet causing the masses and the hundred surnames universally to practice your virtue depends on the employment of worthy talents, not on resourceful calculation. Therefore Master Mingdao (Cheng Hao 程顥) spoke to the court, saying: "In governing the empire, rectifying customs and obtaining worthy talents are the root." Allow me humbly to speak of why customs ought to be rectified.

Reaching from the royal court out to the whole empire, across the vast realm laid out by Yu, with hearth-smoke stretching ten thousand li, the people are not just a single person. When profit and harm cross before them, if one person stirs them up, ten will follow, until they are swept along like grass bending before the wind and nothing can stop them. Once the customs of the Three Dynasties—when every household side by side was worthy of enfeoffment—had receded into the distance, there arose usurpation and disorder in the Spring and Autumn period, vertical and horizontal alliances in the Warring States, and the expulsion of guest-advisers under Qin. When the Master (Confucius) died and his subtle words ceased, moral teaching grew decayed and base, and customs sank ever lower. How could one fail to rectify them?

From the Central States out to the corners of the seas and the four extremities, where in bustling profusion the sounds of chickens and dogs are heard from one village to the next, the households are not just a single household. When likes and dislikes arise among them, if one person initiates a trend, ten will echo it, until they drift with the waves and sink together into ruin, and nothing can save them. Once the ethos of the Three Dynasties—when all within the four seas looked up to virtue—had grown remote, there arose the Huang-Lao doctrines under the fiery Han,…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
清談于典午佞佛于梁異端起而大義乖風聲
闊畧而俗益降矣又可以不正乎然上有好者
下有甚者風俗實係乎人之所為彼有所感此
有所應風俗必待其人而後正愚又請言賢才
之所以當得者伊尹耕于有莘以樂堯舜之道
三聘不至尹固不翻然以起也其誰以先知覺
後知以先覺覺後覺而使風俗之正乎傅說居
於傅巖以任版築之事旁求不及說固不奮然
以應也其誰以麴蘗而作酒以鹽梅而和羹而
===
使風俗之醇乎故治天下有本正風俗也得賢
才也正風俗之本又在得賢才而得賢才之本
尤在於脩身知此則知所以治天下矣且就人
之身而觀之心者身之主氣者身之用天君安
而元氣盛則百體從令而身無不和矣就國之
大而觀之賢才者國之元氣風俗者國之百體
賢才用而風俗正則萬事得理而國無不治矣
故以威武治天下者威武有時而弛其如正風
俗何以智慮制天下者智慮有時而窮其如得
punctuated: 清談于典午，佞佛于梁，異端起而大義乖，風聲闊畧而俗益降矣，又可以不正乎？然上有好者，下有甚者，風俗實係乎人之所為；彼有所感，此有所應，風俗必待其人而後正。愚又請言賢才之所以當得者。伊尹耕于有莘，以樂堯舜之道，三聘不至，尹固不翻然以起也，其誰以先知覺後知、以先覺覺後覺，而使風俗之正乎？傅說居於傅巖，以任版築之事，旁求不及，說固不奮然以應也，其誰以麴蘗而作酒、以鹽梅而和羹，而使風俗之醇乎？故治天下有本：正風俗也，得賢才也。正風俗之本，又在得賢才；而得賢才之本，尤在於脩身。知此則知所以治天下矣。且就人之身而觀之：心者，身之主；氣者，身之用。天君安而元氣盛，則百體從令而身無不和矣。就國之大而觀之：賢才者，國之元氣；風俗者，國之百體。賢才用而風俗正，則萬事得理而國無不治矣。故以威武治天下者，威武有時而弛，其如正風俗何？以智慮制天下者，智慮有時而窮，其如得…
translation_en:
…pure conversation (qingtan) in the Jin dynasty (Dianwu), and the fawning worship of Buddha in the Liang dynasty. Heterodoxies arose and the great principles were subverted; moral influence became negligent and customs deteriorated even further. How, moreover, could they not be rectified? Yet when superiors have a fondness for something, inferiors will carry it to even greater extremes, for customs truly depend upon human actions; where there is stimulus on one side, there is response on the other, and customs must await the right men before they can be rectified.

I beg also to speak of why worthy talents must be obtained. Yi Yin plowed in the fields of Youshen, delighting in the Way of Yao and Shun. Had thrice-repeated invitations not reached him, Yin certainly would not have changed his mind and risen up; who then would have used his prior knowledge to awaken those of later knowledge, and his prior awakening to awaken those of later awakening, thereby making customs upright? Fu Yue dwelt at Fuyan, laboring at rammed-earth construction. Had the wide search for worthies not reached him, Yue certainly would not have roused himself to respond; who then would have served as the yeast and malt to make wine, or as the salt and plum to season the broth, thereby making customs pure?

Therefore, governing the world has its root: rectifying customs and obtaining worthy talents. The root of rectifying customs lies in turn in obtaining worthy talents, and the root of obtaining worthy talents lies above all in cultivating the ruler's own person. To know this is to know how to govern the world. Moreover, if we observe it in terms of the human body: the mind is the master of the body, and vital energy (qi) is the function of the body. When the heavenly ruler (the mind) is at peace and primordial energy is flourishing, all the hundred parts of the body obey orders and the body is completely harmonious. If we observe it in terms of the greatness of the state: worthy talents are the primordial energy of the state, and customs are the hundred parts of the state. When worthy talents are employed and customs are rectified, the myriad affairs attain order and the state is completely well-governed. Therefore, for those who govern the world through martial might, martial might at times slackens—what then can they do about rectifying customs? For those who control the world through clever calculation, clever calculation at times is exhausted—what then can they do about obtaining…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
賢才何今之治天下而欲風俗之正也賢才之
得也則所以教人者當自灑掃應對以至於孝
弟忠信誘掖激勵使漸摩成就極於家詩書而
人禮樂而化成之有機所以擇士者當取明敏
識達以及於廉恥禮讓延訪敦遣使振作奮發
足以表當世而繼前聞而效用之有實為政在
人取人以身能自治其本則何患乎佞佛何畏
乎清談而何憂乎黄老何恤乎逐客何辨乎縱
横亦何有乎僭亂風俗既正賢才既用而天下
===
大治矣明道先生既言于朝復詳其制朱子慨
然以為知本有志者皆取以自勉而教化大行
賢才畢用人倫無不明物理無不察父父子子
同一本然之天夫夫婦婦均皆皥然之俗比屋
可封四海仰德愚何幸躬逢
今日之盛哉
表
擬宋以劉珙同知樞密院事謝表
劉實
punctuated:
賢才何？今之治天下，而欲風俗之正也，賢才之得也，則所以教人者，當自灑掃應對，以至於孝弟忠信，誘掖激勵，使漸摩成就，極於家詩書而人禮樂，而化成之有機；所以擇士者，當取明敏識達，以及於廉恥禮讓，延訪敦遣，使振作奮發，足以表當世而繼前聞，而效用之有實。為政在人，取人以身。能自治其本，則何患乎佞佛，何畏乎清談，而何憂乎黄老？何恤乎逐客，何辨乎縱横，亦何有乎僭亂？風俗既正，賢才既用，而天下大治矣。明道先生既言于朝，復詳其制，朱子慨然以為知本，有志者皆取以自勉。而教化大行，賢才畢用，人倫無不明，物理無不察，父父子子同一本然之天，夫夫婦婦均皆皥然之俗，比屋可封，四海仰德，愚何幸躬逢今日之盛哉！

表
擬宋以劉珙同知樞密院事謝表
劉實
translation_en:
… obtaining worthy talents? In governing All-under-Heaven today, if one desires that customs be rectified and worthy talents be obtained, then the means of instructing people ought to proceed from sprinkling and sweeping the floor and responding to elders, all the way to filial piety, fraternal submission, loyalty, and trustworthiness—guiding, supporting, encouraging, and rousing them, causing them to be gradually moulded and brought to completion, until it reaches the point where every family studies the Odes and Documents and every person practices rites and music, so that there is a vital mechanism for transformation and completion; and the means of selecting scholars ought to take those of bright acuity and penetrating insight, extending to those with a sense of shame and ritual deference—seeking them out and earnestly dispatching them to court, causing them to be stirred into vigorous action, sufficient to serve as models for the present age and carry on the renown of predecessors, so that there is substantial reality in their employment. "Governance lies in men; men are attracted by means of one's own person." If one is able to govern the root within oneself, then what worry would there be over flattering the Buddha, what fear over pure conversation (qingtan), and what anxiety over Huang-Lao? What concern would there be over expelling guest ministers, what need to dispute with vertical and horizontal alliance strategists, and what place would there be for usurpation and rebellion? Once customs are rectified and worthy talents are employed, All-under-Heaven is brought to great order. After Master Mingdao (Cheng Hao 程顥) spoke of this at court and further detailed its institutional arrangements, Master Zhu (Zhu Xi 朱熹) sighed with admiration, considering him to have understood the root, and those with high aspirations all took it up to exhort themselves. Now moral transformation prevails everywhere and worthy talents are all employed; human relationships are never unclarified, the principles of things are never unexamined; fathers act as fathers and sons as sons, sharing the same inherent Heaven-endowed nature; husbands act as husbands and wives as wives, all alike enjoying pure and luminous customs; every household side by side is worthy of enfeoffment, and all within the Four Seas look up to the imperial virtue—how fortunate is this foolish student to personally witness the flourishing splendor of the present day!

Memorial
Imitation of a Memorial of Thanks from the Song Dynasty by Liu Gong (劉珙) upon Being Appointed Co-Administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs (Tongzhi Shumiyuan shi)
Liu Shi (劉實)

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭張批表得體
考試官教諭劉批表合𠉀儷而有法敘事實
而無遺佳作也
考試官教諭吳批表佳
伏以
西府為崇嚴之地位亞台衡貳樞執邃密之機
職同屏翰宜求俊彥乃及寒微顧揣分而奚堪
實銜
恩而知愧恭惟
〇〇〇〇
默思夢賚
志感
推心遂令牛溲馬勃之餘亦荷虎節
龍章之
寵煌煌
天澤凛凛氷兢臣珙蚤掇賢科習聞
聖教眷一門之通顯慶千載之竒逢豸史叨聯

punctuated:
同考試官教諭張批：表得體。
考試官教諭劉批：表合𠉀儷而有法，敘事實而無遺，佳作也。
考試官教諭吳批：表佳。
伏以西府為崇嚴之地，位亞台衡；貳樞執邃密之機，職同屏翰。宜求俊彥，乃及寒微。顧揣分而奚堪，實銜恩而知愧。恭惟〇〇〇〇，默思夢賚，志感推心，遂令牛溲馬勃之餘，亦荷虎節龍章之寵。煌煌天澤，凛凛氷兢。臣珙蚤掇賢科，習聞聖教。眷一門之通顯，慶千載之竒逢。豸史叨聯，鑾坡獲選。詎意中州作鎮，分節制于三邊；累蒙
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner, Instructor Zhang: The memorial strikes the proper tone.
Comment by Examiner, Instructor Liu: The memorial conforms to parallel prose [?] and follows proper method; it narrates the historical facts without omission. It is a fine piece of work.
Comment by Examiner, Instructor Wu: The memorial is fine.
Your servant humbly considers that the Western Office [Bureau of Military Affairs] is an exalted and solemn place, second in rank only to the Three Ducal Ministers; the Associate Administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs holds the pivot of deep and confidential affairs, with duties comparable to those of a bulwark of the state. Eminent talents ought to be sought for it, yet the appointment has reached one of humble and lowly station. Looking at myself and measuring my lot, how could I be worthy of this? Truly holding Your grace in my mouth, I know only shame. Reverently I reflect upon Your Majesty [〇〇〇〇]: silently pondering as when high heaven granted a minister in a dream, and moved in spirit to repose heartfelt trust, You have consequently caused even leftover scraps like cow-urine and horse-dung puffballs to bear the favor of tiger tallies and dragon-emblazoned insignia. Brilliant is the heavenly bounty; trembling, I am as cautious as one treading on thin ice. Your servant Gong plucked success in the examination for the worthy at an early age and became conversant with the sagely teachings. Looking back upon the distinguished prominence of my whole family, I rejoice in the rare encounter of a thousand years. I unworthily joined the ranks of the Censorate, and was fortunate to be selected for the Hanlin Academy. How could I have expected to serve as a regional commander in the central provinces and share military command across the three frontiers, repeatedly receiving…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
行在召還寄長城于萬里卧棘薪而嘗膽與雲不
共戴天之讐效葵藿以傾誠用蹙就之如日之
敬敢自偷安于帷幄益惟補報于涓埃利涉大
川竊欲同乎舟楫安如磐石期有奠乎邦家伏
願
大一統而化成允復
皇圖之舊兼三才而立極式迎
帝命之新萬邦協和四海來假臣無任瞻
天仰
===
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
策
第一問
梁翬
同考試官教諭劉批策舉
二聖之制作而備及教化勸懲之實蓋真誦習講求之有素者與數
punctuated:
行在召還，寄長城于萬里。卧棘薪而嘗膽，與雲不共戴天之讐；效葵藿以傾誠，用蹙就之如日之敬。敢自偷安于帷幄，益惟補報于涓埃。利涉大川，竊欲同乎舟楫；安如磐石，期有奠乎邦家。伏願大一統而化成，允復皇圖之舊；兼三才而立極，式迎帝命之新。萬邦協和，四海來假。臣無任瞻天仰聖，激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。

策

第一問

梁翬

同考試官教諭劉批：策舉二聖之制作，而備及教化勸懲之實，蓋真誦習講求之有素者，與數
translation_en:
…recalled from the temporary imperial residence, I was entrusted with the bulwark across ten thousand li. Sleeping on thorny brushwood and tasting gall, I vow that I cannot live under the same sky as the enemy; emulating the sunflower and bean leaf in inclining my sincerity, I humbly draw near with reverence as toward the sun. How dare I seek comfort for myself within the command tent? All the more do I think only of making repayment, even by a drop of water or a grain of dust. To cross the great river advantageously, I privately wish to serve together like boat and oars; to secure peace as firm as agreat rock, I hope to help stabilize the state and ruling house. I humbly pray that Your Majesty will achieve the great unification and bring moral transformation to completion, truly restoring the former glory of the imperial domain; and encompass the Three Powers to establish the supreme standard, thereby welcoming the renewal of the imperial mandate. May the myriad states be in harmony, and all within the four seas come in allegiance. Your servant is overcome to the utmost with awe and earnest trepidation as I gaze up at Heaven and look up to the Sage; I reverently present this memorial of gratitude for Your Majesty's hearing.

Policy Essays (Ce)

First Question

Liang Hui 梁翬

Associate Examiner and Instructor (Jiaoyu) Liu comments: This policy essay cites the institutions created by the Two Sages, and thoroughly addresses the realities of moral transformation, encouragement, and punishment.
