title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
術問自有望庭矣
考試官教諭劉批策塲得此如太阿出匣而
光怪流動明珠投地而精采爛發心目不覺為之
開明可以自慶於得人矣
考試官教諭吳批敦勸懲別淑慝正欲得
賢才也此策歷舉忠孝之畧循良之實無一有
遺其有志於尚友古人者乎
日星麗天而
聖皇之制作以顯風雲應會而
===
===
聖皇之教化以行盖不有制作固無以為教化之具
不有教化又何以別淑慝而示勸懲哉此書周
官之篇所以言董正治官而詩時邁之詞所以
有式序在位百官既正而庶民從之以正故舜
之有天下選於眾而得皐陶湯之有天下舉於
眾而得伊尹其不仁者皆化而為仁也我
朝
太祖高皇帝受
天明命統理萬邦掃胡元之弊俗復中國之常典既
punctuated:
術問，自有望庭矣。
考試官教諭劉批：策塲得此，如太阿出匣而光怪流動，明珠投地而精采爛發，心目不覺為之開明，可以自慶於得人矣。
考試官教諭吳批：敦勸懲、別淑慝，正欲得賢才也。此策歷舉忠孝之畧、循良之實，無一有遺，其有志於尚友古人者乎！
日星麗天，而聖皇之制作以顯；風雲應會，而聖皇之教化以行。盖不有制作，固無以為教化之具；不有教化，又何以別淑慝而示勸懲哉？此《書》〈周官〉之篇所以言董正治官，而《詩》〈時邁〉之詞所以有式序在位。百官既正，而庶民從之以正。故舜之有天下，選於眾而得皐陶；湯之有天下，舉於眾而得伊尹。其不仁者，皆化而為仁也。我朝太祖高皇帝受天明命，統理萬邦，掃胡元之弊俗，復中國之常典，既
translation_en:
… [?] inquiry, one may naturally look forward to his appearance at the imperial court [?].

Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: Obtaining this in the policy essay session is like the Tai'e sword emerging from its scabbard with wondrous radiance flowing, or a bright pearl cast upon the ground with brilliant luster bursting forth. One's mind and eyes are involuntarily enlightened by it, and we may congratulate ourselves on having found a man of talent.

Examiner Wu, Instructor, comments: Emphasizing encouragement and warning and distinguishing the virtuous from the wicked are precisely aimed at obtaining worthy talent. This policy essay enumerates in turn the essentials of loyalty and filial piety and the realities of upright and capable governance without omitting a single point. Surely he is one who aspires to befriend the ancients!

The sun and stars adorn the heavens, and thereby the institutions created by the Sacred Emperors are made manifest; winds and clouds respond in harmony, and thereby the moral transformation of the Sacred Emperors is put into practice. Indeed, without institutional creations, there would certainly be no instruments for moral transformation; and without moral transformation, how could one distinguish the virtuous from the wicked and display encouragement and warning? This is why the "Officers of Zhou" (Zhouguan) chapter of the Book of Documents speaks of supervising and rectifying the governing officials, and why the lyrics of "Timely Progress" (Shimai) in the Book of Odes contain the line about ordering the officials in their positions according to their merits. Once the hundred officials are rectified, the common people follow them in rectitude. Therefore, when Shun possessed the empire, he selected from among the multitude and obtained Gao Yao; when Tang possessed the empire, he raised up from among the multitude and obtained Yi Yin; and those who were inhumane were all transformed and became humane. In our dynasty, Emperor Taizu Gao received the bright mandate of Heaven to rule and govern the myriad states, sweeping away the corrupt customs of the barbarian Yuan and restoring the constant canons of the Central Kingdom. Having already…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
已高出百代而遠超舜湯矣當時侍從之臣莫
非臯陶伊尹下至庶民亦皆化於為善不見有
邪慝者而猶勤
聖慮作大誥三編
太宗文皇帝嗣大歷服復作為善陰隲孝順事實二
書
宣宗章皇帝用保乂民又作五倫一書固與周官時
邁所云同歸一揆欲求如舜湯之於臯陶伊尹
而詳舉其人則事存史冊考有未暇請以
===
三聖制作所及而條陳之以見我
朝敎化有成而勸懲淑慝之明備焉執事所問剛
斷嫉惡不容奸僞者都御史詹徽也交不變色
德優於才者掌部事唐鐸也
大誥嘉之視
為善陰隲大理卿張文瓘之斷獄四百人無怨言
博陽侯丙吉之深厚不伐絕口舊恩者同一忠
也何可辨其優劣夙夜在公恪遵古道者左通
政茹瑺也超出羣職進膺嘉勞者知縣朱□□
punctuated:
已高出百代而遠超舜、湯矣。當時侍從之臣，莫非臯陶、伊尹，下至庶民，亦皆化於為善，不見有邪慝者，而猶勤聖慮，作《大誥》三編。太宗文皇帝嗣大歷服，復作《為善陰隲》、《孝順事實》二書。宣宗章皇帝用保乂民，又作《五倫》一書。固與〈周官〉、〈時邁〉所云同歸一揆。欲求如舜、湯之於臯陶、伊尹而詳舉其人，則事存史冊，考有未暇；請以三聖制作所及而條陳之，以見我朝敎化有成，而勸懲淑慝之明備焉。

執事所問，剛斷嫉惡、不容奸僞者，都御史詹徽也；交不變色、德優於才者，掌部事唐鐸也。《大誥》嘉之，視《為善陰隲》大理卿張文瓘之斷獄四百人無怨言、博陽侯丙吉之深厚不伐、絕口舊恩者，同一忠也，何可辨其優劣？夙夜在公、恪遵古道者，左通政茹瑺也；超出羣職、進膺嘉勞者，知縣朱□□…
translation_en:
…had already risen high above a hundred generations and far surpassed Shun and Tang. At that time, the officials in attendance were all the likes of Gao Yao and Yi Yin, and down to the common people, all were transformed toward doing good, with none who were evil or wicked to be seen. Yet He still exerted His sacred thoughts and composed the three parts of the Grand Pronouncements (Dagao). Emperor Wen, the Grand Ancestor [the Yongle Emperor], inherited the great succession and in turn composed the two books, Secret Rewards for Doing Good (Weishan yinzhi) and True Accounts of Filial Piety (Xiaoshun shishi). Emperor Zhang, the Propagating Ancestor [the Xuande Emperor], in order to protect and govern the people, further composed the book The Five Human Relationships (Wulun). Indeed, these share the exact same principle as what is said in the "Officers of Zhou" (Zhouguan) and "Timely Progress" (Shimai). If one wished to seek out those like Gao Yao and Yi Yin under Shun and Tang and enumerate those individuals in detail, their deeds are preserved in the historical records and there is not the leisure to examine them all here; I beg leave to set forth point by point those mentioned in the works composed by the Three Sages, so as to show that our dynasty's moral transformation has achieved success and that the encouragement of the good and punishment of the wicked are clear and complete.

As for what Your Excellency asks about: the one who was firm and decisive, hated evil, and tolerated no treachery or falsehood was Censor-in-Chief Zhan Hui 詹徽; the one whose countenance did not change in his associations and whose virtue surpassed his talent was Tang Duo 唐鐸, who administered the affairs of a Ministry. The Grand Pronouncements praised them. Compared with Chamberlain for Law Enforcement Zhang Wenguan 張文瓘 in Secret Rewards for Doing Good, who decided four hundred criminal cases without a single word of complaint, and Bing Ji 丙吉, Marquis of Boyang, who was deep and generous without boasting and never spoke of his past kindnesses, they are of the exact same loyalty—how could one distinguish superiority or inferiority between them? The one who was devoted to public duty from dawn to night and reverently followed the ancient way was Left Transmission Commissioner Ru Chang 茹瑺; the one who stood out above the multitude of officials and was promoted and received laudatory rewards for his toil was the District Magistrate Zhu □□ 朱□□ [?]…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
也
大誥美之與
為善陰隲開封府功曹陳泊之為政公忠注當貴
顯密令卓茂之教化大行中年令魯恭之政有
三異者同一賢也何可議其得失他若大將軍
徐達之克元都禁戢士卒無敢侵暴人民安業
市肆不移知府費震之在漢中發廩賑飢民多
來歸立為保伍賴以存活此又我
朝將帥守令之卓卓者也
===
五倫書載之與曹彬之伐蜀申令戢下所至悅服
富弼之徙青救灾有法從者如歸見采於
為善陰隲者不同一心乎御史中丞章溢之念母
不置遂以成疾母殁居喪悲戚而卒韓太初妻
劉氏之姑疾體腐齧蛆號呼事達于
朝姑獲賜葬此亦我
朝孝子節婦之表表者也
五倫書載之與張九齡之求養累詔不許毀不勝
哀徐積之廬墓悲慟嘔血聞者泣下見采於
punctuated: 也。《大誥》美之，與《為善陰隲》開封府功曹陳泊之為政公忠、注當貴顯，密令卓茂之教化大行，中年令魯恭之政有三異者，同一賢也，何可議其得失？他若大將軍徐達之克元都，禁戢士卒，無敢侵暴，人民安業，市肆不移；知府費震之在漢中，發廩賑飢，民多來歸，立為保伍，賴以存活。此又我朝將帥守令之卓卓者也。《五倫書》載之，與曹彬之伐蜀，申令戢下，所至悅服；富弼之徙青，救灾有法，從者如歸，見采於《為善陰隲》者，不同一心乎？御史中丞章溢之念母不置，遂以成疾，母殁居喪，悲戚而卒；韓太初妻劉氏之姑疾體腐，齧蛆號呼，事達于朝，姑獲賜葬。此亦我朝孝子節婦之表表者也。《五倫書》載之，與張九齡之求養，累詔不許，毀不勝哀；徐積之廬墓，悲慟嘔血，聞者泣下，見采於
translation_en:
…. The Grand Pronouncements (Dagao 大誥) praises them. Compared with the examples in the Secret Merits of Doing Good (Weishan yinzhi 為善陰隲)—Chen Bo 陳泊, Personnel Evaluation Officer of Kaifeng Prefecture 開封府, who governed with fairness and loyalty and was destined in the register of fate for noble rank and eminence; Zhuo Mao 卓茂, Magistrate of Mi 密, whose moral transformation prevailed widely; and Lu Gong 魯恭, Magistrate of Zhongmu 中牟 [written 中年 in text], whose governance produced the three marvels—they are of the same worthiness; how could one debate their respective merits and failings?

As for others, such as Grand General Xu Da 徐達, who conquered the Yuan capital and strictly restrained his soldiers so that none dared to plunder or commit violence, allowing the people to remain peacefully in their occupations and the market shops to go unchanged; and Prefect Fei Zhen 費震 in Hanzhong 漢中, who opened the granaries to relieve the starving, so that many people came to give their allegiance, and organized them into mutual-security groups (baowu 保伍), whereby they were able to survive—these, again, are among the most outstanding generals, commanders, prefects, and magistrates of our Dynasty. The Book of the Five Relationships (Wulun shu 五倫書) records them. Compared with Cao Bin 曹彬, who in his campaign against Shu 蜀 issued strict orders to restrain his subordinates so that wherever he went the people gladly submitted, and Fu Bi 富弼, who when transferred to Qingzhou 青州 had effective methods for disaster relief so that refugees flocked to him as if returning home—both selected for inclusion in the Secret Merits of Doing Good—do they not share the very same mind?

Vice Censor-in-Chief Zhang Yi 章溢 longed for his mother without ceasing until he fell ill from it, and when his mother died and he was observing the mourning period, he died of grief; and Madam Liu 劉氏, wife of Han Taichu 韓太初, whose mother-in-law fell ill with rotting flesh, bit the maggots to kill them and wailed aloud—when the matter reached the Court, her mother-in-law was granted an imperial burial. These, too, are among the most illustrious filial sons and chaste wives of our Dynasty. The Book of the Five Relationships records them. Compared with Zhang Jiuling 張九齡, who requested leave to care for his parents, was repeatedly refused by imperial edict, and became emaciated beyond endurance from grief; and Xu Ji 徐積, who lived in a hut by his parent's grave and mourned so bitterly that he vomited blood, moving all who heard him to tears—both selected for inclusion in…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
孝順事實者不同一誡乎夫勸懲既至則邪慝者
皆化而為善猶舜湯選舉有法則不仁者皆化
而為仁於是進一賢者於衆人之中何患不賢
者之不勸拔一能者於庶民之列何患不能者
之不戒今
聖人在上監于
成憲而
列聖之制作日益敷布勤于治理而
列聖之教化日益申明敦勸懲別淑慝而野無遺賢
===
朝無幸位所以保萬萬年之
鴻業者實係於此矣愚也誦習講求生逢其盛敢
不以善自勖以惡自戒惟執事其進教之
第二問
梁儲
同考試官教諭張批小學家禮人所通習條具
意義宜無不知場中乃多泛泛直寫問目何哉
忽得此卷兼二書而條陳至終篇而益暢真異
乎人也
punctuated:
《孝順事實》者，不同一誠乎？夫勸懲既至，則邪慝者皆化而為善，猶舜、湯選舉有法，則不仁者皆化而為仁。於是進一賢者於衆人之中，何患不賢者之不勸？拔一能者於庶民之列，何患不能者之不戒？今聖人在上，監于成憲，而列聖之制作日益敷布；勤于治理，而列聖之教化日益申明。敦勸懲，別淑慝，而野無遺賢，朝無幸位，所以保萬萬年之鴻業者，實係於此矣。愚也誦習講求，生逢其盛，敢不以善自勖，以惡自戒？惟執事其進教之。

第二問
梁儲
同考試官教諭張批：《小學》、《家禮》，人所通習，條具意義，宜無不知。場中乃多泛泛，直寫問目，何哉？忽得此卷，兼二書而條陳，至終篇而益暢，真異乎人也。
translation_en:
… the True Records of Filial Piety (Xiaoshun shishi)—do they not share the very same sincerity [rendered as 誡, "admonition," in the woodblock]? Now, once encouragement and punishment are carried to the utmost, those who are wicked and perverse will all be transformed toward goodness, just as when Shun and Tang had proper methods for selection and recommendation, the inhumane were all transformed into being humane. Thus, when one worthy person is promoted from among the multitude, why worry that the unworthy will not be encouraged? When one capable person is selected from the ranks of the common people, why worry that the incapable will not take warning? Today, the Sage is on the throne. Taking the established statutes as his mirror, the institutions created by the successive imperial ancestors are ever more widely promulgated; diligent in governance and administration, the transformative teachings of the successive imperial ancestors are ever more clearly set forth. Emphasizing encouragement and punishment and distinguishing the virtuous from the wicked, so that no worthy is left overlooked in the countryside and no official holds a post by mere luck at court—that by which the great enterprise is preserved for tens of thousands of years truly depends upon this. Simpleminded though I am, I have recited, practiced, and inquired into these matters, and having had the fortune to be born in this flourishing age, how could I dare not exhort myself with goodness and warn myself against evil? May Your Excellency offer further instruction.

Question 2
Liang Chu 梁儲
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Zhang: The Elementary Learning (Xiaoxue) and the Family Rituals (Jiali) are works with which everyone is thoroughly familiar; as for setting forth their meanings item by item, there ought to be no one who does not know them. Why is it, then, that in the examination hall so many candidates responded with vague generalities or simply copied out the words of the question? Suddenly coming upon this paper, which sets out both books point by point and grows ever more fluent and thorough right to the end of the essay—he is truly different from the rest!

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭劉批條對無遺而辨析有理
昌黎低頭拜東野歐陽極口道聖俞正不能不
爾也
考試官教諭吴批答小學家禮惟此甚悉其
嘗究心者歟
著垂法立教之典莫先於脩身齊家推脩身齊
家之道斯可以治國平天下此朱子小學家禮
二書所以大有功於世也即小學言之其大綱
不過立教明倫敬身三者而立教篇所載首言
===
胎教次言保傅之教次言學校君政之教又次
言師弟子之教盖人始生則母主之既就外傅
則父主之雖不言父教而亦在其中矣至稽古
言父教乃孔子之所以教其子學詩學禮之事
為萬世立教之大法于此究極諸教之指歸故
不得不有先後之序也明倫自父子之親君臣
之義夫婦之別長幼之序至朋友之交其目有
五敬身自心術之要威儀之則衣服之制至飲
食之節其目有四然既立其大綱又舉古之聖
punctuated:
考試官教諭劉批：條對無遺，而辨析有理。「昌黎低頭拜東野，歐陽極口道聖俞」，正不能不爾也。
考試官教諭吴批：答《小學》、《家禮》惟此甚悉，其嘗究心者歟！
著垂法立教之典，莫先於脩身齊家；推脩身齊家之道，斯可以治國平天下。此朱子《小學》、《家禮》二書，所以大有功於世也。即《小學》言之，其大綱不過「立教」、「明倫」、「敬身」三者。而〈立教篇〉所載，首言胎教，次言保傅之教，次言學校君政之教，又次言師弟子之教。盖人始生則母主之，既就外傅則父主之，雖不言父教，而亦在其中矣。至〈稽古〉言父教，乃孔子之所以教其子學《詩》、學《禮》之事，為萬世立教之大法，于此究極諸教之指歸，故不得不有先後之序也。「明倫」自父子之親、君臣之義、夫婦之別、長幼之序，至朋友之交，其目有五。「敬身」自心術之要、威儀之則、衣服之制，至飲食之節，其目有四。然既立其大綱，又舉古之聖
translation_en:
Examiner and Instructor Liu’s comment: He replies to the items without omission, and his analysis is sound. As the saying goes, "Han Yu of Changli bowed his head to pay homage to Meng Jiao (Dongye), and Ouyang Xiu praised Mei堯臣 (Shengyu) to the skies"—one truly cannot help doing just that here!

Examiner and Instructor Wu’s comment: Among the answers on the Elementary Learning (Xiaoxue) and the Family Rituals (Jiali), only this one is thoroughly detailed. Surely he is someone who has devoted deep attention to them!

In composing canons that hand down laws and establish instruction, nothing comes before cultivating the person and regulating the family; by extending the Way of cultivating the person and regulating the family, one can then govern the state and bring peace to the world. This is why Master Zhu’s two books, the Elementary Learning (Xiaoxue) and the Family Rituals (Jiali), have rendered such great service to the world. Speaking of the Elementary Learning, its main outlines consist of no more than three parts: "Establishing Instruction" (Lijiao), "Clarifying Human Relationships" (Minglun), and "Revering the Person" (Jingshen). What is recorded in the chapter "Establishing Instruction" first speaks of fetal instruction, next speaks of the instruction of nurses and tutors, next speaks of the instruction of schools and royal governance, and next again speaks of the instruction of teachers and disciples. For when a person is first born, the mother presides over it; once he goes to an outside tutor, the father presides over it—so although paternal instruction is not explicitly mentioned, it is nonetheless contained therein. When it comes to "Investigating Antiquity" (Jigu), which speaks of paternal instruction, it records the matter of how Confucius taught his son to study the Odes (Shi) and study the Rites (Li), serving as the great model for establishing instruction for ten thousand generations and bringing to ultimate completion the essential import of all forms of instruction; therefore, there could not but be this sequence of first and last. "Clarifying Human Relationships," from the affection between father and son, the righteousness between ruler and minister, the distinction between husband and wife, and the precedence between old and young, down to the intercourse between friends, has five sub-categories. "Revering the Person," from the essentials of mental disposition, the rules of dignified demeanor, and the regulations of clothing, down to the moderation of food and drink, has four sub-categories. Yet having set up its main outlines, he also cited the deeds of the ancient sages and…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
賢立教明倫敬身之事以證之矣苟不取嘉言
以廣之則漢唐宋諸賢言及於立教明倫敬身
者無以知不取善行以實之則漢唐宋諸賢行
合於立教明倫敬身者無以見此内篇紀三代
之事迹以為小學之本源外篇具漢唐宋之言
行以為小學之支流也然又為通論一篇寓乎
其間莫非申明立教明倫敬身之畧而致意於
曰寵禄曰威儀者夫寵禄過則驕怠由以生左
傳所載公子州吁之事姑置勿論而威儀者敬
===
身之大節而立教明倫之所由以成者也諸家
釋小學者饒氏許氏而熊氏著為句解何氏纂
為集成黃氏輯為通義然皆不及括蒼于氏之
解為明備其於威儀惟西山真氏言人之動作
禮義威儀非可以强為也皆有自然之則能者
養之以福亦在敬而已矣今具載海虞吳氏之
集解此其說之最優者歟即家禮言之其大綱
不過冠昏喪祭四者而冠禮篇所載首言戒賓
次言宿賓次言迎賓又次言賓揖將冠者就席
punctuated:
賢立教、明倫、敬身之事以證之矣。苟不取嘉言以廣之，則漢、唐、宋諸賢言及於立教、明倫、敬身者無以知；不取善行以實之，則漢、唐、宋諸賢行合於立教、明倫、敬身者無以見。此内篇紀三代之事迹，以為《小學》之本源；外篇具漢、唐、宋之言行，以為《小學》之支流也。然又為通論一篇寓乎其間，莫非申明立教、明倫、敬身之畧，而致意於曰寵禄、曰威儀者。夫寵禄過，則驕怠由以生，《左傳》所載公子州吁之事，姑置勿論；而威儀者，敬身之大節，而立教、明倫之所由以成者也。諸家釋《小學》者，饒氏、許氏，而熊氏著為《句解》，何氏纂為《集成》，黃氏輯為《通義》，然皆不及括蒼于氏之解為明備。其於威儀，惟西山真氏言：「人之動作禮義威儀，非可以强為也，皆有自然之則，能者養之以福，亦在敬而已矣。」今具載海虞吳氏之《集解》，此其說之最優者歟！
即《家禮》言之，其大綱不過冠、昏、喪、祭四者。而《冠禮》篇所載，首言戒賓，次言宿賓，次言迎賓，又次言賓揖將冠者就席，
translation_en:
…and worthies in establishing instruction, clarifying human relationships, and revering the self to substantiate them. If one did not select "Admirable Words" (Jiayan) to broaden them, there would be no way to know the sayings of the various worthies of the Han, Tang, and Song dynasties that touch upon establishing instruction, clarifying human relationships, and revering the self; and if one did not select "Good Deeds" (Shanxing) to substantiate them, there would be no way to see the actions of the various worthies of the Han, Tang, and Song dynasties that accord with establishing instruction, clarifying human relationships, and revering the self. Thus, the "Inner Chapters" (Neipian) record the deeds of the Three Dynasties as the fountainhead of Elementary Learning (Xiaoxue), while the "Outer Chapters" (Waipian) present the words and deeds of the Han, Tang, and Song as the tributary streams of Elementary Learning. Moreover, there is a "General Discussion" (Tonglun) section placed within them, which does nothing other than reiterate the essentials of establishing instruction, clarifying human relationships, and revering the self, while paying special attention to what are called favor and emolument, and dignified demeanor. When favor and emolument are excessive, arrogance and indolence arise therefrom—let us set aside without discussion for now the affair of Prince Zhouxu recorded in the Zuo Commentary (Zuozhuan)—whereas dignified demeanor is a great principle of revering the self, and that whereby establishing instruction and clarifying human relationships are brought to completion. Among the various scholars who have explicated Elementary Learning, there are Mr. Rao [Rao Lu 饒魯] and Mr. Xu [Xu Heng 許衡], while Mr. Xiong [Xiong He 熊禾] wrote the Clause-by-Clause Explanations (Jujie), Mr. He [He Shixin 何士信] compiled the Collected Commentaries (Jicheng), and Mr. Huang [Huang Chang 黃常] edited the Comprehensive Meaning (Tongyi); yet none of these is as clear and complete as the explanations of Mr. Yu of Kuocang [Yu Wenchuan 于文傳]. With regard to dignified demeanor, only Mr. Zhen of Xishan [Zhen Dexiu 真德秀] said: "A person's movements, rites, righteousness, and dignified demeanor cannot be forced; all have their natural rules. Those who are able cultivate them to attain good fortune—this, too, lies simply in reverence." This is now fully recorded in the Collected Explanations (Jijie) of Mr. Wu of Haiyu [Wu Ne 吳訥]; is this not the most superior of these explanations?
Speaking of the Family Rituals (Jiali), its main outlines consist of no more than the four rites of capping, wedding, mourning, and sacrifice. What is recorded in the "Capping Rites" (Guanli) chapter speaks first of notifying the guests (jiebin), next of confirming the principal guest (subin), next of welcoming the guest (yingbin), and next again of the guest bowing to the one about to be capped to take his mat, …

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
始加再加三加盖冠者成人之道始於正容體
終於正君臣親父子和長幼而禮不可以不重
故極於三加至笄禮亦有賓加笄而服背子乃
醮乃冠不用三加者以女將從陽履順故惟一
加而服背子之禮服以少致其謹始之意而示
以裁抑之道也婚禮自議婚納采納幣親迎婦
見舅姑廟見至壻見婦之父母其目有七喪禮
自初終沐浴襲奠為位飯含至小祥大祥禫其
目四十有六祭禮自時祭忌祭至墓祭其目有
===
三然既立其大綱又酌古之禮制而自附於孔
子從先進之意以準之矣苟不取雜儀以附之
則古今喪禮儀文之詳無以知不即祖禰以辨
之則宗支祭禮降殺之由無以見此古禮或不
宜於今務少加損益而不失謹名分崇愛敬之
本俗禮或不合於古亦詳加折衷而必得畧浮
文敦本實之意也然又為通禮一篇以列乎其
前莫非表明喪祭冠禮之畧而致意於曰祠堂
曰深衣者祠堂立則禮敬有所寓朱子所定四
punctuated: 始加、再加、三加。盖冠者，成人之道，始於正容體，終於正君臣、親父子、和長幼，而禮不可以不重，故極於三加。至笄禮亦有賓加笄而服背子，乃醮，乃冠，不用三加者，以女將從陽履順，故惟一加而服背子之禮服，以少致其謹始之意，而示以裁抑之道也。婚禮自議婚、納采、納幣、親迎、婦見舅姑、廟見，至壻見婦之父母，其目有七；喪禮自初終、沐浴、襲、奠、為位、飯含，至小祥、大祥、禫，其目四十有六；祭禮自時祭、忌祭，至墓祭，其目有三。然既立其大綱，又酌古之禮制，而自附於孔子從先進之意以準之矣。苟不取雜儀以附之，則古今喪禮儀文之詳無以知；不即祖禰以辨之，則宗支祭禮降殺之由無以見。此古禮或不宜於今，務少加損益，而不失謹名分、崇愛敬之本；俗禮或不合於古，亦詳加折衷，而必得畧浮文、敦本實之意也。然又為《通禮》一篇以列乎其前，莫非表明喪祭冠禮之畧，而致意於曰祠堂、曰深衣者：祠堂立則禮敬有所寓，朱子所定四
translation_en: … then the first capping, the second capping, and the third capping. For capping marks the way of becoming an adult: it begins with rectifying one's deportment and physical bearing, and ends with rectifying the relations between ruler and minister, fostering affection between father and son, and harmonizing elder and younger. Because the rite must not be treated lightly, it culminates in three cappings. As for the hair-pinning ceremony for girls (jili), there is also a female guest who places the hairpin and invests the girl in a ceremonial vest (beizi), followed by the ceremonial cup of wine (jiao) and the colocar of the headdress. That it does not employ three placements is because a woman is about to follow the yang principle and tread the path of compliance; therefore there is only a single placement and the putting on of the ceremonial vest, so as to express in a modest degree the care taken at the beginning while demonstrating the principle of restraint. For weddings (hunli), from negotiating the marriage, presenting the betrothal gifts (nacai), presenting the bride-wealth (nabi), welcoming the bride in person (qinying), the bride's presentation to her parents-in-law, and her presentation at the ancestral temple (miaojian), down to the groom's presentation to the bride's parents, there are seven sub-headings. For funerals (sangli), from the initial moment of death, bathing the corpse, dressing the corpse (xi), setting out offerings (dian), establishing the mourning places, and placing the mouth-gem and rice (fanhan), down to the lesser auspicious sacrifice (xiaoxiang), the greater auspicious sacrifice (daxiang), and the peace-offering at the end of mourning (tan), there are forty-six sub-headings. For sacrifices (jili), from seasonal sacrifices and death-anniversary sacrifices down to graveside sacrifices, there are three sub-headings. Having thus established the main outlines, [Master Zhu] also weighed ancient ritual institutions and aligned himself with Confucius's intention of following the "men of former times" as his standard. Yet if one did not take the miscellaneous ritual procedures and append them, there would be no way to know the detailed ceremonial forms of ancient and modern funeral rites; if one did not examine the ancestral and paternal shrines to distinguish them, there would be no way to see the reasons for the gradations and reductions in sacrificial rites between the main lineage and branch lineages. Thus, where ancient rites might not be suited to the present, he sought to make slight additions and reductions without losing the fundamental purpose of carefully maintaining status obligations and exalting love and reverence; where popular customs might not accord with antiquity, he likewise carefully weighed and reconciled them so as surely to attain the intention of curtailing superficial ornament and emphasizing fundamental substance. Furthermore, he composed a chapter on "General Rites" (Tongli) and placed it at the front, all of which serves to set forth the general outlines of mourning, sacrificial, and capping rites, while devoting special attention to what are called the ancestral hall (citang) and the deep robe (shenyi): when the ancestral hall is established, ritual reverence has a place to reside—setting aside without discussion for the moment Master Zhu's regulation of four …

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
龕一室之說姑置勿講而深衣平居之常服其
制度精密古服之僅存者也諸家釋家禮者蔡
氏黃氏劉氏而王氏著為深衣考朱氏復為深
衣刋誤然皆不如楊氏之說為精確其於深衣
之制惟慈谿黃氏言玉藻深衣制十有二幅深
長也深長被體故謂之深衣未嘗言裳十有二
幅言裳者鄭註之誤也今具載古燕岳氏之纂
誤此其說之為得者歟愚嘗考朱子小學書題
有曰皆所以為脩身齊家治國平天下之本又
===
考朱子家禮序有曰庶幾古人所以脩身齊家
之道於國家所以崇化導民之意或有小補故
知脩身齊家不可以不勉而垂法立教其功莫
大於朱子也敢舉其槩從下執事請教幸恕其
狂妄而正焉
第三問
黃廷圭
同考試官教諭李批〔以孔子信教二者為時政之急可謂知本之論〕
punctuated:
龕一室之說，姑置勿講。而深衣，平居之常服，其制度精密，古服之僅存者也。諸家釋《家禮》者，蔡氏、黃氏、劉氏，而王氏著為《深衣考》，朱氏復為《深衣刋誤》，然皆不如楊氏之說為精確。其於深衣之制，惟慈谿黃氏言：《玉藻》深衣制十有二幅。深，長也。深長被體，故謂之深衣，未嘗言裳十有二幅。言裳者，鄭註之誤也。今具載古燕岳氏之《纂誤》，此其說之為得者歟？愚嘗考朱子《小學書題》有曰：「皆所以為脩身、齊家、治國、平天下之本。」又考《朱子家禮序》有曰：「庶幾古人所以脩身、齊家之道，於國家所以崇化導民之意，或有小補。」故知脩身、齊家不可以不勉，而垂法立教，其功莫大於朱子也。敢舉其槩，從下執事請教，幸恕其狂妄而正焉。

第三問
黃廷圭
同考試官教諭李批：〔以孔子信、教二者為時政之急，可謂知本之論。〕
translation_en:
…four shrines in one hall may be set aside without discussion for now. As for the deep robe (shenyi), the ordinary dress for daily life, its specifications are precise and detailed, and it is the only ancient garment that survives. Among the various scholars who have explicated the Family Rituals (Jiali)—Mr. Cai, Mr. Huang, and Mr. Liu, while Mr. Wang wrote the Investigation of the Deep Robe (Shenyi kao) and Master Zhu further composed the Correction of Errors on the Deep Robe (Shenyi kanwu)—none is as precise and accurate as Mr. Yang's explanation. Regarding the tailoring of the deep robe, only Mr. Huang of Cixi states: "In the 'Jade-Bead Pendants' (Yuzao) chapter, the deep robe is tailored of twelve widths of cloth. 'Deep' (shen) means long. Because it is deep and long in covering the body, it is called the deep robe; it never says the lower skirt (chang) consists of twelve widths. Speaking of the lower skirt is an error in Zheng Xuan's commentary." This is now fully recorded in the Compilation of Errors (Zuanwu) by Mr. Yue of ancient Yan; is this not the explanation that hits the mark? I have examined Master Zhu's "Note on the Elementary Learning" (Xiaoxue shuti), which says: "All these serve as the foundation for cultivating the self, regulating the family, ordering the state, and bringing peace to the world." I have also examined the Preface to Master Zhu's Family Rituals (Zhuzi jiali xu), which says: "Perhaps the way by which the ancients cultivated the self and regulated the family may be of some small assistance to the dynasty's intention of exalting moral transformation and guiding the people." Thus we know that one cannot fail to exert oneself in cultivating the self and regulating the family, and that in handing down models and establishing teachings, no one's achievement is greater than Master Zhu's. I venture to present the general outline to seek instruction from you, the Attending Examiners; I hope you will forgive my rashness and correct it.

Third Question
Huang Tinggui
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Li: [Taking Confucius's two principles of trustworthiness and instruction as the urgent priorities of current governance can truly be called an argument that understands the fundamentals.]

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭劉批信以足兵食教以安富庶
孔子之格言也而舉以答時務盖王道之要儒
者豈真迂腐哉
考試官教諭吳批策有援據當是有識之士
足食足兵而守之以信既庶既富而加之以教
此先聖之格言而今日之急務也請因明問而
條陳之詩不云乎脩爾車馬弓矢戎兵用戒戎
作用遏蠻方此武衛之所以防禦寇亂也往者
蠻夷弗靖或遇戰而畏怯以守而弛惰誠有如
===
明問所云者今邊塵不驚而野草增綠亦已有
年矣然逸不忘勞而武事其可以不脩乎必欲
將皆智勇兵皆精銳則
朝廷具有
大法總府復有成規惟如孔子所云守之以信於
將帥也量能而後遣乘便而後用賞之必信賞
一人而莫不皆悅罰之必信罰一人而莫不皆
懼如是而使之各練習其兵士則何患戰之不
克而守之不固哉詩不云乎式遏寇虐無俾民
punctuated:
考試官教諭劉批：信以足兵食，教以安富庶，孔子之格言也，而舉以答時務，盖王道之要，儒者豈真迂腐哉！
考試官教諭吳批：策有援據，當是有識之士。
足食、足兵，而守之以信；既庶、既富，而加之以教。此先聖之格言，而今日之急務也。請因明問而條陳之。《詩》不云乎：「脩爾車馬，弓矢戎兵，用戒戎作，用遏蠻方。」此武衛之所以防禦寇亂也。往者蠻夷弗靖，或遇戰而畏怯，以守而弛惰，誠有如明問所云者。今邊塵不驚，而野草增綠，亦已有年矣。然逸不忘勞，而武事其可以不脩乎？必欲將皆智勇，兵皆精銳，則朝廷具有大法，總府復有成規，惟如孔子所云守之以信。於將帥也，量能而後遣，乘便而後用；賞之必信，賞一人而莫不皆悅；罰之必信，罰一人而莫不皆懼。如是而使之各練習其兵士，則何患戰之不克而守之不固哉？《詩》不云乎：「式遏寇虐，無俾民…
translation_en:
Examiner Instructor Liu comments: Trustworthiness to make troops and food sufficient, and instruction to bring peace to a numerous and wealthy populace, are the maxims of Confucius. To cite them in answer to current affairs captures the essentials of the Kingly Way—how could Confucians truly be pedantic and impractical!
Examiner Instructor Wu comments: This policy essay is well-substantiated; he must be a man of insight.
To have sufficient food and sufficient troops, and to uphold them with trustworthiness; when the people are already numerous and already wealthy, to add instruction to them—these are the maxims of the Former Sage and the urgent tasks of today. Allow me to set them forth item by item in response to your enlightened question. Does not the Book of Odes (Shijing) say: "Prepare your chariots and horses, your bows, arrows, and weapons of war, so as to be ready for military action, so as to keep the southern tribes in check"? This is how military defenses guard against and repel banditry and rebellion. In the past, when the southern tribes were unpacified, some met battle with cowardice and held defenses with laxity and sloth, truly just as your enlightened question describes. Now the border dust is undisturbed and the wild grass has grown green again for some years already. Yet in ease one must not forget toil—how could military preparedness go uncultivated? If we wish every general to be wise and brave and every soldier to be well-trained and keen, the imperial court already possesses grand laws, and the regional military command likewise has established regulations; it is simply a matter of upholding them with trustworthiness, as Confucius said. With regard to generals and commanders, measure their abilities before dispatching them, and seize the right opportunity before employing them; in rewarding them, be unfailingly trustworthy, so that by rewarding one man none fail to rejoice; in punishing them, be unfailingly trustworthy, so that by punishing one man none fail to be struck with fear. If in this way each is made to drill and train his soldiers, what worry would there be of failing to conquer in battle or failing to hold fast in defense? Does not the Book of Odes say: "Give check to the cruel and tyrannical, and let not the people…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
憂無棄爾勞以為王休此有司之所以牧養斯
民也往者軍旅屢興或供億而有費饋餉而致
勞亦有如明問所憂者今閭閻寧謐而禾稼登
隴亦既有年矣然安不忘危而治政其可以不
飭乎必欲吏皆循廉民皆安乂則
朝廷具有
成憲撫察亦有定法惟如孔子所云守之以信於
守令也獎勸其賢能懲戒其貪墨進之必信進
一人而莫不皆悅退之必信退一人而莫不皆
===
懼如是而使之各愛養其人民則何患賦不正
供力至重困哉流移之民許之附籍蓋
朝廷一視同仁之心也然爭奪田產以致興訟而
相攻殺此其見利而忘義也今欲絕夫意外之
虞亦惟如孔子所云教之而已誠能謹庠序之
教申之以孝弟之義則斑白者不負戴於道路
何況田產之微乎雖云流移附籍其必永建乃
家而各安生業矣頑梗之徒使之向化此
朝廷篤近舉遠之意也然田耕不賦以至丁壯而
punctuated: 憂。無棄爾勞，以為王休。」此有司之所以牧養斯民也。往者軍旅屢興，或供億而有費，饋餉而致勞，亦有如明問所憂者。今閭閻寧謐，而禾稼登隴，亦既有年矣。然安不忘危，而治政其可以不飭乎？必欲吏皆循廉，民皆安乂，則朝廷具有成憲，撫察亦有定法。惟如孔子所云「守之以信」，於守令也，獎勸其賢能，懲戒其貪墨；進之必信，進一人而莫不皆悅；退之必信，退一人而莫不皆懼。如是而使之各愛養其人民，則何患賦不正供，力至重困哉？流移之民，許之附籍，蓋朝廷一視同仁之心也。然爭奪田產，以致興訟而相攻殺，此其見利而忘義也。今欲絕夫意外之虞，亦惟如孔子所云「教之」而已。誠能謹庠序之教，申之以孝弟之義，則斑白者不負戴於道路，何況田產之微乎？雖云流移附籍，其必永建乃家，而各安生業矣。頑梗之徒，使之向化，此朝廷篤近舉遠之意也。然田耕不賦，以至丁壯而
translation_en:
… distress; do not cast aside your past services, so as to redound to the glory of the king." As for the officials' shepherding and nourishing of the people: in the past, military campaigns were repeatedly launched, which sometimes incurred expenses for supplies and caused hardship in transporting provisions, just as the enlightened question worries. Now the villages are peaceful and tranquil, and the grain crops have been harvested from the fields for several years already. Yet in peace one must not forget danger—how then can civil administration not be kept in order? If we desire that all officials be law-abiding and incorruptible, and that all the people be peaceful and well-governed, the Court already possesses established constitutions, and the pacifying and inspecting authorities also have fixed statutes. We need only, as Confucius said, "uphold them with trustworthiness." In dealing with prefects and magistrates, encourage the worthy and capable among them, and punish the greedy and corrupt; in promoting them, be unfailingly trustworthy, so that when one man is promoted, all without exception are pleased; in demoting them, be unfailingly trustworthy, so that when one man is demoted, all without exception are made fearful. If in this way each is made to cherish and nourish his people, what worry will there be that taxes are not properly supplied or that corvée labor leads to severe exhaustion?

Allowing displaced and wandering people to register in the local household rolls stems from the Court's impartial benevolence toward all. Yet they fight over land and property to the point of initiating lawsuits and attacking and killing one another—this is because they see profit and forget righteousness. If we now wish to put an end to such unexpected perils, we need only, as Confucius said, "instruct them." If we can truly attend carefully to the education in local schools and repeatedly expound to them the duty of filial piety and fraternal respect, then gray-haired elders will not be carrying loads on the roads—how much less would people fight over something as trivial as land and property? Even though they are displaced migrants attached to the registers, they will surely establish their homes permanently and each be content in his livelihood.

Leading stubborn and recalcitrant elements to turn toward civilization reflects the Court's intention of deepening kindness to those nearby while extending it to those far away. Yet they cultivate the fields without paying taxes, and even when they are able-bodied adults…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
不役于官此其見小而遺大也今欲固其率服
之志亦惟如孔子所云教之而已誠能使其壮
者以暇日脩其孝弟忠信入以事其父兄出以
事其長上則可使制挺以撻堅甲利兵何况力
役之微乎雖云頑梗向化其必畏威懷德而格
其非心矣愚也窮經固將以致用觀理亦欲以
應事故對明問不敢妄有所引以語小而遺大
語近而遺遠竊舉孔子之說足食足兵而守之
以信旣庶旣富而加之以教者如此以今觀于
===
將帥守令與流移附籍强梗向化者其所以操
縱之機設施之道在
朝廷則有
廟筭在大臣則有才畧區區愚生乃舉孔子之說雖
若迂闊不切然明問固云窮經以致用觀理以
應事經豈外孔子哉理豈舍孔子哉故始終言
之進退惟命
第四問
陳亹
punctuated:
不役于官，此其見小而遺大也。今欲固其率服之志，亦惟如孔子所云「教之」而已。誠能使其壮者以暇日脩其孝弟忠信，入以事其父兄，出以事其長上，則可使制挺以撻堅甲利兵，何况力役之微乎？雖云頑梗向化，其必畏威懷德，而格其非心矣。愚也窮經固將以致用，觀理亦欲以應事，故對明問不敢妄有所引，以語小而遺大，語近而遺遠。竊舉孔子之說，足食足兵而守之以信，旣庶旣富而加之以教者如此。以今觀于將帥、守令，與流移附籍、强梗向化者，其所以操縱之機、設施之道，在朝廷則有廟筭，在大臣則有才畧。區區愚生，乃舉孔子之說，雖若迂闊不切，然明問固云「窮經以致用，觀理以應事」，經豈外孔子哉？理豈舍孔子哉？故始終言之，進退惟命。

第四問
陳亹
translation_en:
… perform no labor service for the officials—this is because they see only small matters and overlook the great. If today we wish to strengthen their resolve to submit and obey, it is likewise simply a matter of "instructing them," just as Confucius said. If indeed we can cause their able-bodied men in their spare time to cultivate filial piety, fraternal respect, loyalty, and trustworthiness, so that inside the home they serve their fathers and elder brothers and outside they serve their elders and superiors, then they can be made to fashion wooden clubs to strike down strong armor and sharp weapons—how much more so a trifle like labor service? Even though they are said to be obstinate and unruly people turning toward civilization, they will surely stand in awe of authority and cherish virtue, thereby rectifying their errant minds.

I, in my simplicity, exhaustively study the Classics assuredly in order to put them to practical use, and examine principles wishing likewise to respond to affairs. Therefore, in replying to your enlightened inquiry, I dare not rashly cite things that speak of the small while overlooking the great, or speak of the near while overlooking the distant. Instead, I have ventured to adduce the words of Confucius—having sufficient food and sufficient troops and holding to them with trustworthiness, and once the people are numerous and enriched, adding instruction to them—in this manner. Looking today at our generals and commanders, prefects and magistrates, as well as the wandering migrants who have been entered into the registers and the recalcitrant who have turned toward civilization, as for the mechanisms by which to manage them and the ways of implementing policy: in the court there are the imperial strategic counsels, and among the great ministers there are talent and resourcefulness. That a mere ignorant student like myself should bring forward the words of Confucius may seem impractical and wide of the mark; yet your enlightened inquiry explicitly speaks of "exhaustively studying the Classics for practical use and examining principles to respond to affairs." How could the Classics lie outside Confucius? How could principles abandon Confucius? Therefore I have spoken of this from beginning to end; whether I am advanced or rejected rests solely with your command.

Fourth Question
Chen Wei 陈亹

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭許批策發□三代漢唐宋諸賢
忠愛之實而歸宿於善名之重與心術之正亦是確論
考試官教諭劉批諫諍策場中皆善答惟
此包羅無遺佳作也
考試官教諭吴批策有議論非泛泛者可比
慕士之虛名不可不重其善名愛士之學術不
可不察其心術斯言也先民固嘗及之今請以
為執事對夫諫諍者非徒然也孟子云非仁義
之道不陳又云不得其言則去此萬世諫諍之
===
法也自犯顏逆鱗叩頭流血者出而直諫之名
起自和容愉色微言婉辭者見而諷諫之名立
虛名之與善名學術之與心術判于此矣伯益
因禹之有言也而吁以致戒既曰罔失法度罔
遊于逸罔淫于樂而又曰罔違道以干譽罔咈
百姓以從欲其諫不直乎而直之名未起召康
公因王之遊歌也而詩以致警既曰有馮有翼
有孝有德以引以翼而又曰矢詩不多維以遂
歌其諫不諷乎而諷之名未立伊尹將告歸而
punctuated:
同考試官教諭許批：策發□三代、漢、唐、宋諸賢忠愛之實，而歸宿於善名之重與心術之正，亦是確論。
考試官教諭劉批：諫諍策，場中皆善答，惟此包羅無遺，佳作也。
考試官教諭吴批：策有議論，非泛泛者可比。
慕士之虛名，不可不重其善名；愛士之學術，不可不察其心術。斯言也，先民固嘗及之，今請以為執事對。夫諫諍者，非徒然也。孟子云：「非仁義之道不陳。」又云：「不得其言則去。」此萬世諫諍之法也。自犯顏逆鱗、叩頭流血者出，而直諫之名起；自和容愉色、微言婉辭者見，而諷諫之名立。虛名之與善名、學術之與心術，判于此矣。伯益因禹之有言也，而吁以致戒，既曰「罔失法度，罔遊于逸，罔淫于樂」，而又曰「罔違道以干譽，罔咈百姓以從欲」。其諫不直乎？而直之名未起。召康公因王之遊歌也，而詩以致警，既曰「有馮有翼，有孝有德，以引以翼」，而又曰「矢詩不多，維以遂歌」。其諫不諷乎？而諷之名未立。伊尹將告歸而
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Xu: The policy essay brings forth [?] the true loyalty and affection of the worthies of the Three Dynasties, Han, Tang, and Song, and concludes with the importance of a good reputation and the rectitude of mental disposition—this is indeed a sound argument.

Comment by Examiner Instructor Liu: On the policy question concerning remonstrance, everyone in the examination hall answered well, but this essay alone is all-encompassing without omission; it is a fine piece of work.

Comment by Examiner Instructor Wu: The policy essay possesses substantive discussion and is not comparable to superficial ones.

"When admiring a scholar's empty reputation, one cannot but value his good reputation; when cherishing a scholar's learning, one cannot but examine his mental disposition." These words were indeed spoken by people of former times, and now I beg to offer them as my reply to you, the Examiners. Now, remonstrance is not done in vain. Mencius said: "I do not set forth anything other than the ways of benevolence and righteousness." He also said: "When one's words are not heeded, one leaves." This is the standard for remonstrance for ten thousand generations. Ever since those who braved the ruler's countenance, rubbed against the reverse scales of the dragon, and knocked their heads until they bled appeared, the reputation for "direct remonstrance" (zhijian) arose; ever since those who showed a harmonious countenance and pleasant expression and spoke with subtle words and gentle phrases appeared, the reputation for "indirect remonstrance" (fengjian) was established. Empty reputation versus good reputation, and learning versus mental disposition, diverged at this point. Because Yu made a statement, Boyi sighed to deliver an admonition, saying first: "Do not lose the laws and measures, do not wander in idleness, do not indulge in pleasure," and saying further: "Do not go against the Way to seek praise, do not oppose the hundred surnames to follow your desires." Was his remonstrance not direct? Yet the name of "direct remonstrance" had not yet arisen. Because the King went on an excursion and sang, Duke Kang of Shao presented a poem to deliver a warning, saying first: "You have helpers and supporters, men of filial piety and virtue, to lead and to support you," and saying further: "I have offered not many verses, only to accompany your own song." Was his remonstrance not indirect? Yet the name of "indirect remonstrance" had not yet been established. When Yi Yin was about to announce his retirement and…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
陳戒始言惟吉凶不僭在人惟天降灾祥在德
而終之以無自廣以狹人近於直矣傅說旣作
相而受命始言木從繩則正后從諫則聖終之
以對揚天子之休近於諷矣董仲舒天人之策
諷也賈誼治安之疏直也而誼為絳灌所毁遂
至於見斥張蘊古大寶之箴直也張九齡金鑑
之錄諷也而蘊古為萬紀所劾遂至於見疑他
如婁敬諫漢高帝伐匈奴身受械繫而終見褒
美劉行本諫周宣帝不之顧投笏求退而上為
===
斂容此直而不慕虛名庶幾心術之正者歟谷
永之越職抗議似慷慨也而陰黨王氏劉栖楚
之叩墀死爭若高亢也而欲附逢吉其與范仲
淹孔道輔之伏閣奏事叩環呼聲寇萊公之挽
衣苦諍叩榻抗論唐介寧為英州之行而必奪
寵臣之命蘇軾寧為雪堂之游而力沮新法之
行者不啻霄壤豈曰優劣而已哉善名之重心
術之正與務虛名而逞學術者不可同日語也
又如司馬相如之賦子虛鋪張景物諫絶奢侈
punctuated: 陳戒，始言「惟吉凶不僭在人，惟天降灾祥在德」，而終之以「無自廣以狹人」，近於直矣。傅說旣作相而受命，始言「木從繩則正，后從諫則聖」，終之以「對揚天子之休」，近於諷矣。董仲舒《天人》之策，諷也；賈誼《治安》之疏，直也；而誼為絳、灌所毁，遂至於見斥。張蘊古《大寶》之箴，直也；張九齡《金鑑》之錄，諷也；而蘊古為萬紀所劾，遂至於見疑。他如婁敬諫漢高帝伐匈奴，身受械繫而終見褒美；劉行本諫周宣帝不之顧，投笏求退而上為斂容。此直而不慕虛名，庶幾心術之正者歟！谷永之越職抗議，似慷慨也，而陰黨王氏；劉栖楚之叩墀死爭，若高亢也，而欲附逢吉。其與范仲淹、孔道輔之伏閣奏事、叩環呼聲，寇萊公之挽衣苦諍、叩榻抗論，唐介寧為英州之行而必奪寵臣之命，蘇軾寧為雪堂之游而力沮新法之行者，不啻霄壤，豈曰優劣而已哉！善名之重、心術之正，與務虛名而逞學術者，不可同日語也。又如司馬相如之賦《子虛》，鋪張景物，諫絶奢侈；
translation_en: …set forth his admonitions, beginning with the words, "Good and ill fortune do not err in visiting men; Heaven sends down calamity or blessing according to their virtue," and ending with, "Do not aggrandize yourself so as to belittle others"—this was close to direct remonstrance. When Fu Yue 傅說 was made chief minister and received his charge, he began by saying, "When wood follows the marking-line it becomes straight, and when the sovereign follows remonstrance he becomes sage," and ended with, "to respond to and extol the grace of the Son of Heaven"—this was close to indirect remonstrance. Dong Zhongshu's 董仲舒 policy essays on Heaven and Man (Tianren ce) were indirect remonstrance; Jia Yi's 賈誼 memorial on public order and security (Zhi'an shu) was direct remonstrance; yet Jia Yi was slandered by Zhou Bo 周勃 (Marquis of Jiang 絳) and Guan Ying 灌嬰, and consequently was sidelined. Zhang Yungu's 張蘊古 Admonition on the Great Treasure (Dabao zhen) was direct remonstrance; Zhang Jiuling's 張九齡 Record of the Golden Mirror (Jinjian lu) was indirect remonstrance; yet Zhang Yungu was impeached by权 Wanji 權萬紀, and consequently fell under suspicion. As for others, Lou Jing 婁敬 remonstrated with Emperor Gaozu of Han 漢高帝 against attacking the Xiongnu; though personally bound in fetters, he was praised and honored in the end. When Liu Xingben 劉行本 remonstrated with Emperor Xuan of Northern Zhou 周宣帝 and was ignored, he threw down his court tablet and asked to retire, whereupon the Emperor composed his countenance. Were these not men who were direct without coveting empty fame, coming close to rectitude in the art of the mind? Gu Yong's 谷永 stepping beyond his office to submit defiant protests seemed impassioned, yet he secretly sided with the Wang 王 clan; Liu Qichu's 劉栖楚 knocking his head on the palace steps to contend to the death seemed lofty and unyielding, yet he wished to attach himself to Li Fengji 李逢吉. Compared with Fan Zhongyan 范仲淹 and Kong Daofu 孔道輔 prostrating themselves at the palace gates to present memorials, knocking the door-rings and crying out aloud; or Duke Lai, Kou Zhun 寇準 (Kou Laigong 寇萊公), pulling at the Emperor's robes in bitter remonstrance and striking the couch in forthright argument; or Tang Jie 唐介 preferring banishment to Yingzhou 英州 so long as he could strip a favored minister of his appointment; or Su Shi 蘇軾 preferring exile at the Hall of Snow (Xuetang 雪堂) while strenuously opposing the enforcement of the New Policies—the difference is no less than that between heaven and earth! How could one speak of it merely in terms of superiority and inferiority? Cherishing a good name and possessing rectitude in the art of the mind cannot be spoken of on the same day as pursuing empty fame and parading one's scholarly skills. Again, take Sima Xiangru's 司馬相如 rhapsody Sir Fantasy (Zixu), which lavishly depicted scenery and objects so as to remonstrate against extravagance and put an end to luxury;…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
揚雄之賦羽獵盛言車騎諫去夸詐此諷而欲
重善名庶幾學術之美者歟相如再為通西南
之書蓋喜功也而起帝窮兵之念吾丘壽王亦
有得寶鼎之對蓋好大也而萌帝封禪之心其
視歐陽脩侍從規諫不諍口舌范淳夫經筵開
陳色温氣和呂公著辨錫王勇智之語神宗聞
之而為戒范祖禹論酣酒嗜音之句哲宗聽之
而首肯者不啻天淵豈曰是非而已哉蓋心術
之正善名之重與眩學術以求虛名者不可同
時而語也且名一也術亦一也有意於求名則
心術不正矣何取乎學術有意於眩術則善名
不重矣何取乎虛名故有伯益康公伊尹傅說
之忠愛則所以責難而順美者不訐不阿無求
於諷直之名而自得夫諫諍之道有董仲舒賈
誼張蘊古張九齡之忠愛則所以告戒而陳請
者不矯不媚無求於諷直之術而自得夫諫諍
之正忠愛者事
上之本也諫諍者忠愛之發也今欲臨大政決大計
punctuated: 揚雄之賦《羽獵》，盛言車騎，諫去夸詐，此諷而欲重善名，庶幾學術之美者歟？相如再為通西南之書，蓋喜功也，而起帝窮兵之念；吾丘壽王亦有得寶鼎之對，蓋好大也，而萌帝封禪之心。其視歐陽脩侍從規諫，不諍口舌；范淳夫經筵開陳，色温氣和；呂公著辨「錫王勇智」之語，神宗聞之而為戒；范祖禹論「酣酒嗜音」之句，哲宗聽之而首肯者，不啻天淵，豈曰是非而已哉？蓋心術之正、善名之重，與眩學術以求虛名者，不可同時而語也。且名一也，術亦一也。有意於求名，則心術不正矣，何取乎學術？有意於眩術，則善名不重矣，何取乎虛名？故有伯益、康公、伊尹、傅說之忠愛，則所以責難而順美者，不訐不阿，無求於諷、直之名，而自得夫諫諍之道；有董仲舒、賈誼、張蘊古、張九齡之忠愛，則所以告戒而陳請者，不矯不媚，無求於諷、直之術，而自得夫諫諍之正。忠愛者，事上之本也；諫諍者，忠愛之發也。今欲臨大政、決大計，
translation_en: …and Yang Xiong 揚雄 in his Rhapsody on the Plume Hunt (Yulie fu 羽獵賦) grandly described chariots and cavalry to remonstrate against boastfulness and deceit—were these not instances of indirect remonstrance that sought to value a good reputation and nearly achieved beauty in scholarly learning? Yet Sima Xiangru 司馬相如 again composed a letter on opening the Southwest, which stemmed from a fondness for exploits and aroused the emperor's thoughts of exhausting his military forces; and Wuqiu Shouwang 吾丘壽王 likewise offered his reply on obtaining the precious tripod, which stemmed from a fondness for grandiosity and sprouted the emperor's desire to perform the feng and shan sacrifices. Compared with Ouyang Xiu 歐陽脩, who as an attendant official offered corrective remonstrance without verbal contention; Fan Chunfu 范淳夫 (Fan Zuyu 范祖禹), who set forth explanations at the Classics Colloquium with a gentle countenance and harmonious demeanor; Lü Gongzhu 呂公著, who analyzed the phrase "investing the king with courage and wisdom," which Emperor Shenzong 神宗 heard and took as a warning; and Fan Zuyu, who discussed the lines on "reveling in wine and indulging in music," to which Emperor Zhezong 哲宗 listened and nodded in approval—the difference is no less than that between heaven and the abyss; how could one merely speak of right and wrong? For rectitude of mental disposition and the valuing of a good reputation cannot be spoken of at the same time as showing off scholarly learning in order to seek an empty reputation. Moreover, reputation is one, and art is also one. If one has the intention of seeking reputation, then the disposition of the mind is not upright—what is there to commend in one's scholarly learning? If one has the intention of showing off one's art, then a good reputation is not valued—what is there to commend in an empty reputation? Therefore, when one possesses the loyal affection of Boyi 伯益, Duke Kang of Shao 召康公, Yi Yin 伊尹, and Fu Yue 傅說, the way in which one urges difficult duties upon the ruler and complies with his virtues is neither abrasive nor flattering; without seeking a reputation for either indirect or direct remonstrance, one naturally attains the Way of remonstrance. When one possesses the loyal affection of Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒, Jia Yi 賈誼, Zhang Yungu 張蘊古, and Zhang Jiuling 張九齡, the way in which one offers admonitions and submits requests is neither pretentious nor sycophantic; without seeking the art of either indirect or direct remonstrance, one naturally attains the rectitude of remonstrance. Loyal affection is the foundation of serving the Sovereign; remonstrance is the manifestation of loyal affection. Now, if one wishes to confront great affairs of state, decide great plans,…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而一言之必如前數公與范仲淹寇準歐陽脩
蘇軾之當直而直非慕其名也當諷而諷非眩
其術也理有不得已也則何患
朝廷之不信而天下之不慕哉愚也學未能以及
古道未足以入官何敢出位而思但心術之正
善名之重則不可以不勉故以奉復惟垂教焉
第五問
李旹
同考試官訓導陳批禮樂一策詞不冗而事不遺
===
可羨可羨
同考試官教諭張批禮樂辨析明白考據詳
備當冠策場
考試官教諭劉批五策皆優魁選其在是矣
考試官教諭吳批五策詳贍而文皆奇宜第一
本立而文從而禮樂之制以明功成而治定而
禮樂之制以備故歷代之制禮樂皆在功成治
定之日而用禮樂必極本立文從之美也請申
言之敬而將之以玉帛則為禮和而發之以鍾
punctuated:
而一言之，必如前數公與范仲淹、寇準、歐陽脩、蘇軾之當直而直，非慕其名也；當諷而諷，非眩其術也，理有不得已也。則何患朝廷之不信，而天下之不慕哉！愚也學未能以及古，道未足以入官，何敢出位而思？但心術之正、善名之重，則不可以不勉，故以奉復，惟垂教焉。

第五問

李旹
同考試官訓導陳批：禮樂一策，詞不冗而事不遺，可羨可羨。
同考試官教諭張批：禮樂辨析明白，考據詳備，當冠策場。
考試官教諭劉批：五策皆優，魁選其在是矣。
考試官教諭吳批：五策詳贍而文皆奇，宜第一。

本立而文從，而禮樂之制以明；功成而治定，而禮樂之制以備。故歷代之制禮樂，皆在功成治定之日，而用禮樂，必極本立文從之美也。請申言之。敬而將之以玉帛，則為禮；和而發之以鍾…
translation_en:
…and speak of them, one must be like those several worthies mentioned previously, as well as Fan Zhongyan 范仲淹, Kou Zhun 寇準, Ouyang Xiu 歐陽脩, and Su Shi 蘇軾: being forthright when one ought to be forthright, not out of a desire for fame; and offering indirect remonstrance when one ought to offer indirect remonstrance, not to show off one's skill, but because principle leaves no other choice. Then what worry would there be that the court would not trust one, or that the world would not admire one? Stupid as I am, my learning has not yet caught up with the ancients, and my grasp of the Way is not yet sufficient to enter officialdom—how would I dare to think beyond my station? Yet as for rectitude of mind and the weight of a good name, I cannot fail to exert myself in them; therefore I respectfully offer this in reply, praying only for your instruction.

Fifth Question

Li Shi 李旹
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor (xundao) Chen comments: In this policy essay on ritual and music, the wording is not verbose and no facts are omitted—truly admirable, truly admirable!
Associate Examiner and Instructor (jiaoyu) Zhang comments: The analysis of ritual and music is clear and distinct, and the evidentiary research is detailed and complete; it ought to top the policy essay session.
Examiner and Instructor Liu comments: All five policy essays are excellent; the top selection surely lies right here.
Examiner and Instructor Wu comments: All five policy essays are detailed and rich, and their prose is extraordinary throughout; he deserves first place.

When the fundamental is established and the outward form follows, the system of ritual and music is thereby made clear; when merit is achieved and order is settled, the system of ritual and music is thereby made complete. Therefore, the instituting of ritual and music across the ages has always taken place in the days when merit was achieved and order settled, and the employment of ritual and music must reach the perfection of establishing the fundamental with the outward form following. Allow me to elaborate on this. Reverence, when conveyed through jade and silk, becomes ritual; harmony, when expressed through bells…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
鼓則爲樂敬者禮之本和者樂之本以禮之儀
文觀之經禮三百曲禮三千莫非言其經常之
禮委曲之節而禮文之重則玉帛是也以樂之
聲音觀之八音克諧無相奪倫莫非言其衆音
之備和諧之美而樂器之大則鍾鼓是也此書
所以有五玉三帛之文詩所以有賁鼓維鏞之
語孔子欲人因文以知其本故特舉而言之歟
古今禮不相襲樂不相沿伏羲制嫁娶正姓氏
以重人倫歌扶徠斲琴瑟以理情性而禮樂之
===
端肇于此矣繼之者黃帝堯舜也象天地而製
衣裳聽鳳凰而别律吕非黃帝極制作之大乎
薦玉以白繒而大章以奏頒瑞于羣后而大韶
以作非堯舜極制作之大乎至成王祭方明見
藩服以著朝儀教樂舞序祭饗以文聲音而禮
樂之文盛于此矣前之者禹湯文武也以黑爲
徽號而服収冠而黑衣作樂曰大夏而九成五
音以聽治非大禹盡參酌之妙乎服尋冠縞衣
而作大濩服冕旒玄衣而奏大武非湯武盡□□
punctuated:
鼓，則爲樂。敬者，禮之本；和者，樂之本。以禮之儀文觀之，「經禮三百，曲禮三千」，莫非言其經常之禮、委曲之節，而禮文之重，則玉帛是也。以樂之聲音觀之，「八音克諧，無相奪倫」，莫非言其衆音之備、和諧之美，而樂器之大，則鍾鼓是也。此《書》所以有「五玉三帛」之文，《詩》所以有「賁鼓維鏞」之語。孔子欲人因文以知其本，故特舉而言之歟？

古今禮不相襲，樂不相沿。伏羲制嫁娶、正姓氏以重人倫，歌《扶徠》、斲琴瑟以理情性，而禮樂之端肇于此矣。繼之者，黃帝、堯、舜也。象天地而製衣裳，聽鳳凰而别律吕，非黃帝極制作之大乎？薦玉以白繒而《大章》以奏，頒瑞于羣后而《大韶》以作，非堯、舜極制作之大乎？至成王祭方明、見藩服以著朝儀，教樂舞、序祭饗以文聲音，而禮樂之文盛于此矣。前之者，禹、湯、文、武也。以黑爲徽號，而服収冠而黑衣，作樂曰《大夏》，而九成五音以聽治，非大禹盡參酌之妙乎？服尋冠縞衣而作《大濩》，服冕旒玄衣而奏《大武》，非湯、武盡□□
translation_en:
…and drums, it is music. Reverence is the root of rites; harmony is the root of music. Viewed from the ceremonial forms of rites, "three hundred cardinal rites and three thousand detailed rules of ceremony" speak of nothing other than their constant principles and intricate regulations, yet the weightiest of ritual forms are jade and silk. Viewed from the sounds and tones of music, "the eight timbres are able to be in harmony, without encroaching upon one another's proper order" speaks of nothing other than the completeness of the various sounds and the beauty of their harmony, yet the grandest of musical instruments are bells and drums. This is why the Book of Documents has the phrase "five jades and three silks," and why the Book of Odes has the words "large drums and great bells." Did Confucius not single these out for mention because he wished people to know the root through the outward form?

Between antiquity and the present, rites do not copy one another, and music does not simply follow what came before. Fuxi instituted marriage and rectified clan names to give weight to human relationships, and composed the song "Fulai" and fashioned the qin and se zithers to regulate emotions and nature; the beginnings of rites and music originated here. Those who succeeded him were the Yellow Emperor, Yao, and Shun. Modeling on heaven and earth to make upper and lower garments, and listening to the phoenix to distinguish the yang and yin pitch-pipes—was this not the Yellow Emperor reaching the utmost greatness in institution-making? Presenting jade on white silk while performing the "Dazhang" music, and bestowing jade tallies on the various lords while composing the "Dashao" music—was this not Yao and Shun reaching the utmost greatness in institution-making? By the time of King Cheng of Zhou, he sacrificed to the Fangming deity of the four quarters and gave audience to the feudatory lords to make manifest court ceremonial, and taught musical dances and ordered sacrifices and banquets to refine musical sounds; the cultural forms of rites and music reached their flourishing height here. Those who preceded him were Yu, Tang, King Wen, and King Wu. Taking black as his emblem, wearing the shou cap [?] and black robes, composing music called "Daxia" in nine movements, and using the five musical notes to attend to governance—was this not Great Yu exhausting the subtlety of deliberation and adaptation? Wearing the xun cap and white silk robes while composing the "Dahuo" music, and wearing the ceremonial crown with pendants and dark robes while performing the "Dawu" music—was this not Tang and King Wu exhausting [the subtlety of deliberation and]…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
酌之妙乎漢高帝用叔孫通朝儀與通因秦樂
人所定樂制大抵皆秦舊焉武帝時河間獻王
以為治道非禮樂不成乃獻禮五百餘篇又獻
所集雅樂盖漢去古未遠獻王所集多得古書
之遺豈無合於古者至明帝時博士曹充言漢
再受命宜興禮樂自是樂凡四品一曰大予樂
二曰周頌雅樂三曰黄門鼓吹樂四曰短簫鐃
歌樂又采百官詩頌以為登歌此其可考者也
太宗用房玄齡魏徵等所脩貞觀禮及祖孝
===
雅樂大槩皆隋舊焉玄宗時李銳與諸學士
所定五禮盖唐古書猶多有存諸學士所脩亦
豈無合於古者起居舍人王仲丘請依顯慶禮
脩明祀事遂以高祖配圓丘方丘太宗配雩祀
及神州地祗睿宗配明堂此其可言者也宋太
祖因博士聶崇義上所撰三禮圖詔集儒學之
士參議而閱定為十五卷者非竇儼乎儼又改
周樂章十二順為十二安者盖取治世之音安
以樂之義也元世祖詔太保劉秉忠起朝儀徵
punctuated: 酌之妙乎？漢高帝用叔孫通朝儀，與通因秦樂人所定樂制，大抵皆秦舊焉。武帝時，河間獻王以為治道非禮樂不成，乃獻禮五百餘篇，又獻所集雅樂。盖漢去古未遠，獻王所集多得古書之遺，豈無合於古者？至明帝時，博士曹充言漢再受命，宜興禮樂。自是樂凡四品：一曰大予樂，二曰周頌雅樂，三曰黄門鼓吹樂，四曰短簫鐃歌樂；又采百官詩頌以為登歌。此其可考者也。太宗用房玄齡、魏徵等所脩《貞觀禮》及祖孝雅樂，大槩皆隋舊焉。玄宗時，李銳與諸學士所定《五禮》，盖唐古書猶多有存，諸學士所脩亦豈無合於古者？起居舍人王仲丘請依《顯慶禮》脩明祀事，遂以高祖配圓丘、方丘，太宗配雩祀及神州地祗，睿宗配明堂。此其可言者也。宋太祖因博士聶崇義上所撰《三禮圖》，詔集儒學之士參議，而閱定為十五卷者，非竇儼乎？儼又改周樂章「十二順」為「十二安」者，盖取「治世之音安以樂」之義也。元世祖詔太保劉秉忠起朝儀，徵
translation_en:
…the subtlety of adaptation and deliberation? Emperor Gaozu of Han adopted the court ceremonial prepared by Shusun Tong 叔孫通, along with the musical institutions that Tong established by drawing upon the musicians of Qin; on the whole, these were all legacies of the Qin. In the time of Emperor Wu, King Xian of Hejian 河間獻王, believing that the Way of governance cannot be brought to completion without rites and music, presented over five hundred chapters on ritual and also offered the refined music (yayue) he had collected. Now, since the Han was not yet far removed from antiquity, what King Xian gathered preserved much that remained of ancient books—how could there not have been parts that accorded with antiquity? By the time of Emperor Ming, the Erudite (boshi) Cao Chong 曹充 stated that since the Han had received the Mandate a second time, it was fitting to revive rites and music. From then on, music was divided into four categories: the first was called Music of the Grand Predictor (Dayu yue), the second Refined Music of the Zhou Odes (Zhousong yayue), the third Yellow Gate Fife-and-Drum Music (Huangmen guchui yue), and the fourth Short-Flute and Bell-Song Music (Duanxiao naoge yue); in addition, poetic eulogies by the hundred officials were collected to serve as songs for the upper hall (dengge). These are what can be verified from the records.

Emperor Taizong [of Tang] employed the Rites of the Zhenguan Era (Zhenguan li) compiled by Fang Xuanling 房玄齡, Wei Zheng 魏徵, and others, together with the refined music of Zu Xiao[sun] 祖孝[孫] [?], which in general were all legacies of the Sui. In the time of Emperor Xuanzong, the Five Rites (Wuli) were established by Li Rui 李銳 [?] and various Scholars (xueshi); since many ancient books still survived in the Tang, how could what those Scholars compiled not also have had parts that accorded with antiquity? The Imperial Recorder (qiju sheren) Wang Zhongqiu 王仲丘 requested that the sacrificial services be revised and clarified in accordance with the Rites of the Xianqing Era (Xianqing li), and consequently Emperor Gaozu was paired as coadjutor at the Round Mound and Square Mound, Emperor Taizong was paired with the Rain Sacrifice (yusi) and the Earth-Deity of the Divine Continent (Shenzhou dizhi), and Emperor Ruizong was paired with the Hall of Light (mingtang). These are what can be spoken of.

When Emperor Taizu of Song, prompted by the Erudite Nie Chongyi's 聶崇義 presentation of the Illustrations to the Three Ritual Classics (Sanli tu) that he had composed, decreed that Confucian scholars be assembled to deliberate upon it, was it not Dou Yan 竇儼 who reviewed and finalized it into fifteen scrolls (juan)? Moreover, Yan changed the "Twelve Harmonies" (Shi'er shun) of the Zhou musical hymns into the "Twelve Tranquilities" (Shi'er an), taking the meaning from the saying that "the music of a well-governed age is tranquil and joyous." When Emperor Shizu of Yuan decreed that Grand Guardian (taibao) Liu Bingzhong 劉秉忠 should institute court ceremonial and summoned…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
儒生周鐸等議之而稽古典參時宜沿情稱文
制者非許衡乎秉忠復奏無樂以相猶有闕未
備乃製大成雅樂蓋依律運譜而成也及我
朝
太祖高皇帝功成治定制禮作樂
詔有司各行鄉飲命禮部取儀禮及唐宋之制又
采周官屬民讀法之旨參定其儀府州縣每歲
孟春正月孟冬十月行之於學校民間里社以
百家為一會每季行之於里中大率皆本於正
===
齒位之說而賓興賢能春秋習射亦通行焉又
諭尚書牛諒曰定著禮儀宜與諸儒參詳考議今
百官常朝班次及奏事禮儀節目之文官僚所
通習有不待於言也且以前代樂章率用諛詞
以為容悅甚者鄙陋不稱
命尚書陶凱製宴享九奏之樂一曰本太初二曰
仰大明三曰民初生四曰品物亨五曰御六龍
六曰泰階平七曰君德成八曰聖道成九曰樂
清寧而流俗諠譁之樂悉屏去之又
punctuated: 儒生周鐸等議之，而稽古典、參時宜，沿情稱文制者，非許衡乎？秉忠復奏無樂以相，猶有闕未備，乃製《大成雅樂》，蓋依律運譜而成也。及我朝太祖高皇帝功成治定，制禮作樂，詔有司各行鄉飲，命禮部取《儀禮》及唐、宋之制，又采《周官》「屬民讀法」之旨，參定其儀：府、州、縣每歲孟春正月、孟冬十月行之於學校；民間里社以百家為一會，每季行之於里中。大率皆本於「正齒位」之說，而賓興賢能、春秋習射亦通行焉。又諭尚書牛諒曰：「定著禮儀，宜與諸儒參詳考議。」今百官常朝班次及奏事禮儀節目之文，官僚所通習，有不待於言也。且以前代樂章率用諛詞以為容悅，甚者鄙陋不稱，命尚書陶凱製宴享九奏之樂：一曰《本太初》，二曰《仰大明》，三曰《民初生》，四曰《品物亨》，五曰《御六龍》，六曰《泰階平》，七曰《君德成》，八曰《聖道成》，九曰《樂清寧》，而流俗諠譁之樂悉屏去之。又
translation_en:
…Confucian scholars such as Zhou Duo 周鐸 and others to deliberate on it; and as for investigating ancient canons, consulting what was appropriate to the times, and following human sentiments to match cultural institutions, was that not Xu Heng 許衡? [Liu] Bingzhong 劉秉忠 further memorialized that without music to accompany the rites, there were still deficiencies and things left incomplete; thereupon they composed the Elegant Music of Great Perfection (Dacheng yayue), which was crafted by arranging musical scores in accordance with the pitch-pipes.

When it came to our dynasty, after Emperor Gaozu, the Grand Progenitor (Taizu Gao Huangdi), had achieved his merit and stabilized governance, he instituted rites and created music. He decreed that the competent authorities should each carry out the District Symposium (xiangyin), ordering the Ministry of Rites to take the Etiquette and Ceremonial (Yili) as well as the institutions of the Tang and Song, and also to adopt the purport of "assembling the populace to read the laws" from the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan), so as to consult and fix the ceremonial. Prefectures, subprefectures, and counties performed it every year at the schools in the first month of early spring and the tenth month of early winter; among the people, the village communities formed an association of every hundred households and performed it every season within the village. In general, all of this was rooted in the doctrine of "rectifying seats by age," while honoring and recommending the worthy and able, and practicing archery in spring and autumn, were also universally carried out therein. He further instructed Minister Niu Liang 牛諒, saying: "In fixing and setting forth the ritual ceremonies, you should thoroughly examine, investigate, and deliberate on them with the various Confucian scholars." Today, the texts regarding the rank order of the hundred officials at regular court audiences and the ceremonial details for presenting memorials are thoroughly practiced by the bureaucracy and need not be spoken of here. Moreover, because the musical stanzas of previous dynasties generally used flattering words in order to curry favor, and in extreme cases were vulgar and unbefitting, he ordered Minister Tao Kai 陶凱 to compose the music of nine performances for banquets: the first is called "Rooted in the Grand Primordium" (Ben Taichu); the second is called "Looking Up to the Great Brilliance" (Yang Daming); the third is called "The People First Born" (Min chusheng); the fourth is called "All Things Flourish" (Pinwu heng); the fifth is called "Driving the Six Dragons" (Yu liulong); the sixth is called "The Grand Steps Are Level" (Taijie ping); the seventh is called "The Sovereign's Virtue Is Accomplished" (Junde cheng); the eighth is called "The Sage's Way Is Accomplished" (Shengdao cheng); and the ninth is called "Rejoicing in Purity and Tranquility" (Le qingning)—while noisy and clamorous music of vulgar custom was entirely banished. He also…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
諭禮部臣曰大成樂器以祀孔子此宜究心今登
歌樂舞酌獻迎送名義之詳學校所通肄亦不
待贅也惟禮樂之本所謂敬與和者則斯須不
可以去身而禮樂之制所謂明與備者必見聞
而後有所識愚也何幸生
今之世而得昌言其盛哉謹對
punctuated: 諭禮部臣曰：「大成樂器以祀孔子，此宜究心。」今登歌樂舞、酌獻迎送名義之詳，學校所通肄，亦不待贅也。惟禮樂之本，所謂敬與和者，則斯須不可以去身；而禮樂之制，所謂明與備者，必見聞而後有所識。愚也何幸生今之世，而得昌言其盛哉！謹對。
translation_en: … instructed the officials of the Ministry of Rites, saying: "The musical instruments of Great Perfection (Dacheng) are used to sacrifice to Confucius; to this you should devote thorough attention." Now, as for the detailed terms and meanings of the songs sung on the upper terrace, the musical dances, the libation offerings, and the welcoming and sending off of the spirits, these are universally practiced in the schools and need no superfluous elaboration. Only the fundamentals of rites and music—what are called reverence and harmony—may not be separated from one's person even for a moment; whereas the institutions of rites and music—what are called clarity and completeness—must first be seen and heard before they can be understood. How fortunate I am, in my ignorance, to be born in the present age and to be able to speak forthrightly of their flourishing! I respectfully reply.

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣東鄉試錄後序
皇朝設科取士逾百年每三年大比
上詔禮部申飭方岳祗舉
舊章方岳重臣預聘儒碩司考校憲
臣預汰冗濫嚴防範協恭萃和咸
勤罔怠而士之升自庠序舉于山
林拔于戎伍者亦奮志厲氣鼓勇
陳文藝有敬罔肆上下胥
===
丕應同一寅畏奮庸之心
也抑何至哉廣東甲午鄉試璣等
叨職主司凡命題考校第貢士之
名錄中式之文刻為小錄一循其
舊而執事之敬求賢之誠恒若不
及罔敢斁思焉洪惟
天眷
聖明保佑申命純明不已故篤生賢俊
punctuated:
廣東鄉試錄後序

皇朝設科取士，逾百年。每三年大比，上詔禮部申飭方岳，祗舉舊章。方岳重臣預聘儒碩司考校，憲臣預汰冗濫、嚴防範。協恭萃和，咸勤罔怠。而士之升自庠序、舉于山林、拔于戎伍者，亦奮志厲氣，鼓勇陳文藝，有敬罔肆。上下胥丕應，同一寅畏奮庸之心也，抑何至哉！廣東甲午鄉試，璣等叨職主司，凡命題考校，第貢士之名，錄中式之文，刻為小錄，一循其舊。而執事之敬、求賢之誠，恒若不及，罔敢斁思焉。洪惟天眷聖明，保佑申命，純明不已，故篤生賢俊，
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

Since Our August Dynasty established the civil service examinations to select scholars, more than a hundred years have passed. Every three years at the time of the Great Triennial Examination, His Majesty issues an edict to the Ministry of Rites instructing the provincial authorities to reverently carry out the established statutes. The senior provincial administrative officials invite eminent Confucians in advance to take charge of the examining and grading, while the surveillance officials weed out the superfluous and unqualified in advance and strictly enforce the regulations and precautions. Working together in reverent harmony, all are diligent and never remiss. Meanwhile, the scholars—whether promoted from the local schools, recommended from retirement in the mountains and forests, or selected from the military ranks—also rouse their ambitions and sharpen their spirits, mustering their courage to display their literary arts with reverence and without laxity. Superiors and inferiors alike respond grandly to one another, united in a single mind of reverent awe and eagerness to rise to service—how supreme this is! For the jiawu-year (1474) Provincial Examination in Guangdong, I, [Wang] Ji, and my colleagues unworthily held the office of Examiners. In all matters of setting the questions, grading the papers, ranking the names of the tribute scholars, and recording the essays that met the standard to be engraved as this Record, we wholly followed the established precedents. Yet in our reverence in discharging our duties and our sincerity in seeking out the worthy, we constantly felt as though we might fall short, never daring to grow weary in our thoughts. Humbly considering how Heaven looks with favor upon Our Sacred and Enlightened Sovereign, protecting and assisting Him and renewing His Mandate with unceasing purity and brilliance, it thereby generously brings forth worthy and outstanding men…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
無間遐邇雖海隅嶺表譽髦勃興
惟
聖天子秉哲貴德克承
天休簡賢乂民慎終如始惟小大庶臣
欽若
德意進賢匡
國竭忠效職惟爾諸士子漸被
清俟領藏脩丘壑詩書禮樂
===
久仁義忠信存養宜深矧
茲英華之發言有章而文有則獲
登名鄉舉將循資以有祿位矣然
文之中式特進身入官之階耳若
夫潤身以德任官以事德脩于明
事成于畏明之則德無或昧畏之
則事無或隳德不昧而恒明則有
化事不隳而恒立則有功化行功
punctuated: 無間遐邇，雖海隅嶺表，譽髦勃興。惟聖天子秉哲貴德，克承天休，簡賢乂民，慎終如始。惟小大庶臣，欽若德意，進賢匡國，竭忠效職。惟爾諸士子，漸被清俟領，藏脩丘壑，詩、書、禮、樂久，仁、義、忠、信存養宜深。矧茲英華之發，言有章而文有則，獲登名鄉舉，將循資以有祿位矣。然文之中式，特進身入官之階耳。若夫潤身以德，任官以事，德脩于明，事成于畏。明之則德無或昧，畏之則事無或隳。德不昧而恒明則有化，事不隳而恒立則有功。化行功
translation_en: …without distinction between far and near; even at the maritime periphery and beyond the Southern Ranges, men of renown and talent rise up in abundance. Our Sacred Son of Heaven holds fast to wisdom and esteems virtue, capably receiving the blessings of Heaven; He selects the worthy to govern the people, remaining as prudent at the end as at the beginning. All the various officials, great and small, reverently conform to His virtuous intentions, advancing the worthy to assist the state, exhausting their loyalty and fulfilling their duties. And as for you scholars, having long been steeped in the pure transformative influence [?] and having cultivated yourselves in retirement among the hills and valleys, your study of the Odes, Documents, Rites, and Music has been long, and your preservation and nourishment of benevolence, righteousness, loyalty, and trustworthiness ought to be deep. How much more so now that, with this blossoming of your finest talents—your words possessing pattern and your compositions following the standard—you have succeeded in having your names registered in the provincial examination and will follow the order of qualification to attain emolument and office! Yet meeting the standard in literary composition is merely a stepping stone for advancing oneself and entering officialdom. As for enriching one's person through virtue and fulfilling one's office through service, virtue is cultivated through clarity and affairs are brought to completion through reverent caution. When one clarifies it, virtue is never obscured; when one approaches them with reverent caution, affairs are never ruined. When virtue is not obscured but remains constantly bright, there is transformative influence; when affairs are not ruined but remain constantly established, there is achievement. When transformative influence is carried out and achievement…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣可以配天命賛
皇猷可以共天職理天民而天之付畀
於我者斯無愧焉天且不愧况怍
於人乎垂聲炳耀永世無窮諸士
子其以是自勉
成化十年秋八月既望江西廣信
府鉛山縣儒學教諭劉璣謹序
punctuated:
廣，可以配天命、賛皇猷，可以共天職、理天民，而天之付畀於我者，斯無愧焉。天且不愧，况怍於人乎？垂聲炳耀，永世無窮，諸士子其以是自勉！
成化十年秋八月既望，江西廣信府鉛山縣儒學教諭劉璣謹序。
translation_en:
…far-reaching, one can match the Mandate of Heaven and assist the imperial plan, and one can share in the offices of Heaven and govern the people of Heaven; thus, in what Heaven has endowed upon us, there will be nothing of which to be ashamed. If one is not ashamed before Heaven, how much less will one be abashed before men? To leave behind a resplendent reputation that endures forever without end—may all you scholars strive for this!
Respectfully written as a postface on the sixteenth day of the eighth month in the autumn of the tenth year of the Chenghua era [1474] by Liu Ji 劉璣, Instructor in the Confucian School of Yanshan County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi.

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣東鄕試録序
聖天子統御天下之十年
德化流洽民用康阜乃益稽古右文
誕敷詩書禮樂之教以惠幸天下
天下之士莫不爭先淬濯樂於自
新期以仰答
休恩康誥有云作新民今之所以鼓
舞歆動乎其自新之民者既有德
===
以爲本有詩書禮樂以爲輔亦惟
置選舉爵賞之階以爲勸如是而
已廣東爲嶺南大藩士之沾沭
德化以從事乎詩書禮樂蓋百有餘
年其起而登高科縻好爵者亦已
彬彬其盛况有總鎭太監陳瑄平
蠻將軍平鄉伯陳政耀兵出銳以
廓清奸氛有足以佐文教賛治功
punctuated:
廣東鄕試録序
聖天子統御天下之十年，德化流洽，民用康阜，乃益稽古右文，誕敷詩書禮樂之教，以惠幸天下。天下之士，莫不爭先淬濯，樂於自新，期以仰答休恩。《康誥》有云：「作新民。」今之所以鼓舞歆動乎其自新之民者，既有德以爲本，有詩書禮樂以爲輔，亦惟置選舉爵賞之階以爲勸，如是而已。廣東爲嶺南大藩，士之沾沭德化，以從事乎詩書禮樂，蓋百有餘年；其起而登高科、縻好爵者，亦已彬彬其盛。况有總鎭太監陳瑄、平蠻將軍平鄉伯陳政，耀兵出銳，以廓清奸氛，有足以佐文教、賛治功；
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

In the tenth year of the Sacred Son of Heaven's rule over the realm, moral transformation has flowed far and wide, and the people accordingly enjoy peace and abundance. He has therefore all the more studied antiquity and esteemed civil culture, broadly spreading the teachings of the Odes, the Documents, the Rites, and Music so as to favor and bless the world. Among the scholars of the realm, there is none who does not strive to be first to cleanse and polish himself, delighting in self-renewal in the hope of looking up to repay His gracious favor. The "Announcement to Kang" (Kanggao) says: "arouse them to become a new people." Now, the means of inspiring and moving this self-renewing people consists not only in having virtue as the foundation and the Odes, Documents, Rites, and Music as auxiliaries, but also simply in establishing the ranks of selection by examination, noble title, and reward as encouragement—nothing more than this. Guangdong is a great province South of the Ranges. Its scholars have been steeped in moral transformation and have devoted themselves to the Odes, Documents, Rites, and Music for more than a hundred years; those who have risen to attain high examination degrees and hold fine offices are already refined and flourishing in their abundance. Moreover, there are Grand Defender Eunuch Chen Xuan 陳瑄 and General Who Pacifies the Man Barbarians and Earl of Pingxiang Chen Zheng 陳政, who have displayed military might and sent forth elite troops to sweep away the noxious miasma of rebels, sufficient to assist civil education and aid the achievements of governance; …

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而都察院右副都御史吴琛又新
受
簡命加總督兩廣諸軍事舉庶政而
一新之於
朝廷之所以鼓舞歆動乎其自新之
民者必求其所為本與其所為輔
表明倡導使勉就選舉爵賞之階
士學為自新而欲推以新民者顧
===
不繼奮於是哉時監察御史江泝
建節来巡適當選舉之期因慨然
言曰吾將於此驗士所以自新之
效不可以不慎遂勤日夜嚴規程
而防範斥故常之弊文藝戒陳腐
之習務以新嶺南士俗之聞見乃
與布政使周鐸袁凱按察使吕洪
叅政劉昌謝燫卓天錫副使章格
punctuated: 而都察院右副都御史吴琛又新受簡命，加總督兩廣諸軍事，舉庶政而一新之。於朝廷之所以鼓舞歆動乎其自新之民者，必求其所為本與其所為輔，表明倡導，使勉就選舉爵賞之階。士學為自新，而欲推以新民者，顧不繼奮於是哉！時監察御史江泝建節来巡，適當選舉之期，因慨然言曰：「吾將於此驗士所以自新之效，不可以不慎。」遂勤日夜，嚴規程而防範，斥故常之弊，文藝戒陳腐之習，務以新嶺南士俗之聞見。乃與布政使周鐸、袁凱，按察使吕洪，叅政劉昌、謝燫、卓天錫，副使章格、
translation_en:
… Moreover, the Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate, Wu Chen 吳琛, has newly received a special commission giving him the added title of Supreme Commander of Military Affairs in Guangdong and Guangxi, taking up all administrative affairs and renewing them entirely. Regarding the means by which the Court inspires and moves its self-renewing people, he surely seeks out what serves as the foundation and what serves as the auxiliary, making them manifest and championing them so as to encourage men to strive toward the steps of selection by examination, noble rank, and reward. As for scholars who study in order to renew themselves and wish to extend this to renew the people—will they not continue to rouse themselves at this juncture!

At this time, the Investigating Censor Jiang Su 江泝 came bearing his credentials on a tour of inspection, which coincided with the period of the examinations. Moved with resolve, he said: "By means of this, I shall test the efficacy of how the scholars renew themselves; I must not fail to be cautious." Thereupon he toiled day and night, enforcing strict regulations and precautions to cast out entrenched abuses, and warning against stale and hackneyed habits in literary composition, striving thereby to renew what the scholars and commoners of Lingnan hear and see. He then consulted with Administration Commissioners Zhou Duo 周鐸 and Yuan Kai 袁凱; Surveillance Commissioner Lü Hong 呂洪; Administration Vice Commissioners Liu Chang 劉昌, Xie Lian 謝燫, and Zhuo Tianxi 卓天錫; Surveillance Vice Commissioners Zhang Ge 章格, …

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
馮定孔鏞凃棐叅議傅實僉事俞
俊陶魯林錦陳燮諸正陳昭提學
僉事胡榮謀聘儒紳集羣職且獎
飭其士之就選舉者革其舊而新
是圖士亦以聞見之新相與堅其
志作其氣試之日洪親蒞之而凱
與昌司提調格與俊任監巡合試
者千五百人得士七十有五實精
===
選也孜叨典文衡僭因小錄之成
而序之曰夫士之欲有用於天下
必先有以治其心心之所具者充
之可以配天地一蔽於私則銷鑠
殆盡近而無以立其身况及於人
乎是故貴自新也能加之淬濯而
日新焉則其可以配天地者將復
具於我推之而無不準用之而無
punctuated:
馮定、孔鏞、凃棐，叅議傅實，僉事俞俊、陶魯、林錦、陳燮、諸正、陳昭，提學僉事胡榮，謀聘儒紳，集羣職，且獎飭其士之就選舉者，革其舊而新是圖。士亦以聞見之新，相與堅其志，作其氣。試之日，洪親蒞之，而凱與昌司提調，格與俊任監巡。合試者千五百人，得士七十有五，實精選也。

孜叨典文衡，僭因小錄之成而序之曰：夫士之欲有用於天下，必先有以治其心。心之所具者，充之可以配天地；一蔽於私，則銷鑠殆盡，近而無以立其身，况及於人乎？是故貴自新也。能加之淬濯而日新焉，則其可以配天地者將復具於我，推之而無不準，用之而無
translation_en:
…Feng Ding 馮定, Kong Yong 孔鏞, and Tu Fei 凃棐; Assistant Administration Commissioner Fu Shi 傅實; Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Yu Jun 俞俊, Tao Lu 陶魯, Lin Jin 林錦, Chen Xie 陳燮, Zhu Zheng 諸正, and Chen Zhao 陳昭; and Education-intendant Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Hu Rong 胡榮, consulted to invite Confucian gentry and assemble the various officials. Furthermore, they encouraged and admonished the scholars coming for the examination to cast off their old ways and plan anew. Because of the renewal of what they heard and saw, the scholars likewise mutually firmed their resolve and roused their spirits. On the days of the examination, Lü Hong 吕洪 personally oversaw it, while Yuan Kai 袁凱 and Liu Chang 劉昌 served as Proctors, and Zhang Ge 章格 and Yu Jun undertook the duties of Surveillance and Patrol. Altogether those examined numbered one thousand five hundred men, from whom seventy-five scholars were obtained—truly achoice selection.

I, Zi 孜, having had the undeserved honor of taking charge of the literary balance [as Examiner], presumptuously take the occasion of the completion of this brief record to write a preface for it, saying: When a scholar wishes to be of use to the world, he must first have the means to govern his mind. That with which the mind is endowed, if fully developed, can match Heaven and Earth; yet once obscured by selfishness, it melts away almost entirely. Close at hand, he will have no means to establish his own person—how much less extend it to others? For this reason, self-renewal is prized. If one can subject it to tempering and cleansing so as to renew it daily, then that which can match Heaven and Earth will once again be complete within oneself. Extended outward, nothing will fail to be regulated by it; put to use, nothing will fail…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
不化於事業之著夫孰得而禦士
之登是録者既嘗樂育乎
德化之中以從事詩書禮樂而學為
自新尚思今日大臣表明倡導之
功與憲臣及藩臬諸重臣獎飭期
待之意皆所以宣
聖天子惠幸之恩以自致於新而欲以
新士俗者也其可不推其自新以
===
新乎民而無負乎哉惟無所負斯
然後身名光榮有以新嶺南之聞
見又將以新天下之聞見矣爾多
士勉之孜日望之是嵗八月既望
江西吉安府萬安縣儒學教諭吳孜
謹序
punctuated:
不化，於事業之著，夫孰得而禦？士之登是録者，既嘗樂育乎德化之中，以從事《詩》《書》禮樂而學為自新，尚思今日大臣表明倡導之功，與憲臣及藩臬諸重臣獎飭期待之意，皆所以宣聖天子惠幸之恩，以自致於新而欲以新士俗者也。其可不推其自新以新乎民，而無負乎哉！惟無所負，斯然後身名光榮，有以新嶺南之聞見，又將以新天下之聞見矣。爾多士勉之，孜日望之。
是嵗八月既望，江西吉安府萬安縣儒學教諭吳孜謹序。
translation_en:
… not transform; in the manifestation of achievements, who then could withstand it? The scholars whose names are entered in this record have already rejoiced in being nurtured within our sovereign's moral transformation, devoting themselves to the Book of Odes (Shi), the Book of Documents (Shu), ritual, and music, and learning to renew themselves. May they reflect upon the achievements of the grand ministers today in making clear and leading the way, as well as the intentions of the censorial officials and the high provincial administrative and judicial officials in encouraging, admonishing, and holding high expectations for them—all of which serve to proclaim the grace of the Sacred Son of Heaven's benevolent favor, whereby they attain renewal themselves and desire to renew the customs of the scholars. How could they not extend their self-renewal to renew the people, and thus not fail these expectations! Only by failing nothing will their persons and reputations thereafter be glorious, enabling them to renew what is heard and seen in Lingnan, and furthermore to renew what is heard and seen throughout the realm. Strive on, all you scholars! I, Zi, hope for this day by day.

On the sixteenth day of the eighth month of this year [September 26, 1474], respectfully prefaced by Wu Zi 吳孜, Instructor of the Confucian School of Wan'an County in Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi.

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
成化十年廣東鄉試
監臨官
巡按廣東監察御史江泝〔本達福建建安縣人丙戌進士〕
提調官
廣東等處承宣布政使司右布政使袁凱〔舜舉直隸華亭縣人辛未進士〕
廣東等處承宣布政使司左參政劉昌〔欽謨直隸吳縣人乙丑進士〕
監試官
廣東等處提刑按察司副使章格〔韶鳳直隸常熟縣人辛未進士〕
===
廣東等處提刑按察司僉事俞俊〔舜卿直隸揚州衛人丙戌進士〕
考試官
江西吉安府萬安縣儒學教諭吳孜〔勉學福建莆田縣人丁卯貢士〕
江西廣信府鉛山縣儒學教諭劉璣〔叔衡福建甌寧縣人癸酉貢士〕
同考試官
江西饒州府鄱陽縣儒學教諭劉浩〔秉義直隸長洲縣人庚午貢士〕
湖廣武昌府江夏縣儒學教諭李高〔尚節浙江慈谿縣人壬午貢士〕
浙江温州府平陽縣儒學教諭張璨〔彥明福建閩縣人丙子貢士〕
punctuated:
成化十年廣東鄉試。

監臨官：
巡按廣東監察御史江泝〔本達，福建建安縣人，丙戌進士〕。

提調官：
廣東等處承宣布政使司右布政使袁凱〔舜舉，直隸華亭縣人，辛未進士〕；
廣東等處承宣布政使司左參政劉昌〔欽謨，直隸吳縣人，乙丑進士〕。

監試官：
廣東等處提刑按察司副使章格〔韶鳳，直隸常熟縣人，辛未進士〕；
廣東等處提刑按察司僉事俞俊〔舜卿，直隸揚州衛人，丙戌進士〕。

考試官：
江西吉安府萬安縣儒學教諭吳孜〔勉學，福建莆田縣人，丁卯貢士〕；
江西廣信府鉛山縣儒學教諭劉璣〔叔衡，福建甌寧縣人，癸酉貢士〕。

同考試官：
江西饒州府鄱陽縣儒學教諭劉浩〔秉義，直隸長洲縣人，庚午貢士〕；
湖廣武昌府江夏縣儒學教諭李高〔尚節，浙江慈谿縣人，壬午貢士〕；
浙江温州府平陽縣儒學教諭張璨〔彥明，福建閩縣人，丙子貢士〕。
translation_en:
Guangdong Provincial Examination of the Tenth Year of the Chenghua Reign (1474)

Supervising Official:
Jiang Su 江泝, Regional Inspector of Guangdong and Investigating Censor (courtesy name Benda 本達, a native of Jian'an County, Fujian, and a metropolitan graduate of the bingxu year [1466]).

Proctors:
Yuan Kai 袁凱, Right Administration Commissioner of the Guangdong Provincial Administration Commission (courtesy name Shunju 舜舉, a native of Huating County, Zhili, and a metropolitan graduate of the xinwei year [1451]).
Liu Chang 劉昌, Left Administration Vice Commissioner of the Guangdong Provincial Administration Commission (courtesy name Qinmo 欽謨, a native of Wu County, Zhili, and a metropolitan graduate of the yichou year [1445]).

Monitoring Officials:
Zhang Ge 章格, Surveillance Vice Commissioner of the Guangdong Provincial Surveillance Commission (courtesy name Shaofeng 韶鳳, a native of Changshu County, Zhili, and a metropolitan graduate of the xinwei year [1451]).
Yu Jun 俞俊, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner of the Guangdong Provincial Surveillance Commission (courtesy name Shunqing 舜卿, a native of Yangzhou Guard, Zhili, and a metropolitan graduate of the bingxu year [1466]).

Examiners:
Wu Zi 吳孜, Instructor of the Confucian School of Wan'an County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi (courtesy name Mianxue 勉學, a native of Putian County, Fujian, and a tribute scholar [provincial graduate] of the dingmao year [1447]).
Liu Ji 劉璣, Instructor of the Confucian School of Yanshan County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi (courtesy name Shuheng 叔衡, a native of Ouning County, Fujian, and a tribute scholar of the guiyou year [1453]).

Associate Examiners:
Liu Hao 劉浩, Instructor of the Confucian School of Poyang County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi (courtesy name Bingyi 秉義, a native of Changzhou County, Zhili, and a tribute scholar of the gengwu year [1450]).
Li Gao 李高, Instructor of the Confucian School of Jiangxia County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang (courtesy name Shangjie 尚節, a native of Cixi County, Zhejiang, and a tribute scholar of the renwu year [1462]).
Zhang Can 張璨, Instructor of the Confucian School of Pingyang County, Wenzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang (courtesy name Yanming 彥明, a native of Min County, Fujian, and a tribute scholar of the bingzi year [1456]).

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
