title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第一場
四書
斯民也三代之所以直道而行也
衣錦尚絅惡其文之著也故君子之道
闇然而日章
觀水有術必觀其瀾日月有明容光必
照焉
易
===
后以財成天地之道輔相天地之宜以
左右民初九拔茅茹以其彙征吉
利見大人亨利貞
易與天地準故能彌綸天地之道仰以
觀於天文俯以察於地理是故知幽
明之故原始反終故知死生之說精
氣為物游魂為變是故知鬼神之情
狀與天地相似故不違知周乎萬物
punctuated:
第一場
四書
斯民也，三代之所以直道而行也。
衣錦尚絅，惡其文之著也。故君子之道，闇然而日章。
觀水有術，必觀其瀾。日月有明，容光必照焉。
易
后以財成天地之道，輔相天地之宜，以左右民。初九，拔茅茹，以其彙，征吉。
利見大人，亨，利貞。
易與天地準，故能彌綸天地之道。仰以觀於天文，俯以察於地理，是故知幽明之故；原始反終，故知死生之說；精氣為物，游魂為變，是故知鬼神之情狀。與天地相似，故不違；知周乎萬物，
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

"These people are the same as those by whom the Three Dynasties pursued the straightforward path."

"She puts on an unlined outer garment over her embroidered robe, disliking the display of its elegance. Thus the Way of the noble man is unobtrusive, yet it grows more illustrious day by day."

"There is an art to contemplating water: one must contemplate its foaming waves. When the sun and moon shine forth, their light necessarily illuminates every chink that admits a beam."

Book of Changes (Yi)

"The ruler thereby regulates and completes the Way of Heaven and Earth, and aids and furthers the suitability of Heaven and Earth, in order to support and guide the people. Nine in the first place: Pulling up thatch grass with its tangled roots, each according to its kind. Going forward brings good fortune."

"It is advantageous to see the great man. Success. It is advantageous to be resolute and upright."

"The Changes are on a par with Heaven and Earth, and thus can comprehensively order the Way of Heaven and Earth. Looking up, one contemplates the patterns of Heaven; looking down, one examines the configurations of Earth; thus one knows the causes of the obscure and the manifest. Tracing back to the beginnings and following through to the ends, one therefore knows the explanation of life and death. Refined qi forms things, and the wandering soul produces change; thus one knows the conditions and appearances of ghosts and spirits. Being similar to Heaven and Earth, there is no divergence from them. Knowledge encompasses the myriad things,…"

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而道濟天下故不過旁行而不流樂
天知命故不憂安土敦乎仁故能愛
範圍天地之化而不過曲成萬物而
而不遺通乎晝夜之道而知故神无
方而易无體
其旨遠其辭文
書
至誠感神矧茲有苗禹拜昌言曰俞班
===
師振旅
人惟求舊器非求舊惟新古我先王暨
乃祖乃父胥及逸勤予敢動用非罰
世選爾勞予不掩爾善
越三日庚戌太保乃以庶殷攻位于洛
汭越五日甲寅位成若翼日乙卯周
公朝至于洛則達觀于新邑營越三
日丁巳用牲于郊牛二越翼日戊午
punctuated:
而道濟天下，故不過；旁行而不流，樂天知命，故不憂；安土敦乎仁，故能愛。範圍天地之化而不過，曲成萬物而而不遺，通乎晝夜之道而知，故神无方而易无體。
其旨遠，其辭文。
《書》：
「至誠感神，矧茲有苗。」禹拜昌言曰：「俞。」班師振旅。
「人惟求舊；器非求舊，惟新。古我先王暨乃祖乃父，胥及逸勤，予敢動用非罰？世選爾勞，予不掩爾善。」
越三日庚戌，太保乃以庶殷攻位于洛汭。越五日甲寅，位成。若翼日乙卯，周公朝至于洛，則達觀于新邑營。越三日丁巳，用牲于郊，牛二。越翼日戊午，
translation_en:
…and his Dao brings aid to all under Heaven, so he makes no mistakes. He acts extensively yet is not swept away; he rejoices in Heaven and knows its decree, so he is free from anxiety. Content in his station and earnest in benevolence, he is able to love. He encompasses the transformations of Heaven and Earth without erring, and brings all things to completion in their varied ways without omission. He penetrates the course of day and night and understands it; therefore spirit has no spatial restriction and Change has no physical form.

Its meaning is far-reaching, and its expressions are refined.

Book of Documents (Shu):

"Utmost sincerity moves the spirits; how much more so this ruler of Miao!" Yu bowed to the admirable words and said, "Yes." Thereupon he led back the army and marshaled the troops.

"In men, we seek the old; in vessels, we do not seek the old, but the new. Of old, our former kings together with your grandfathers and fathers shared both ease and toil; how should I dare to move and apply undeserved punishments? For generations your labors have been counted, and I do not conceal your goodness."

On the third day, gengxu, the Grand Guardian (Taibao) led the multitude of Yin to prepare the altar sites at the bend of the Luo River. On the fifth day, jiayin, the altar sites were completed. On the next day, yimao, the Duke of Zhou arrived at Luo in the morning and thoroughly inspected the layout of the new city. On the third day, dingsi, he offered sacrifice in the suburbs, using two bulls. On the next day, wuwu,…

工祝致告，徂賚孝孫。苾芬孝祀，神嗜飮食，卜爾百福，如幾如式。既齊既稷，既匡既敕，永錫爾極，時萬時億。禮儀既備，鍾鼓既戒，孝孫徂位，工祝致告。
鳳凰于飛，翽翽其羽，亦集爰止。藹藹王多吉士，維君子使，媚于天子。鳳凰于飛，翽翽其羽，亦傅于天。藹藹王多吉人，維君子命，媚于庶人。鳳凰鳴矣，于彼高岡。梧桐生矣，于彼朝陽。
學有緝熈于光明。
《春秋》：
齊師、宋師次于郎〔莊公十年〕；齊人、陳人、曹
translation_en:
…"then sacrificed to the altars of soil and grain in the new city, with one ox, one sheep, and one pig."
"Heaven orders the people and grants me a single day; whether one comes to a bad end or a good end depends on man."
Classic of Odes (Shi):
"Now let us change the year, and enter this house to dwell."
"The skillful invoker conveys the announcement, and goes to present it to the filial descendant: 'Fragrant has been your filial sacrifice, and the spirits have enjoyed your drink and food. They confer on you a hundred blessings; each as desired, each as sure. You have been exact and expeditious; you have been correct and cautious. They will everlastingly grant you the utmost blessings, in thousands and tens of thousands.' The ceremonies having been completed, and the bells and drums having given their warning, the filial descendant goes to his place, and the skillful invoker conveys the announcement."
"The male and female phoenixes fly about, their wings rustling, as they settle down in their resting place. Numerous are the king's many admirable officers; by the lord they are employed, showing their love for the Son of Heaven. The male and female phoenixes fly about, their wings rustling, reaching up to heaven. Numerous are the king's many admirable men; by the lord they are commanded, showing their love for the common people. The male and female phoenixes give out their notes, on that high ridge. The parasol trees grow, on that eastern slope facing the morning sun."
"By learning, may I make continuous progress toward bright enlightenment."
Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu):
"The army of Qi and the army of Song halted at Lang [tenth year of Duke Zhuang]; the men of Qi, the men of Chen, and the men of Cao…"

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
人伐宋莊公十四年叔孫州仇帥師墮郈
季孫斯仲孫何忌帥師墮費公
圍成定公十二年
遂伐楚僖公四年晉侯齊師宋師秦師及
楚人戰于城濮僖公二十八年公會劉子晉
侯宋公蔡侯衛侯陳子鄭伯許男曹
伯莒子邾子頓子胡子滕子薛伯杞
伯小邾子齊國夏于召陵侵楚定公四年
===
公會晉侯齊侯宋公蔡侯鄭伯衛子莒
子盟于踐土公朝于王所僖公二十八年
公會宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯許男曹伯
晉趙盾癸酉同盟于新城公至自
會晉人納捷菑于邾文公十四年
同盟于戲襄公九年公至自伐鄭襄公十年
同盟于亳城北公至自伐鄭會
于蕭魚公至自會襄公十一年
punctuated:
人伐宋。莊公十四年。叔孫州仇帥師墮郈。季孫斯、仲孫何忌帥師墮費。公圍成。定公十二年。
遂伐楚。僖公四年。晉侯、齊師、宋師、秦師及楚人戰于城濮。僖公二十八年。公會劉子、晉侯、宋公、蔡侯、衛侯、陳子、鄭伯、許男、曹伯、莒子、邾子、頓子、胡子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子、齊國夏于召陵，侵楚。定公四年。
公會晉侯、齊侯、宋公、蔡侯、鄭伯、衛子、莒子盟于踐土。公朝于王所。僖公二十八年。
公會宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯、晉趙盾，癸酉，同盟于新城。公至自會。晉人納捷菑于邾。文公十四年。
同盟于戲。襄公九年。公至自伐鄭。襄公十年。同盟于亳城北。公至自伐鄭。會于蕭魚。公至自會。襄公十一年。
translation_en:
… and the men of Cao attacked Song." (14th year of Duke Zhuang). "Shusun Zhouqiu led a force and dismantled the walls of Hou. Jisun Si and Zhongsun Heji led a force and dismantled the walls of Bi. The Duke laid siege to Cheng." (12th year of Duke Ding).

"Thereupon they attacked Chu." (4th year of Duke Xi). "The Marquis of Jin, an army of Qi, an army of Song, and an army of Qin fought with the men of Chu at Chengpu." (28th year of Duke Xi). "The Duke met with Viscount Liu, the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Cai, the Marquis of Wei, the Viscount of Chen, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Dun, the Viscount of Hu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, the Viscount of Little Zhu, and Guo Xia of Qi at Shaoling, and made an incursion into Chu." (4th year of Duke Ding).

"The Duke met with the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Cai, the Earl of Zheng, the Viscount of Wei, and the Viscount of Ju, and covenanted at Jiantu. The Duke had an audience at the King's residence." (28th year of Duke Xi).

"The Duke met with the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, the Earl of Cao, and Zhao Dun of Jin; on the guiyou day, they covenanted together at Xincheng. The Duke arrived back from the meeting. The men of Jin sought to install Jiezai in Zhu." (14th year of Duke Wen).

"They covenanted together at Xi." (9th year of Duke Xiang). "The Duke arrived back from attacking Zheng." (10th year of Duke Xiang). "They covenanted together north of Bocheng. The Duke arrived back from attacking Zheng. They met at Xiaoyu. The Duke arrived back from the meeting." (11th year of Duke Xiang).

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
禮記
毋失經紀以初為常
樂所以脩内也禮所以脩外也禮樂交
錯於中發形於外
故玄酒在室醴醆在戶粢醍在堂澄酒
在下陳其犧牲備其鼎俎列其琴瑟
管磬鐘鼓脩其祝嘏以降上神與其
先祖以正君臣以篤父子以睦兄弟
===
以齊上下夫婦有所是謂承天之祜
金石絲竹樂之器也詩言其志也歌咏
其聲也舞動其容也三者本於心然
後樂器從之
第二場
論
治天下以正風俗得賢才為本
詔誥表〔內科壹道〕
punctuated:
《禮記》
毋失經紀，以初為常。
樂所以脩内也，禮所以脩外也。禮樂交錯於中，發形於外。
故玄酒在室，醴醆在戶，粢醍在堂，澄酒在下。陳其犧牲，備其鼎俎，列其琴瑟、管磬、鐘鼓，脩其祝嘏，以降上神與其先祖。以正君臣，以篤父子，以睦兄弟，以齊上下，夫婦有所。是謂承天之祜。
金石絲竹，樂之器也。詩，言其志也；歌，咏其聲也；舞，動其容也。三者本於心，然後樂器從之。

第二場
論
治天下以正風俗得賢才為本
詔誥表〔內科壹道〕
translation_en:
Record of Rites (Liji)
Do not lose the guiding norms, taking the beginning as the constant rule.
Music is that by which the interior is cultivated; rites are that by which the exterior is cultivated. Rites and music interweave within and manifest in form without.
Therefore, the dark water is in the inner chamber, the sweet wine and must are by the door, the reddish-clear wine is in the hall, and the clarified wine is below. They set out the sacrificial victims, prepare the tripods and stands, array the zithers, pipes, chime-stones, bells, and drums, and order the prayers and benedictions, so as to bring down the spirits on high and the ancestors; so as to rectify ruler and minister, to deepen the affection between father and son, to harmonize elder and younger brothers, to regulate superiors and inferiors, and so that husband and wife have their proper places. This is called receiving the blessings of Heaven.
Metal, stone, silk, and bamboo are the instruments of music. Poetry expresses the intent; song prolongs the voice; dance moves the countenance. These three originate in the mind, and only afterward do the musical instruments follow them.

Second Session
Discourse
Governing All under Heaven Takes Rectifying Customs and Obtaining Worthy Talent as Its Foundation
Imperial Edict, Mandate, and Memorial [Candidates answer one]

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
擬漢高帝定元功位次詔
擬唐以韓愈爲國子祭酒誥
擬宋以劉珙同知樞密院事謝表
判語
官文書稽程
立嫡子違法
良賤為婚姻
主將不固守
===
屏去人服食
第三場
策
問古先聖王之治天下必旌別淑慝示
之勸懲書云董正治官詩云式序在
位盖先正百官而後及萬民也舜有
天下選於眾舉臯陶不仁者遠矣湯
有天下選於眾舉伊尹不仁者遠矣
punctuated:
擬漢高帝定元功位次詔。
擬唐以韓愈爲國子祭酒誥。
擬宋以劉珙同知樞密院事謝表。

判語：
官文書稽程。
立嫡子違法。
良賤為婚姻。
主將不固守。
屏去人服食。

第三場

策：
問：古先聖王之治天下，必旌別淑慝，示之勸懲。《書》云「董正治官」，《詩》云「式序在位」，盖先正百官而後及萬民也。舜有天下，選於眾，舉臯陶，不仁者遠矣；湯有天下，選於眾，舉伊尹，不仁者遠矣；
translation_en:
Imitation of an edict by Emperor Gaozu of Han determining the order of ranks for those of foremost merit.
Imitation of a Tang mandate appointing Han Yu 韓愈 as Chancellor of the Directorate of Education (Guozi jijiu).
Imitation of a Song memorial of gratitude by Liu Gong 劉珙 upon his appointment as Co-administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs (Tongzhi shumiyuan shi).

Legal Judgments:
Delay in the transmission of official documents.
Illegally establishing an heir-apparent.
Marriage between free persons and those of mean status.
Commanding generals failing to hold their positions firmly.
Depriving a person of clothing and food.

Third Session

Policy Questions:
Question: When the ancient sage-kings governed all under heaven, they invariably distinguished the good from the evil in order to demonstrate encouragement and warning. The Classic of Documents (Shu) says, "Strictly regulate the governing officials," and the Classic of Odes (Shi) says, "Ordering them according to their positions." This is because they first rectified the hundred officials and only afterward extended their governance to the myriad people. When Shun possessed all under heaven, he selected from among the multitude and raised up Gao Yao 臯陶, and those who were inhumane were kept at a distance; when Tang possessed all under heaven, he selected from among the multitude and raised up Yi Yin 伊尹, and those who were inhumane were kept at a distance…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
豈亦勸懲明而淑慝分歟我
朝
太祖高皇帝大誥三編
太宗文皇帝為善陰隲孝順事實二書
宣宗章皇帝五倫書皆以訓戒天下敦勸懲
別淑慝於詩書所云固同一揆而視
舜湯所舉抑亦有可考者歟且所載
有剛斷嫉惡不容奸偽者又有交不
===
變色德優於才者其與斷獄四百人
無怨言深厚不伐絕口舊恩果何優
劣有夙夜在公恪遵古道者又有超
出羣職進膺嘉勞者其與為政公忠
注當貴顯教化大行政有三異果何
得失有禁戢士卒市肆不移者又有
發廩賑饑民多來歸者其與申令戢
下所至悅服救灾有法從如歸市果
punctuated: 豈亦勸懲明而淑慝分歟？我朝太祖高皇帝《大誥》三編，太宗文皇帝《為善陰隲》、《孝順事實》二書，宣宗章皇帝《五倫書》，皆以訓戒天下，敦勸懲、別淑慝，於《詩》、《書》所云固同一揆，而視舜、湯所舉抑亦有可考者歟？且所載有剛斷嫉惡、不容奸偽者，又有交不變色、德優於才者，其與斷獄四百、人無怨言，深厚不伐、絕口舊恩，果何優劣？有夙夜在公、恪遵古道者，又有超出羣職、進膺嘉勞者，其與為政公忠、注當貴顯，教化大行、政有三異，果何得失？有禁戢士卒、市肆不移者，又有發廩賑饑、民多來歸者，其與申令戢下、所至悅服，救灾有法、從如歸市，果
translation_en:
Was this not also because encouragement and chastisement were made clear and the good and the wicked were distinguished? In our dynasty, the three compilations of the Grand Pronouncements (Dagao) by Emperor Taizu Gaohuangdi, the two books Secret Merits of Doing Good (Weishan yinzhi) and True Examples of Filial Piety (Xiaoshun shishi) by Emperor Taizong Wenhuangdi, and the Book of the Five Human Relationships (Wulun shu) by Emperor Xuanzong Zhanghuangdi were all meant to instruct and admonish the realm, to foster encouragement and chastisement, and to distinguish the good from the wicked. They are certainly identical in principle to what is stated in the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents; yet when compared with the appointments made by Shun and Tang, is there also something that can be examined in them?

Moreover, among those recorded therein, there was one who was resolute and decisive, hated evil, and did not tolerate treachery or falsehood, and another who did not change countenance in his dealings and whose virtue surpassed his talent; how do they compare in superiority or inferiority with the one who adjudicated four hundred prison cases without a single word of resentment from the people, and the one who was profound and unboastful, never speaking of past favors? There was one who attended to public duties from morning till night and reverently followed the ancient way, and another who stood out above the multitude of officials and was advanced to receive commendation for his labors; how do they compare in merits and shortcomings with the one whose governance was public-spirited and loyal and who was noted as destined for noble prominence, and the one under whom moral transformation greatly prevailed and whose administration produced three marvels? There was one who restrained his soldiers so that the market stalls remained undisturbed, and another who opened the granaries to relieve famine so that the people came in great numbers to give their allegiance; when compared with the one who reiterated orders to restrain his subordinates so that people gladly submitted wherever he went, and the one who had a method for disaster relief so that people followed him as if flocking to a market, how do they…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
何同異有思母不置悲戚而卒者又
有嚙蛆剠股姑獲賜羹者其與不許
歸養毀不勝哀悲慟嘔血聞者泣下
果何甄別此諸生素所誦習而講求
者今欲舉一賢者則使不賢者勸進
一能者則使不能者戒何道以致之
歟願詳對毋讓
問朱子著小學家禮二書以為脩身齊
===
家治國平天下之本今天下所通習
者請舉其槩從諸生論之夫立教明
倫敬身小學一書之大綱也立教篇
載教非一端而先於母教至稽古始
言父教而亦後於母教何歟其亦有
可考歟明倫之目五敬身之目四可
得而詳歟然既立為大綱而又稽古
以證之矣何又取嘉言以廣之而善
punctuated:
何同異？有思母不置、悲戚而卒者，又有嚙蛆剠股、姑獲賜羹者，其與不許歸養、毀不勝哀，悲慟嘔血、聞者泣下，果何甄別？此諸生素所誦習而講求者。今欲舉一賢者則使不賢者勸，進一能者則使不能者戒，何道以致之歟？願詳對毋讓。
問：朱子著《小學》、《家禮》二書，以為脩身、齊家、治國、平天下之本，今天下所通習者，請舉其槩，從諸生論之。夫「立教」、「明倫」、「敬身」，《小學》一書之大綱也。〈立教〉篇載教非一端，而先於母教，至〈稽古〉始言父教，而亦後於母教，何歟？其亦有可考歟？「明倫」之目五，「敬身」之目四，可得而詳歟？然既立為大綱，而又〈稽古〉以證之矣，何又取〈嘉言〉以廣之，而〈善
translation_en:
…after all is their similarity or difference? There was one who longed ceaselessly for his mother and died of grief, and another who bit off maggots and cut flesh from her thigh, and whose mother-in-law was bestowed soup; how after all are they to be distinguished from the one who was not permitted to return home to care for his mother and became emaciated beyond what grief could bear, and the one who mourned so bitterly that he vomited blood and moved those who heard him to tears? These are matters that you students have long recited, studied, and investigated. Now, if one wishes to promote a single worthy man so that the unworthy are encouraged, and advance a single capable man so that the incapable are admonished, by what way can this be brought about? Please reply in detail and do not hold back.

Question: Master Zhu [Zhu Xi 朱熹] wrote the two books Elementary Learning (Xiaoxue) and Family Rituals (Jiali) as the foundation for cultivating the person, regulating the family, governing the state, and bringing peace to the world. Since they are universally studied throughout the empire today, allow me to raise their general outlines and discuss them with you students. Now, "Establishing Instruction" (Lijiao), "Clarifying Human Relations" (Minglun), and "Revering the Person" (Jingshen) are the main guiding principles of the Elementary Learning. The chapter "Establishing Instruction" records more than one kind of instruction, yet it begins with maternal instruction; only when we reach "Examining Antiquity" (Jigu) is paternal instruction mentioned, and even there it comes after maternal instruction—why is this? Can this also be investigated and verified? There are five subheadings under "Clarifying Human Relations" and four subheadings under "Revering the Person"—can they be explained in detail? Moreover, having already set up these three as the main guiding principles and further adduced "Examining Antiquity" to substantiate them, why did he also select "Fine Words" (Jiayan) to broaden them, and "Good…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
行以實之歟所謂内篇外篇何所指
歟而又著為通論以介乎其間其故
何歟或者謂其所以申明立教明倫
敬身之畧而獨致意於曰寵祿曰威
儀何歟諸家之說有可舉其優劣歟
冠婚喪祭家禮一書之大綱也冠禮
載冠非一節而極於三加至笄禮不
用三加而又獨服背子何歟其亦有
===
可考歟婚禮之目七喪禮之目四十
有六祭禮之目三可得而詳歟然既
立為大綱而又酌古以準之矣何又
取雜儀以附之而祖禰以辨之歟所
謂古禮俗禮何所别歟而又摘為通
禮以列乎其前其故何歟或者謂其
表明家居日用之常而獨致意於曰
祠堂曰深衣何歟諸家之說有可言
punctuated: 行以實之歟？所謂內篇、外篇，何所指歟？而又著為《通論》以介乎其間，其故何歟？或者謂其所以申明立教、明倫、敬身之畧，而獨致意於曰寵祿、曰威儀，何歟？諸家之說，有可舉其優劣歟？冠、婚、喪、祭，《家禮》一書之大綱也。《冠禮》載冠非一節，而極於三加；至笄禮不用三加，而又獨服背子，何歟？其亦有可考歟？《婚禮》之目七，《喪禮》之目四十有六，《祭禮》之目三，可得而詳歟？然既立為大綱，而又酌古以準之矣，何又取雜儀以附之，而祖禰以辨之歟？所謂古禮、俗禮，何所別歟？而又摘為《通禮》以列乎其前，其故何歟？或者謂其表明家居日用之常，而獨致意於曰祠堂、曰深衣，何歟？諸家之說，有可言…
translation_en:
…Deeds (Shanxing) to substantiate them? What do the so-called "Inner Chapters" (Neipian) and "Outer Chapters" (Waipian) refer to? And why did he also compose the "General Discussions" (Tonglun) to place between them? Some say it was in order to reiterate the general outlines of Establishing Instruction (Lijiao), Clarifying Human Moral Relations (Minglun), and Revering the Person (Jingshen), yet why did he pay special attention solely to what is called favor and emolument, and what is called dignified demeanor? Among the explanations of the various commentators, can their relative merits be cited?

Capping, wedding, mourning, and ancestral sacrifices are the overarching themes of the book Family Rituals (Jiali). The chapter on Capping Rituals (Guanli) records more than a single step for capping, culminating in the "threefold bestowal of caps" (sanjia); yet when it comes to the hairpinning ceremony (jili) for women, why does it not use the threefold bestowal, and why does she uniquely wear the sleeveless jacket (beizi)? Is there also something in this that can be investigated? There are seven sub-headings under Wedding Rituals (Hunli), forty-six sub-headings under Mourning Rituals (Sangli), and three sub-headings under Sacrificial Rituals (Jili)—can these be explained in detail? Moreover, having already established these as the overarching themes and deliberated upon antiquity to set the standard for them, why did he also select miscellaneous ceremonies to append to them, and distinguish between distant ancestors and deceased fathers (zuni)? What is the distinction between the so-called "ancient rituals" and "customary rituals"? And why did he also extract the "General Rituals" (Tongli) to place at the front of the work? Some say this was to elucidate the constant norms of daily life at home, yet why did he pay special attention solely to what is called the ancestral hall (citang) and what is called the deep robe (shenyi)? Among the explanations of the various commentators, can one speak of…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
其得失歟諸生行將出以用世其明
以告我以觀脩身齊家之學
問窮經將以致用觀理所以應事天下
之事小可以喻大近可以該遠姑舉
二廣言之武衞防禦寇亂也往年蠻
夷弗靖或遇戰則潰以守則失矣今
雖邊塵已息然武事不可不脩何以
使將皆智勇兵皆精銳而戰無不克
===
守無不固歟有司牧養斯民也比年
軍旅屢興或斂財以供費勞民以餽
餉矣今雖閭閻不擾然治政不可不
飭何以使吏皆循廉民皆安乂而賦
惟正供力無重困歟流移之民雖曰
附籍然爭奪田產小則興詞訟大則
相攻殺團結嘯聚意外之虞可憂也
何以使永建乃家而各安生業歟頑
punctuated:
其得失歟？諸生行將出以用世，其明以告我，以觀脩身齊家之學。
問：窮經將以致用，觀理所以應事。天下之事，小可以喻大，近可以該遠，姑舉二廣言之：武衞，防禦寇亂也。往年蠻夷弗靖，或遇戰則潰，以守則失矣。今雖邊塵已息，然武事不可不脩。何以使將皆智勇、兵皆精銳，而戰無不克、守無不固歟？有司，牧養斯民也。比年軍旅屢興，或斂財以供費，勞民以餽餉矣。今雖閭閻不擾，然治政不可不飭。何以使吏皆循廉、民皆安乂，而賦惟正供、力無重困歟？流移之民，雖曰附籍，然爭奪田產，小則興詞訟，大則相攻殺，團結嘯聚，意外之虞，可憂也。何以使永建乃家，而各安生業歟？頑
translation_en:
… their merits and defects? You students are soon to go forth to be of service to the world; explain this clearly to me, so that I may observe your learning in cultivating the person and regulating the family.

Question: Exhausting the Classics is intended for practical application, and observing principles is the means to respond to affairs. In the affairs of the realm, the small can illustrate the great, and the near can encompass the distant. Let us speak tentatively by taking the Two Guang [Guangdong and Guangxi] as an example: Military Guards (wuwei) are for defending against banditry and rebellion. In past years, when the southern tribes were unpacified, at times our forces routed upon encountering battle, and lost their positions when attempting to defend them. Although the dust on the frontiers has now settled, military preparedness must not be neglected. How can we ensure that the commanders are all wise and courageous, the soldiers all elite and sharp, so that in attack nothing is unconquered and in defense nothing is unheld? The local authorities (yousi) are there to shepherd and nourish the people. In recent years, military campaigns have been repeatedly launched; at times wealth has been exacted to supply expenses, and the people have been burdened with transporting provisions. Although the villages are now undisturbed, civil administration must not go unrectified. How can we ensure that the officials are all law-abiding and incorruptible, the people all peaceful and well-governed, and that taxes are limited to regular quotas while corvée labor does not impose heavy distress? As for displaced and migrant people, although they are said to have been entered into the household registers, they contend over fields and property—on a small scale instigating lawsuits, and on a large scale attacking and killing one another, banding together and gathering in mobs—making the danger of unforeseen incidents cause for concern. How can we ensure that they permanently establish their homes and each take comfort in their livelihoods? As for obstinate …

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
梗之徒雖曰向化然田耕而賦不入
於公廪丁壮而力不役於有司窺覘
侮慢率服之意未誠也何以使畏威
懷德而格其非心歟諸士子生長是
邦凡此數者觸目經心有年矣幸酌
古準今以陳久安長治之策
問君子之事
上也莫急於忠愛忠愛之發莫先於諫諍古
===
有諷諫有直諫其何所取義歟吁咈
致儆與矢詩遂歌者孰為諷而孰為
直告歸陳戒與稽首對揚者孰為直
而孰為諷天人之策治安之疏其詞
之所及者或為諷或為直均一忠愛
也何誼獨見斥大寶之箴金鑑之録
其意之所主者或為直或為諷同一
忠愛也何蘊古獨見疑他如械繫不
punctuated:
梗之徒雖曰向化，然田耕而賦不入於公廪，丁壮而力不役於有司，窺覘侮慢，率服之意未誠也。何以使畏威懷德而格其非心歟？諸士子生長是邦，凡此數者，觸目經心有年矣。幸酌古準今，以陳久安長治之策。

問：君子之事上也，莫急於忠愛；忠愛之發，莫先於諫諍。古有諷諫，有直諫，其何所取義歟？吁咈致儆與矢詩遂歌者，孰為諷而孰為直？告歸陳戒與稽首對揚者，孰為直而孰為諷？《天人》之策、《治安》之疏，其詞之所及者或為諷、或為直，均一忠愛也，何誼獨見斥？《大寶》之箴、《金鑑》之録，其意之所主者或為直、或為諷，同一忠愛也，何蘊古獨見疑？他如械繫不
translation_en:
…and obstinate fellows are said to have turned toward civilization, yet their fields are plowed while their taxes do not enter the public granaries, and their adult males are strong while their labor is not conscripted by the authorities; they spy for opportunities and act with insolent contempt, so their intention to submit is not yet sincere. How can we cause them to stand in awe of authority, cherish virtue, and rectify their errant minds? You gentlemen were born and raised in this region; for years now, all these several matters have met your eyes and occupied your minds. Please weigh antiquity and take the present as your standard to set forth a policy essay for lasting peace and enduring order.

Question: In a gentleman's service to his sovereign, nothing is more urgent than loyalty and affection; in the expression of loyalty and affection, nothing comes before remonstrance. In antiquity there was indirect remonstrance (fengjian) and direct remonstrance (zhijian)—from what do they derive their meaning? Between uttering cries of "Alas!" and "No!" to deliver a warning [as in the Book of Documents] and composing poems to sing in accompaniment [as in the Book of Odes], which is indirect and which is direct? Between announcing one's retirement while setting forth admonitions and bowing one's head to the ground in extolling reply, which is direct and which is indirect? In the policy essays on Heaven and Man (Tianren zhi ce) [by Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒] and the memorial on Peace and Order (Zhi'an zhi shu) [by Jia Yi 賈誼], what their words touched upon was either indirect or direct; both were equally motivated by loyalty and affection, so why was Jia Yi alone rejected? In the Admonition on the Great Treasure (Dabao zhi zhen) [by Zhang Yungu 張蘊古] and the Record of the Golden Mirror (Jinjian zhi lu) [by Zhang Jiuling 張九齡], what their intentions centered upon was either direct or indirect; both were identically motivated by loyalty and affection, so why was Zhang Yungu alone suspected? As for other cases, such as not…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
恤而終受褒美投笏求退而上至歛
容與越職抗議事若慷慨叩墀死争
節若高亢是其諫皆以直自許者也
其視伏閤奏事叩環呼聲挽衣苦諍
叩榻抗論寧為英州之行而必奪寵
臣之命寧為雪堂之游而力沮新法
之行果孰優而孰劣至如子虛之作
鋪張景物羽獵之賦偽言車騎遁西
===
南有書得寳鼎有對是其諫皆以諷
自名者也其視侍從規諫不諍口舌
經筵開陳色溫氣和辨錫王勇智之
語論酣酒嗜音之句果孰是而孰非
方今
朝廷清明政事脩舉固無可言之事設臨
大政關大計欲一言之不訐以為直
不媚以取容必欲
punctuated: 恤，而終受褒美；投笏求退，而上至歛容；與越職抗議，事若慷慨；叩墀死争，節若高亢：是其諫皆以直自許者也。其視伏閤奏事，叩環呼聲；挽衣苦諍，叩榻抗論；寧為英州之行，而必奪寵臣之命；寧為雪堂之游，而力沮新法之行，果孰優而孰劣？至如《子虛》之作，鋪張景物；《羽獵》之賦，偽言車騎；遁西南有書，得寳鼎有對：是其諫皆以諷自名者也。其視侍從規諫，不諍口舌；經筵開陳，色溫氣和；辨「錫王勇智」之語，論「酣酒嗜音」之句，果孰是而孰非？方今朝廷清明，政事脩舉，固無可言之事。設臨大政、關大計，欲一言之，不訐以為直，不媚以取容，必欲
translation_en:
…without regard for oneself, yet finally receiving praise and honor; throwing down one's tablet to request retirement, causing the sovereign to compose his countenance; along with overstepping one's office to protest, acting as if with fervent generosity; and knocking one's head on the palace steps to argue to the death, showing an integrity that seems lofty and unyielding—all of these are remonstrances that prided themselves on being direct. Compared to prostrating oneself before the palace gates to present memorials and knocking on the door-ring while crying out; pulling at the emperor's robes in bitter remonstrance and striking the couch in defiant argument; preferring banishment to Yingzhou if only to revoke the appointment of a favored minister; or preferring exile to Xuetang (Snow Hall) while striving to block the implementation of the New Policies—which of these are superior and which inferior?

As for the composition of the Rhapsody on Sir Fantasy (Zixu), which extravagantly described scenery and objects; the Rhapsody on the Plume Hunt (Yulie), which fabricated accounts of chariots and cavalry; the letter presented upon fleeing to the southwest, and the reply submitted upon the acquisition of the precious tripod—all of these are remonstrances that styled themselves as indirect admonition. Compared to offering corrective advice while in attendance without wrangling in words; setting forth explanations at the Classics Colloquium with a gentle countenance and harmonious breath; analyzing the phrase "Heaven endowed the king with courage and wisdom," or discussing the lines on "indulging in wine and being fond of music"—which of these are right and which wrong?

At present, the Imperial Court is pure and enlightened, and governmental affairs are well-ordered and flourishing, so there is truly nothing that requires remonstrance. Yet suppose one is faced with a major governmental affair or a matter of great state policy and wishes to speak a word on it—neither exposing faults so as to appear upright, nor flattering so as to curry favor, but обязательно wishing that…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
朝廷信之而無疑天下聞之而致慕其道
安在此諸生之所當勉以待用者幸
相與講之
問孔子言禮云禮云玉帛云乎哉樂云
樂云鐘鼓云乎哉盖以其有本也今
姑就其文言之五玉三帛見于書矣
然經禮三百曲禮三千其多有如此
者何以獨言玉帛歟鞀鼓維鏞見于
===
詩矣然八音克諧無相奪倫其義有
如此者何以獨言鐘鼓歟且古今禮
不相襲樂不相沿自伏羲時禮樂之
端已萌繼之者黃帝堯舜也其制作
之大有可舉者歟至成王時禮樂之
文已極前之者禹湯文武也其參酌
之妙有可詳者歟漢初用叔孫通朝
儀樂制大抵皆秦舊也河間獻王以
punctuated:
朝廷信之而無疑，天下聞之而致慕，其道安在？此諸生之所當勉以待用者，幸相與講之。

問：孔子言：「禮云禮云，玉帛云乎哉？樂云樂云，鐘鼓云乎哉？」盖以其有本也。今姑就其文言之，「五玉三帛」見于《書》矣，然「經禮三百，曲禮三千」，其多有如此者，何以獨言玉帛歟？「鞀鼓維鏞」見于《詩》矣，然「八音克諧，無相奪倫」，其義有如此者，何以獨言鐘鼓歟？且古今禮不相襲，樂不相沿。自伏羲時，禮樂之端已萌，繼之者黃帝、堯、舜也，其制作之大有可舉者歟？至成王時，禮樂之文已極，前之者禹、湯、文、武也，其參酌之妙有可詳者歟？漢初用叔孫通朝儀，樂制大抵皆秦舊也。河間獻王以
translation_en:
…the court trusts it without doubt, and the realm hears of it and feels admiration—wherein does this way lie? This is what you students ought to strive after as you await employment; please discuss it together.

Question: Confucius said, "Ritual, oh ritual! Does it mean no more than jade and silk? Music, oh music! Does it mean no more than bells and drums?" This is because they have a fundamental basis. Now, let us speak momentarily just of their outward forms: the "five jades and three silks" appear in the Book of Documents (Shu), yet with "three hundred major rules of ritual and three thousand minor rules of ceremony," numerous as they are, why did he speak solely of jade and silk? The "hand-drums, drums, and large bells" appear in the Book of Odes (Shi), yet with "the eight timbres in harmony, none encroaching upon the order of another," rich in meaning as they are, why did he speak solely of bells and drums? Moreover, past and present do not duplicate one another's rituals, nor do they perpetuate one another's music. From the time of Fuxi 伏羲, the beginnings of ritual and music had already sprouted; those who succeeded him were the Yellow Emperor (Huangdi 黃帝), Yao 堯, and Shun 舜—can the greatness of their creations be enumerated? By the time of King Cheng 成王, the cultural forms of ritual and music had reached their peak; those who preceded him were Yu 禹, Tang 湯, King Wen 文, and King Wu 武—can the subtlety of their deliberations and adaptations be detailed? At the beginning of the Han dynasty, the court ceremonial of Shusun Tong 叔孫通 was employed, and the musical system was on the whole the old practice of Qin. Prince Xian of Hejian 河間獻王 considered that…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
為治道非禮樂不成獻禮五百餘篇
復獻所集雅樂其有合於古歟博士
曹充請興禮樂有可考者歟唐用房
玄齡等貞觀禮雅樂大槩因隋舊也
李銳與諸學士刋定五禮其亦有合
於古歟起居舍人王仲丘又請脩明
堂祀禮有可言者歟宋以三禮圖闕
定為十五卷者誰歟改周樂章十二
===
順為十二安者其何所取義歟元起
朝儀稽古典而參以時宜者誰歟新
製大成雅樂其何所推本歟我
朝
太祖高皇帝命禮部取儀禮及采周官屬民
讀法之旨為鄉飲酒禮又謂尚書牛
諒定著禮儀宜與諸儒參詳考議甚
盛心也可言其節目歟且厭前代樂章用
punctuated: 為治道非禮樂不成，獻禮五百餘篇，復獻所集雅樂，其有合於古歟？博士曹充請興禮樂，有可考者歟？唐用房玄齡等《貞觀禮》，雅樂大槩因隋舊也。李銳與諸學士刋定《五禮》，其亦有合於古歟？起居舍人王仲丘又請脩明堂祀禮，有可言者歟？宋以《三禮圖》闕，定為十五卷者誰歟？改周樂章「十二順」為「十二安」者，其何所取義歟？元起朝儀，稽古典而參以時宜者誰歟？新製大成雅樂，其何所推本歟？我朝太祖高皇帝命禮部取《儀禮》，及采《周官》屬民讀法之旨，為鄉飲酒禮，又謂尚書牛諒定著禮儀，宜與諸儒參詳考議，甚盛心也，可言其節目歟？且厭前代樂章用…
translation_en: … held that the way of governance cannot be brought to completion without ritual and music; he presented more than five hundred chapters on ritual and further presented the court music (yayue) he had collected—did these accord with antiquity? Erudite (boshi) Cao Chong 曹充 requested the revival of ritual and music—is there anything in this that can be examined? The Tang employed the Rituals of the Zhenguan Era (Zhenguan li) compiled by Fang Xuanling 房玄齡 and others, while its court music largely followed the old practices of the Sui. Li Rui 李銳 [?] and various Scholars (xueshi) revised and fixed the Five Rites (Wuli)—did these too accord with antiquity? Imperial Diarist (qiju sheren) Wang Zhongqiu 王仲丘 further requested the revision of the sacrificial rites for the Hall of Light (Mingtang)—is there anything in this that can be discussed? In the Song, because the Illustrations to the Three Ritual Classics (Sanli tu) was defective, who was it that established a version in fifteen juan? And in changing the "Twelve Harmonies" (Shi'er shun) of the Later Zhou musical pieces to the "Twelve Tranquilities" (Shi'er an), from what was that meaning derived? In the Yuan, who was it that instituted the court ceremonial by investigating ancient canons and adapting them to the needs of the time? And in newly creating the court music of Great Perfection (Dacheng), upon what foundation was it traced and based? In our dynasty, Emperor Gaozu, the Grand Progenitor (Taizu Gaohuangdi), ordered the Ministry of Rites (Libu) to draw upon the Etiquette and Ceremonial (Yili) and to adopt the purport of the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan) regarding assembling the people to read the laws, so as to formulate the rite of the District Symposium (xiang yinjiu li). He also told Minister (shangshu) Niu Liang 牛諒 that in fixing and codifying the ritual ceremonies, he ought to consult carefully and deliberate with the various Confucian scholars—a truly magnificent intention! Can you state the specific articles and details of this? Moreover, weary of the musical pieces of previous dynasties employing …

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
諛鄙陋命尚書陶凱更製新詞又諭
禮部臣曰大成樂器以祀孔子此宜
究心甚
盛典也可舉其名義歟夫禮樂不可斯須
去身諸生尚原其本備其文以對毋
泛毋畧
punctuated: 諛鄙陋，命尚書陶凱更製新詞，又諭禮部臣曰：「大成樂器以祀孔子，此宜究心。」甚盛典也，可舉其名義歟？夫禮樂不可斯須去身，諸生尚原其本、備其文以對，毋泛毋畧。
translation_en: … [disliked how the musical stanzas used by the previous dynasty were] sycophantic, vulgar, and crude, he commanded Minister Tao Kai 陶凱 to compose new lyrics anew. He also instructed the officials of the Ministry of Rites, saying: "The musical instruments of the Great Perfection (Dacheng) are used to sacrifice to Confucius; to this you should devote thorough attention." This was truly a grand canon! Can you cite their names and meanings? Now, rites and music may not be separated from one's person even for a moment. May you students trace their origins and set forth their forms in full in your replies; do not be vague, and do not be cursory.

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
中式舉人七十五名
第一名李昕南雄府學生春秋
第二名劉實番禺縣學生詩
第三名鄭鴻香山縣學生書
第四名梁輝南海縣學增廣生易
第五名陳庸南海縣學生禮記
第六名陳政潮州府學增廣生春秋
===
第七名梁儲廣州府學生詩
第八名梁金新會縣學生書
第九名方湜東莞縣學生易

punctuated:

第七名：梁儲，廣州府學生，《詩》。
第八名：梁金，新會縣學生，《書》。
第九名：方湜，東莞縣學生，《易》。

translation_en:
Seventy-five Successful Provincial Graduates (juren):

First Place: Li Xin 李昕, student of the Nanxiong Prefectural School, specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu).
Second Place: Liu Shi 劉實, student of the Panyu County School, specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shi).
Third Place: Zheng Hong 鄭鴻, student of the Xiangshan County School, specializing in the Classic of Documents (Shu).
Fourth Place: Liang Hui 梁輝,Added-Quota Student (zengguang sheng) of the Nanhai County School, specializing in the Classic of Changes (Yi).
Fifth Place: Chen Yong 陳庸, student of the Nanhai County School, specializing in the Record of Rites (Liji).
Sixth Place: Chen Zheng 陳政, Added-Quota Student of the Chaozhou Prefectural School, specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals.
Seventh Place: Liang Chu 梁儲, student of the Guangzhou Prefectural School, specializing in the Classic of Poetry.
Eighth Place: Liang Jin 梁金, student of the Xinhui County School, specializing in the Classic of Documents.

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
四書義
斯民也三代之所以直道而行也
劉實
同考試官教諭張批論語一題作者或達於詞
而旨趣之有遺或得其旨而詞華之不足此篇究
極明暢而敷貫沉雄當是文場老將練習於紀
律者也
考試官教諭劉批此題極難作蓋欲發孤妍
於既枯求至味於不和非老手筆不能也此篇得之
===
考試官教諭吴批作論語題者直致則甓
強合則昧旨此篇詳贍當理足破羣疑
聖人言民心之公無古今之異明已之所以無毀譽
也盖好善惡惡無所私曲乃人心天理之同然聖人
豈有所毀譽自異於古今之人心哉且吾夫子既自
言於人無所毀譽矣至此復申言其故意謂世有古
今而人心之天理不殊人有古今而是非之公論常
在我之稱人之惡所以不敢損其真者誠以今日之
民即三代之時無有作惡之民所以惡其惡而無所
punctuated:
四書義

「斯民也，三代之所以直道而行也。」

劉實

同考試官教諭張批：《論語》一題，作者或達於詞而旨趣之有遺，或得其旨而詞華之不足。此篇究極明暢，而敷貫沉雄，當是文場老將，練習於紀律者也。

考試官教諭劉批：此題極難作，蓋欲發孤妍於既枯，求至味於不和，非老手筆不能也。此篇得之。

考試官教諭吴批：作《論語》題者，直致則甓，強合則昧旨。此篇詳贍當理，足破羣疑。

聖人言民心之公無古今之異，明已之所以無毀譽也。盖好善惡惡、無所私曲，乃人心天理之同然，聖人豈有所毀譽自異於古今之人心哉？且吾夫子既自言於人無所毀譽矣，至此復申言其故。意謂世有古今，而人心之天理不殊；人有古今，而是非之公論常在。我之稱人之惡，所以不敢損其真者，誠以今日之民，即三代之時無有作惡之民，所以惡其惡而無所
translation_en:
Expositions on the Four Books

"These common people are those by whom the Three Dynasties walked the straight way."

Liu Shi 劉實

Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Zhang 張: On this topic from the Analects (Lunyu), writers either achieve fluency in expression while leaving out the underlying purport, or grasp the purport while falling short in literary flourish. This essay is thoroughly clear and fluent, and its exposition and continuity are deep and vigorous; the author must be a veteran general of the examination halls, well-practiced in the rules and standards.

Comment by Examiner Instructor Liu 劉: This topic is extremely difficult to compose on, for one seeks to bring forth solitary beauty from what is already withered, and to seek the ultimate flavor in what is unseasoned—something impossible without the brush of an experienced hand. This essay has achieved it.

Comment by Examiner Instructor Wu 吳: Among those who write on topics from the Analects, being overly direct results in stiffness [?], while forcing connections obscures the purport. This essay is detailed, rich, and faithful to principle, sufficient to dispel all doubts.

The Sage speaks of how the impartiality of the people's minds knows no difference between ancient and modern times, thereby clarifying why he himself neither detracts nor overpraises. For loving the good and hating the evil without selfish partiality is the shared nature of Heavenly Principle in the human mind; how could the Sage indulge in detraction or overpraise and thus set himself apart from the human mind of ancient and modern times? Moreover, having already stated that in regard to others he neither detracts nor overpraises, our Master here further explains the reason. His meaning is that although ages are divided into ancient and modern, the Heavenly Principle in the human mind does not differ; and although people belong to ancient or modern times, impartial public judgment of right and wrong always endures. When I speak of a person's evil, the reason I dare not detract from the truth of it is truly because the people of today are the very people of the Three Dynasties who had no partiality in hating, and by whom evil was hated as evil without any…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
私曲也今日之民心惡惡以直道三代之民心惡惡
亦直道我豈得枉其惡惡之實而有所毀邪我之揚
人之善所以不敢過其實者亦以今此之民即三代
之時無有作好之民所以善其善而無所迂枉也今
此之民心好善以直道三代之民心好善亦直道我
豈得枉其善善之實而有所譽邪吾夫子言此蓋不
以春秋衰世視斯民而以三代盛時視斯民可見矣
吁毀譽者一人之私心直道者萬世之公論不以一
人之私心而掩萬世之公論非聖人之至公至平疇
===
克爾哉抑考上文有曰如有所譽者其有所試矣則
雖無所毀而亦有所譽不幾有所倚乎蓋聖人樂道
人之善惡稱人之惡是以寧有先褒之善終無豫詆
之惡雖曰先褒亦必試其將然而不苟即書所謂與
其殺不辜寧失不經罪疑惟輕功疑惟重同一善善
速惡惡緩之意也豈曰有倚乎哉
衣錦尚絅惡其文之著也故君子之道闇然而
日章
李昪
punctuated:
私曲也。今日之民心惡惡以直道，三代之民心惡惡亦直道，我豈得枉其惡惡之實而有所毀邪？我之揚人之善，所以不敢過其實者，亦以今此之民，即三代之時無有作好之民，所以善其善而無所迂枉也。今此之民心好善以直道，三代之民心好善亦直道，我豈得枉其善善之實而有所譽邪？吾夫子言此，蓋不以春秋衰世視斯民，而以三代盛時視斯民，可見矣。吁！毀譽者，一人之私心；直道者，萬世之公論。不以一人之私心而掩萬世之公論，非聖人之至公至平，疇克爾哉？抑考上文有曰：「如有所譽者，其有所試矣。」則雖無所毀，而亦有所譽，不幾有所倚乎？蓋聖人樂道人之善，惡稱人之惡，是以寧有先褒之善，終無豫詆之惡。雖曰先褒，亦必試其將然而不苟，即《書》所謂「與其殺不辜，寧失不經」、「罪疑惟輕，功疑惟重」，同一善善速、惡惡緩之意也，豈曰有倚乎哉？

「衣錦尚絅，惡其文之著也。故君子之道，闇然而日章。」
李昪
translation_en:
… selfish distortion. In the hearts of the people today, hating evil proceeds by the straight way, and in the hearts of the people of the Three Dynasties, hating evil likewise proceeded by the straight way; how could I distort the reality of their hating evil and indulge in detraction? And the reason that, in praising the good in others, I dare not exceed the reality is likewise because the people of today are the very people of the Three Dynasties who had no partiality in their likes, and therefore approved what was good without any crooked distortion. In the hearts of the people today, loving the good proceeds by the straight way, and in the hearts of the people of the Three Dynasties, loving the good likewise proceeded by the straight way; how could I distort the reality of their approving the good and indulge in overpraise? That our Master spoke thus shows clearly that he did not view these people as those of the declining age of the Spring and Autumn period, but rather viewed them as those of the flourishing era of the Three Dynasties. Alas! Detraction and overpraise are the selfish inclinations of a single individual; the straight way is the impartial judgment of ten thousand generations. Not to let the selfish inclinations of a single individual obscure the impartial judgment of ten thousand generations—without the supreme impartiality and fairness of the Sage, who would be capable of this? Yet if we examine the preceding text, which says, "If there is anyone whom I praise, there is something by which I have tested him," then although he engages in no detraction, he nevertheless does engage in praise—does this not come close to leaning to one side? The fact is that the Sage delights in speaking of the good in others and dislikes mentioning the evil in others; therefore, he would rather praise the good beforehand than ever disparage evil in advance. And even when praising beforehand, he must still have tested what the person will become and does not do so carelessly. This is the very same principle—of being swift to approve the good and slow to condemn evil—as what the Book of Documents (Shu) calls "Rather than put to death an innocent person, you will run the risk of irregularity" and "In cases of doubtful crimes, deal with them lightly; in cases of doubtful merit, deal with them heavily." How could this be called leaning to one side?

"She wears an unlined garment over embroidered silk, because she dislikes the display of its elegance. Thus the Way of the noble man is hidden and yet grows more显著 [manifest] day by day."
Li Bian 李昪

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
同考試官訓導陳批中庸題用心於內自著於
外乃朱子成言而學者不察遂至紛紛臆決茫無
定見此作其超然於倫輩者歟
考試官教諭劉批作此題者或以尚絅為為已
之心日章為為已之驗或以始則不欲其著於外終
則自有以著於外立說然皆不如用心於內自著於
外乃取朱子成語故特表而出之
考試官教諭吳批中庸義千篇一律此作獨異
於眾盖非淺之為講學者
===
中庸既釋詩以見君子之學用心於內復申言以見
君子之道自著於外盖君子之學為已故常用心於
內然既有諸內豈不自著於外乎中庸於末章復自
下學立心之始而言首因詩辭從而釋之意謂衣錦
所以美其服而又尚之以絅者惡其文采之太著也
美服所以章其身而又襲之以衣者不欲華美之外
揚也是則君子之學惟欲自得故常用力於人所不
見初不事乎表暴焉君子之學務求成已故恒修業
於人所不知初不志於烜耀焉豈非衣錦必尚絅歟
punctuated:
同考試官訓導陳批：「《中庸》題『用心於內，自著於外』乃朱子成言，而學者不察，遂至紛紛臆決，茫無定見。此作其超然於倫輩者歟！」
考試官教諭劉批：「作此題者，或以『尚絅』為為已之心，『日章』為為已之驗；或以『始則不欲其著於外，終則自有以著於外』立說。然皆不如『用心於內，自著於外』乃取朱子成語，故特表而出之。」
考試官教諭吳批：「《中庸》義千篇一律，此作獨異於眾，盖非淺之為講學者。」

《中庸》既釋《詩》以見君子之學用心於內，復申言以見君子之道自著於外。盖君子之學為已，故常用心於內；然既有諸內，豈不自著於外乎？《中庸》於末章復自下學立心之始而言，首因《詩》辭從而釋之，意謂：衣錦所以美其服，而又尚之以絅者，惡其文采之太著也；美服所以章其身，而又襲之以衣者，不欲華美之外揚也。是則君子之學惟欲自得，故常用力於人所不見，初不事乎表暴焉；君子之學務求成已，故恒修業於人所不知，初不志於烜耀焉。豈非衣錦必尚絅，斂…
translation_en:
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Chen陳 comments: "On this topic from the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong), 'applying one's mind within, and naturally becoming manifest without' is the established saying of Master Zhu (Zhu Xi 朱熹). Yet scholars fail to examine it closely, leading to a flurry of subjective conjectures without any settled view. Surely this composition stands far above its peers!"
Examiner and Instructor Liu劉 comments: "Among those who wrote on this topic, some set forth their argument by taking 'adding an unlined upper garment' as the mind bent on self-cultivation, and 'daily becoming more illustrious' as the verification of learning for oneself; others argued that 'at first one does not wish it to be manifest without, yet in the end it naturally has that whereby it becomes manifest without.' However, none of these can match 'applying one's mind within, and naturally becoming manifest without,' which draws directly upon Master Zhu's established words. Therefore, I have specially singled it out for distinction."
Examiner and Instructor Wu吳 comments: "The essays on the Doctrine of the Mean are all cast from the same mold; this composition alone stands apart from the crowd. Truly it is not the work of someone shallow in scholarly discourse."

After the Doctrine of the Mean explains the Odes (Shi) to show how the superior man in his learning applies his mind within, it further elaborates to show how the Way of the superior man naturally becomes manifest without. This is because the learning of the superior man is for his own sake, and thus he constantly applies his mind within; yet once he possesses it within, how could it not naturally become manifest without? In its final chapter, the Doctrine of the Mean speaks again from the very beginning of lower-level learning and the establishment of one's resolve. First, drawing upon the words of the Odes, it explains them, meaning to say: wearing brocade is the means to beautify one's attire, yet adding a plain unlined garment over it is because one dislikes the overly conspicuous display of its patterned brilliance; fine clothing is the means to adorn one's person, yet covering it with an outer garment is because one does not wish its splendor to be flaunted externally. Thus, the learning of the superior man seeks only self-realization, so he constantly exerts himself where others do not see, never from the outset engaging in ostentatious display; the learning of the superior man strives for self-completion, so he perpetually cultivates his work where others do not know, never from the outset aiming at dazzling renown. Is this not why, in wearing brocade, one must add an unlined garment over it, restraining [?] …

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
華以就實乎雖然君子之立心固如此然其道之著
見不可掩亦理勢之自然也故申言之若謂君子之
學雖曰惟欲自得不事表暴若闇然矣然美在其中
則有諸内者日形諸外故不求人知而人自知之君
子之學雖曰務求成己不志烜燿若暗昧矣然善有
諸己則積於此者日發於彼故不虞人譽而人自譽
之由是言之尚絅故闇然衣錦故有日章之實實理
自然之符驗焉可誣哉大抵此因前章極致之言子
思子恐學者求之高遠故言之如此下文遂及入德
===
之方謹獨之事馴致篤恭天下平其妙至於無聲無
臭則中庸之極功也先儒有言此章再叙入德成德
之序信夫
觀水有術必觀其瀾日月有明容光必照焉
鄭鴻
同考試官教諭張批孟子此節陳氏以為二
者皆於用處知其本諸作皆不能發惟此篇
得之
考試官教諭劉批此作理得而詞贍滿場
punctuated:
華以就實乎？雖然，君子之立心固如此，然其道之著見不可掩，亦理勢之自然也。故申言之，若謂君子之學，雖曰惟欲自得，不事表暴，若闇然矣；然美在其中，則有諸内者日形諸外，故不求人知而人自知之。君子之學，雖曰務求成己，不志烜燿，若暗昧矣；然善有諸己，則積於此者日發於彼，故不虞人譽而人自譽之。由是言之，尚絅故闇然，衣錦故有日章之實，實理自然之符驗，焉可誣哉？大抵此因前章極致之言，子思子恐學者求之高遠，故言之如此。下文遂及入德之方、謹獨之事，馴致篤恭天下平，其妙至於無聲無臭，則《中庸》之極功也。先儒有言：「此章再叙入德成德之序。」信夫！

觀水有術，必觀其瀾；日月有明，容光必照焉。
鄭鴻
同考試官教諭張批：孟子此節，陳氏以為二者皆於用處知其本，諸作皆不能發，惟此篇得之。
考試官教諭劉批：此作理得而詞贍，滿場
translation_en:
…[discarding?] outward splendor to pursue substance? Even so, although the gentleman establishes his mind in this manner, the fact that his Way becomes manifest and cannot be concealed is also the natural course of principle and circumstance. Therefore, the text elaborates further, as if to say: Although the learning of the gentleman aims solely at self-realization and does not engage in outward display—seeming concealed and unobtrusive—yet because beauty lies within, what is held inside is daily manifested outside; thus he does not seek to be known by others, and yet others naturally come to know him. Although the learning of the gentleman strives solely for self-completion and does not aspire to dazzling brilliance—seeming dim and obscure—yet because goodness resides in himself, what is accumulated here daily shines forth there; thus he does not anticipate the praise of others, and yet others naturally praise him. Spoken of in this light, because he wears an unlined garment over his robe, he appears unobtrusive; because he wears brocade underneath, he possesses the reality of daily becoming more illustrious. This is the natural verification of real principle—how could it be falsified? On the whole, because of the words on the ultimate perfection in the preceding chapter, Master Zisi feared that learners might seek it in what is lofty and distant, and therefore spoke thus. The text below then proceeds to the method of entering into virtue and the practice of watchfulness over oneself when alone, gradually reaching the point where, through devout reverence, all under heaven is brought to peace, its subtlety extending to having neither sound nor smell—which is the ultimate achievement of the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong). A former Confucian scholar said: "This chapter recounts once more the sequence of entering into virtue and perfecting virtue." Truly it is so!

"There is an art to contemplating water: one must contemplate its foaming waves. The sun and moon have brilliance: every crack that admits light is sure to be illuminated by them."
By Zheng Hong 鄭鴻.
Associate Examiner and Instructor Zhang 張 comments: Regarding this passage of the Mencius (Mengzi), Mr. Chen 陳氏 held that in both cases one knows the root from its functioning. None of the other essays were able to bring this out; only this piece grasped it.
Examiner and Instructor Liu 劉 comments: This piece grasps the principle and is rich in diction; in the entire examination hall…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
所無
考試官教諭吴批孟子義詞氣秀發所
謂惟陳言之務去戛戛乎其難哉者歟
大賢即物以明聖道必於其用而知其本焉夫聖人
之道用易見而本難知苟不即水之瀾與日月之必
照以觀之抑何以知之哉何則流而為川潴而為海
者水也人知水之混混而不知其有本也故觀水之
術不於歸會之所必於湍急之處則知其往過來續
而非朝滿夕除也不舍晝夜而非涸可立待也觀水
===
之瀾則知其源之有本如此若夫聖人之道發而為
小德川流無時不然者必有大德敦化者為之本焉
懸象於天代明晝夜者日月也人知日月之有明而
不知其有本也故觀日月之術不於物無遁形之間
必於容光必照之處則知其罅隙不遺而非明此暗
彼也無幽不燭而非大及小遺也觀日月於容光之
隙無不照則知其明之有本如此若夫聖人之道用
而為泛應曲當無物不有者必有一理渾然者為之
本焉然則聖道之大豈徒然而已哉抑嘗論之聖人
punctuated:
所無。
考試官教諭吴批：孟子義詞氣秀發，所謂「惟陳言之務去，戛戛乎其難哉」者歟！
大賢即物以明聖道，必於其用而知其本焉。夫聖人之道，用易見而本難知，苟不即水之瀾與日月之必照以觀之，抑何以知之哉？何則？流而為川，潴而為海者，水也；人知水之混混，而不知其有本也。故觀水之術，不於歸會之所，必於湍急之處，則知其往過來續，而非朝滿夕除也；不舍晝夜，而非涸可立待也。觀水之瀾，則知其源之有本如此。若夫聖人之道，發而為小德川流，無時不然者，必有大德敦化者為之本焉。懸象於天，代明晝夜者，日月也；人知日月之有明，而不知其有本也。故觀日月之術，不於物無遁形之間，必於容光必照之處，則知其罅隙不遺，而非明此暗彼也；無幽不燭，而非大及小遺也。觀日月於容光之隙無不照，則知其明之有本如此。若夫聖人之道，用而為泛應曲當，無物不有者，必有一理渾然者為之本焉。然則聖道之大，豈徒然而已哉！抑嘗論之：聖人
translation_en:
…is unmatched in the entire examination hall.

Comment by Examiner Wu, Instructor: This exposition on the Mencius displays a refined and vigorous spirit in its diction—is this not what is meant by "striving only to rid oneself of hackneyed words—how hard and painstaking it is!"?

The great worthy draws upon physical things to illuminate the Way of the Sages, showing that one must understand its fundamental source through its manifest function. Now, in the Way of the Sages, its function is easy to see, whereas its fundamental source is difficult to know. If one does not observe it through therippling waves of water and the unfailing illumination of the sun and moon, how then could one know it? Why is this so? That which flows to become rivers and pools to become seas is water; people know that water gushes forth abundantly, yet they do not know that it has a source. Therefore, the art of contemplating water lies not in looking at the places where it converges and gathers, but necessarily at the places where its currents are swift and surging. Then one knows that as what goes passes on, what comes continues behind, and it is not something that fills in the morning only to be emptied by evening; it flows on without ceasing day and night, and is not something whose drying up can be expected at any moment. By contemplating the rippling waves of water, one knows that its spring has a fundamental source such as this. As for the Way of the Sages, that it issues forth as "smaller virtud flowing like river currents," never ceasing at any time, must have "great virtue enriching transformation" as its fundamental source.

That which suspends its images in the heavens and alternates in illuminating day and night is the sun and moon; people know that the sun and moon possess brightness, yet they do not know that this brightness has a source. Therefore, the art of contemplating the sun and moon lies not in looking where things have no way to hide their forms, but necessarily at the tiny crevices that receive light and are unfailingly illuminated. Then one knows that no crack or fissure is left out, and it does not illuminate here while leaving it dark there; no hidden recess goes unlit, and it does not reach the great while overlooking the small. By contemplating how the sun and moon leave nothing unilluminated even in the tiniest crevices that admit light, one knows that their brightness has a fundamental source such as this. As for the Way of the Sages, that it functions in responding broadly and fittingly to every turn of circumstance, absent from nothing, must have a single, all-complete principle as its fundamental source. This being so, how could the greatness of the Way of the Sages be merely accidental! Moreover, I have ventured to discuss it thus: The sage…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
卽天地也天地之道其本不可知必觀其發為化育
流行者而後知聖人之道其本不可見必觀其發為
功用顯著者而後見故孔子賛堯舜必指其文章治
化而言詩書稱文武亦以其謨訓功烈而言至門人
記孔子亦備錄其容色言動以示人無乃皆欲人於
其用處驗其本歟後之學聖道者宜於此求焉
易義
后以財成天地之道輔相天地之宜以左右民
初九拔茅茹以其彙征吉
===
方湜
同考試官教諭劉批此題象言財成輔相所謂
賛天地之化育而與天地参聖人大有為之事也
爻言三陽在下相連而進拔茅連茹之象征行之
吉也占者陽剛則其征吉矣塲中作者多昧本義
之旨此篇暢達不窘其庶幾善究易理者歟
考試官教諭劉批易義發明無遺佳作也
考試官教諭吳批易義詞理具備初考得之
象言君道有為之極爻言陽剛類進之占夫時之泰
punctuated:
卽天地也。天地之道，其本不可知，必觀其發為化育流行者而後知；聖人之道，其本不可見，必觀其發為功用顯著者而後見。故孔子賛堯、舜，必指其文章、治化而言；《詩》、《書》稱文、武，亦以其謨訓、功烈而言；至門人記孔子，亦備錄其容色、言動以示人，無乃皆欲人於其用處驗其本歟？後之學聖道者，宜於此求焉。

易義

后以財成天地之道，輔相天地之宜，以左右民。初九，拔茅茹，以其彙，征吉。

方湜
同考試官教諭劉批：此題象言財成、輔相，所謂賛天地之化育而與天地参，聖人大有為之事也；爻言三陽在下，相連而進，拔茅連茹之象，征行之吉也，占者陽剛，則其征吉矣。塲中作者多昧《本義》之旨，此篇暢達不窘，其庶幾善究易理者歟！
考試官教諭劉批：易義發明無遺，佳作也。
考試官教諭吳批：易義詞理具備，初考得之。

象言君道有為之極，爻言陽剛類進之占。夫時之泰
translation_en:
…is indeed Heaven and Earth. As for the Way of Heaven and Earth, its fundamental source cannot be directly known; one must observe where it manifests as the flowing processes of transformation and nourishment before knowing it. As for the Way of the Sage, its fundamental source cannot be directly seen; one must observe where it manifests as prominent achievements and functions before seeing it. Therefore, when Confucius praised Yao and Shun, he invariably pointed to their cultural accomplishments and transformative governance; when the Book of Odes (Shi) and the Book of Documents (Shu) celebrated King Wen and King Wu, they likewise spoke of their counsels, instructions, and meritorious deeds; and when the disciples recorded Confucius, they too thoroughly documented his countenance, demeanor, words, and actions to show others—was not all of this from a desire that people verify the fundamental source through its outward functions? Those of later generations who study the Way of the Sage ought to seek it here.

Exposition on the Book of Changes (Yi)

"The sovereign, in harmony with this, fashions and completes the Way of Heaven and Earth, and assists the suitability of Heaven and Earth, so as to aid the people." "Nine at the beginning: Pulling up the cogon grass with its roots, each according to its kind. Going forward brings good fortune."

Fang Shi 
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor (jiaoyu) Liu: In this topic, the Commentary on the Image (Xiang) speaks of fashioning, completing, and assisting—what is called assisting in the transforming and nourishing of Heaven and Earth and forming a triad with Heaven and Earth, which is the great, active undertaking of the sage. The line statement (Yao) speaks of the three yang lines below advancing in connection with one another—the image of pulling up cogon grass with its entangled roots, signifying the good fortune of going forward; if the diviner possesses yang firmness, then going forward brings good fortune. Most candidates in the examination hall were obscure about the purport of the Original Meaning (Benyi), whereas this essay is fluent and unrestrained; perhaps its author is one who excels at investigating the principles of the Changes!
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Liu: The meaning of the Changes is elucidated without omission; it is a fine work.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Wu: In this exposition on the Changes, both diction and principle are complete; it was selected in the initial evaluation.

The Commentary on the Image speaks of the ultimate active achievement of the Way of the ruler; the line statement speaks of the prognostication of the yang and firm advancing together according to their kind. Now, when the time is one of Peace (Tai)…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而大有為則陽剛得以連類而進也聖人傳彖繫爻
安得不各極言之哉且泰之為卦乾天居下坤地居
上乃二氣交泰之象體斯象者果何如哉亦惟有為
以盡道耳是故氣化流行紛綸相續此天地之道或
有過也人君則財成之敷五典而庸五禮分四時而
奠四方于以制其過焉人物稟受時勢不同此天地
之宜或有不及也人君則輔相之立學校而明禮義
制田里而教樹畜于以補其不及焉人君之財成輔
相如此非有他也惟欲左右斯民俾復其賦受之性
===
導引斯民使遂其長養之天而已斯非君道有為之
極而何若夫泰之初九以陽來居於內正君子道長
之日遇此爻者果如何哉亦惟連類而上進耳是故
九二之爻同類之陽也初則與之相引而進有如拔
夫茅也其茹以彙而相連焉九三之爻同體之剛也
初則與之牽連而往有若茅之拔也其根以類而並
起焉初九類進之象如此征行之吉也占者陽剛則
其征也必得以行其道其吉也可知其往也必得以
遂其志其善也可見斯非陽剛類進之占而何抑論
punctuated: 而大有為，則陽剛得以連類而進也。聖人傳彖繫爻，安得不各極言之哉？且《泰》之為卦，乾天居下，坤地居上，乃二氣交泰之象。體斯象者，果何如哉？亦惟有為以盡道耳。是故氣化流行，紛綸相續，此天地之道或有過也；人君則財成之，敷五典而庸五禮，分四時而奠四方，于以制其過焉。人物稟受，時勢不同，此天地之宜或有不及也；人君則輔相之，立學校而明禮義，制田里而教樹畜，于以補其不及焉。人君之財成輔相如此，非有他也，惟欲左右斯民，俾復其賦受之性；導引斯民，使遂其長養之天而已。斯非君道有為之極而何？若夫《泰》之初九，以陽來居於內，正君子道長之日。遇此爻者，果如何哉？亦惟連類而上進耳。是故九二之爻，同類之陽也，初則與之相引而進，有如拔夫茅也，其茹以彙而相連焉。九三之爻，同體之剛也，初則與之牽連而往，有若茅之拔也，其根以類而並起焉。初九類進之象如此，征行之吉也。占者陽剛，則其征也必得以行其道，其吉也可知；其往也必得以遂其志，其善也可見。斯非陽剛類進之占而何？抑論
translation_en:
…and there is great accomplishment, then the yang and strong are able to advance together with their kind. In commenting on the Image and appending words to the Line, how could the sages not speak exhaustively of each?

Moreover, in the hexagram Tai (Peace), Qian (Heaven) rests below and Kun (Earth) rests above; this is the image of the two vital forces mingling in harmony. For one who embodies this image, how indeed should he act? It is simply to act effectively so as to fulfill the Way. Therefore, as the transformations of vital force flow onward, intricate and continuous, the Way of Heaven and Earth may at times go to excess; the ruler then regulates and completes it—spreading the Five Canonized Relationships and employing the Five Rites, dividing the four seasons and settling the four quarters—thereby curbing its excess. As human beings and things receive their endowments, times and circumstances differ, so the appropriateness of Heaven and Earth may at times fall short; the ruler then assists and furthers it—establishing schools to clarify rites and righteousness, regulating fields and dwellings to teach planting and animal husbandry—thereby remedying its deficiency. That the ruler regulates, completes, assists, and furthers in this manner is for no other reason than that he wishes solely to aid and support these people, enabling them to recover their endowed nature, and to guide and lead these people, allowing them to fulfill their heaven-ordained growth and nourishment. If this is not the ultimate of active accomplishment in the Way of the Ruler, then what is?

As for the First Nine of Tai, coming as a yang line to dwell within, it is precisely the day when the Way of the superior man is growing. For one who encounters this line, how indeed should he act? It is simply to join with his kind and advance upward. Therefore, the line of the Second Nine is a yang of the same kind; the First draws together with it and advances, just like pulling up thatch grass, whose entangled roots are connected according to their class. The line of the Third Nine is a strong line of the same trigram body; the First links together with it and goes forward, just as when thatch grass is pulled up, its roots rise together with their kind. Such is the image of the First Nine advancing with its kind; it is the auspiciousness of going forward. If the diviner possesses yang strength, then in going forward he will surely be able to practice his Way, and his auspiciousness can be known; in proceeding he will surely be able to fulfill his ambition, and his goodness can be seen. If this is not the divination of the yang and strong advancing with their kind, then what is?

Yet if we discuss…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之時之未泰致之為難時之既泰保之尤難但致泰
則關天運保泰則賴人力當此之際財成輔相以左
右民則上有其君矣三陽在下相連而進則下有其
臣矣君臣慶會明良相逢世道通泰民物亨嘉誠千
載一時也愚何幸身逢其盛
易與天地準故能彌綸天地之道仰以觀於天
文俯以察於地理是故知幽明之故原始反
終故知死生之說精氣為物游魂為變是故
知鬼神之情狀與天地相似故不違知周乎
===
萬物而道濟天下故不過旁行而不流樂天
知命故不憂安土敦乎仁故能愛範圍天地
之化而不過曲成萬物而不遺通乎晝夜之
道而知故神无方而易无體
梁輝
同考試官教諭劉批此題言易書與天地準故能彌
綸其道而窮理盡性至命三節皆聖人用易之事場
中作者往往溺於陳腐破語雷同而講欠明潔此篇
超出倫輩可直一魁
punctuated:
之，時之未泰，致之為難；時之既泰，保之尤難。但致泰則關天運，保泰則賴人力。當此之際，財成輔相以左右民，則上有其君矣；三陽在下相連而進，則下有其臣矣。君臣慶會，明良相逢，世道通泰，民物亨嘉，誠千載一時也。愚何幸身逢其盛！

「《易》與天地準，故能彌綸天地之道。仰以觀於天文，俯以察於地理，是故知幽明之故；原始反終，故知死生之說；精氣為物，游魂為變，是故知鬼神之情狀。與天地相似，故不違；知周乎萬物而道濟天下，故不過；旁行而不流，樂天知命，故不憂；安土敦乎仁，故能愛。範圍天地之化而不過，曲成萬物而不遺，通乎晝夜之道而知，故神无方而《易》无體。」

梁輝
同考試官教諭劉批：此題言《易》書與天地準，故能彌綸其道；而窮理、盡性、至命三節，皆聖人用《易》之事。場中作者往往溺於陳腐，破語雷同，而講欠明潔。此篇超出倫輩，可直一魁。
translation_en:
… it: when the times have not yet reached Peace (Tai), bringing it about is difficult; once the times have reached Peace, preserving it is even more difficult. Yet bringing about Peace depends on the revolution of Heaven's destiny, whereas preserving Peace relies on human effort. At a juncture such as this, framing and completing, assisting and regulating the courses of Heaven and Earth so as to aid the people on left and right—above, there is such a ruler; the three yang lines below advancing linked together—below, there are such ministers. Ruler and ministers meet in felicitous union, an enlightened sovereign and worthy subjects encounter one another, the Way of the world is open and at peace, and the people and all things flourish in excellence—truly a moment that comes once in a thousand years! How fortunate am I to witness this golden age in person!

"The Changes (Yi) is on a par with Heaven and Earth, and therefore can wholly encompasses and weave together the Way of Heaven and Earth. Looking up, he contemplates the patterns of Heaven; looking down, he examines the lines of Earth; thus he knows the causes of what is hidden and what is manifest. Tracing things to their beginnings and following them to their ends, he thus knows the explanation of life and death. Refined qi forms things, and the wandering soul produces change; thus he knows the conditions and appearances of ghosts and spirits. He resembles Heaven and Earth, and therefore does not contravene them. His knowledge encompasses all things, and his Way brings aid to all under Heaven; therefore he does not err. He acts versatilely yet is not swept away; he rejoices in Heaven and knows its decree, and therefore has no anxiety. He rests content in his position and is earnest in benevolence, and therefore can love. He molds and encompasses the transformations of Heaven and Earth without mistake, and intricately brings all things to completion without omission. He comprehends the Way of day and night and understands it; therefore spirit has no spatial restriction and the Changes has no fixed form."

Liang Hui 梁輝
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor (jiaoyu) Liu 劉: This topic states that the Book of Changes is on a par with Heaven and Earth and is thus able to wholly encompass and weave together their Way, while the three sections on fathoming principle, fully realizing nature, and arriving at destiny all concern the sage's application of the Changes. Writers in the examination hall often sink into clichés, with identical opening sentences and expositions lacking clarity and conciseness. This essay stands out far above its peers and is well worthy of a top ranking.

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭劉批〔易理深奧非用力精到者不能發其蘊此作得之〕
考試官教諭吳批〔易義簡明有文當是作者〕
易書等乎造化故能賛其道而無遺聖人用乎易書
必欲造其極而無間蓋易與天地準故能賛其道而
無遺也聖人用之以窮理盡性而至命豈不造其極
而無間哉大傳論易道之大意謂天之道陽而健也
易書卦爻具有天之道而與之齊地之道陰而順也
易書卦爻具有地之道而與之準惟其齊準故於天
===
地之道為能彌之使其渾然而無間綸之俾其粲然
而有條焉易道之大如此惟聖人也仰以易而觀天
文之晝夜上下俯以易而察地理之南北高深則知
其幽明之故矣推原人物之始所以生反要人物之
終所以死則知夫死生之說矣陰精陽氣聚而成物
神之伸也魂游魄降散而為變鬼之歸也又有以知
夫鬼神之情狀焉幽明死生鬼神皆陰陽之理聖人
以易而窮之非窮理之事乎若夫天地之道知仁而
已聖人之知仁則與天地相似而不違知似乎天足
punctuated:
考試官教諭劉批：〔《易》理深奧，非用力精到者不能發其蘊，此作得之。〕
考試官教諭吳批：〔《易》義簡明有文，當是作者。〕

《易》書等乎造化，故能賛其道而無遺；聖人用乎《易》書，必欲造其極而無間。蓋《易》與天地準，故能賛其道而無遺也；聖人用之以窮理、盡性而至命，豈不造其極而無間哉？《大傳》論《易》道之大，意謂天之道陽而健也，《易》書卦爻具有天之道而與之齊；地之道陰而順也，《易》書卦爻具有地之道而與之準。惟其齊、準，故於天地之道，為能彌之使其渾然而無間，綸之俾其粲然而有條焉。《易》道之大如此。惟聖人也，仰以《易》而觀天文之晝夜上下，俯以《易》而察地理之南北高深，則知其幽明之故矣；推原人物之始所以生，反要人物之終所以死，則知夫死生之說矣；陰精陽氣聚而成物，神之伸也，魂游魄降散而為變，鬼之歸也，又有以知夫鬼神之情狀焉。幽明、死生、鬼神，皆陰陽之理，聖人以《易》而窮之，非窮理之事乎？若夫天地之道，知、仁而已，聖人之知、仁，則與天地相似而不違。知似乎天，足…
translation_en:
Examiner and Confucian School Instructor Liu comments: [The principles of the Book of Changes (Yi) are profound and abstruse; unless one's effort is refined and thorough, one cannot bring forth its store of meaning. This composition achieves it.]
Examiner and Confucian School Instructor Wu comments: [The exposition of the meaning of the Changes is concise, clear, and well-written; he must be an accomplished writer.]

The Book of Changes is equal to the creative transformations of nature, and therefore it can assist their Way without omission; the sage makes use of the Book of Changes, and necessarily desires to reach its ultimate perfection without any gap. For the Changes is on a par with heaven and earth, and therefore can assist their Way without omission; when the sage uses it to exhaust principles, fulfill nature, and arrive at destiny, does he not reach its ultimate perfection without any gap? In discussing the greatness of the Way of the Changes, the "Great Commentary" (Dazhuan) means to say that the Way of heaven is yang and vigorous, and the hexagrams and lines of the Book of Changes possess the Way of heaven in full and are equal to it; the Way of earth is yin and compliant, and the hexagrams and lines of the Book of Changes possess the Way of earth in full and are on a par with it. Precisely because it is equal to and on a par with them, with respect to the Way of heaven and earth it is able to bind it together so as to make it seamlessly whole without any gap, and to sort it out so as to make it brightly ordered with distinct threads. Such is the greatness of the Way of the Changes. Only the sage, looking up, uses the Changes to observe the day and night, the above and below of the patterns of heaven, and looking down, uses the Changes to examine the south and north, the heights and depths of the configurations of earth, and thus knows the causes of the dark and the bright; tracing back to the beginning of humans and things and how they come to live, and summarizing in return the end of humans and things and how they come to die, he thus knows the explanation of life and death; yin essence and yang vital force gather to form things, which is the expansion of spirit (shen), while the ethereal soul (hun) wanders away and the corporeal soul (po) descends, dispersing to become change, which is the return of the ghost (gui), and thus he also has the means to know the conditions and appearances of ghosts and spirits. The dark and the bright, life and death, and ghosts and spirits are all the principles of yin and yang; when the sage uses the Changes to exhaust them, is this not the work of exhausting principles? As for the Way of heaven and earth, it is nothing more than wisdom and benevolence; the wisdom and benevolence of the sage resemble heaven and earth and do not contravene them. His wisdom resembles heaven, sufficient…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
以周乎萬物仁似乎地足以濟乎天下則知不過矣
知既旁行而不滯仁又不流於姑息則知仁不偏矣
由是樂乎天理又知天命故心無憂而知益深隨處
皆安而無不仁故物能愛而仁益篤曰仁曰知固有
之性也聖人以易而盡之非盡性之事乎至若天地
之化至無窮也聖人則範圍之而不過萬物之生至
不一也聖人則曲成之而不遺晝夜之道未易知也
聖人又有以兼知其妙默契其機焉夫然後可見至
神之無方變易之無體也天地萬物晝夜皆命之所
===
在也聖人用易以至之非至命之事而何哉抑攷之
說卦亦有曰窮理盡性以至於命盖此之窮理盡性
至命以聖人言乃用易之事彼之窮理盡性至命就
易書言乃作易之功所指雖殊其致一也吁易作於
聖人而亦用於聖人此聖人所以有功於易有功於
天下後世也歟
書義
至誠感神矧茲有苗禹拜昌言曰俞班師振旅
鄭鴻
punctuated:
以周乎萬物，仁似乎地，足以濟乎天下，則知不過矣。知既旁行而不滯，仁又不流於姑息，則知仁不偏矣。由是樂乎天理，又知天命，故心無憂而知益深；隨處皆安，而無不仁，故物能愛而仁益篤。曰仁曰知，固有之性也，聖人以《易》而盡之，非盡性之事乎？至若天地之化至無窮也，聖人則範圍之而不過；萬物之生至不一也，聖人則曲成之而不遺；晝夜之道未易知也，聖人又有以兼知其妙、默契其機焉。夫然後可見至神之無方，變易之無體也。天地、萬物、晝夜，皆命之所在也，聖人用《易》以至之，非至命之事而何哉？抑攷之《說卦》，亦有曰：「窮理盡性，以至於命。」盖此之窮理、盡性、至命，以聖人言，乃用《易》之事；彼之窮理、盡性、至命，就《易》書言，乃作《易》之功。所指雖殊，其致一也。吁！《易》作於聖人，而亦用於聖人，此聖人所以有功於《易》，有功於天下後世也歟！

書義
至誠感神，矧茲有苗！禹拜昌言，曰：「俞！」班師振旅。
鄭鴻
translation_en:
…to encompass all things, and his benevolence resembles Earth, sufficient to bring aid to all under Heaven; thus his wisdom does not err by excess. Since his wisdom operates ubiquituously without stagnation, and his benevolence does not degenerate into lax indulgence, neither his wisdom nor his benevolence is one-sided. Consequently, he rejoices in Heavenly Principle and also knows the Mandate of Heaven, so his mind is free from anxiety and his wisdom grows ever deeper; in every circumstance he is at peace and never lacks benevolence, so he is able to love all creatures and his benevolence grows ever more earnest. What are called benevolence and wisdom are the inherent nature; the sage fully realizes them by means of the Changes (Yi)—is this not the work of fully realizing one's nature?

As for the transformations of Heaven and Earth, they are utterly inexhaustible, yet the sage casts and encloses them so that they do not transgress; the generation of the myriad things is utterly diverse, yet the sage brings each to intricate completion so that none is left behind; the Way of day and night is not easily known, yet the sage is further able to comprehend its subtlety in full and silently accord with its pivotal mechanism. Only then can it be seen that supreme spirit has no fixed direction, and that change and transformation have no fixed corporeal form. Heaven and Earth, the myriad things, and day and night are all wherein the Mandate resides; the sage uses the Changes to reach it—what is this if not the work of reaching the Mandate?

Furthermore, if we examine the "Discussion of the Trigrams" (Shuogua), it also says: "Exhausting principle and fully realizing nature, so as to reach the Mandate." For the exhausting of principle, fully realizing of nature, and reaching of the Mandate spoken of here refer to the sage, and represent the work of using the Changes; whereas the exhausting of principle, fully realizing of nature, and reaching of the Mandate spoken of there refer to the Book of Changes itself, and represent the achievement of creating the Changes. Although what they point to differs, their ultimate import is one. Ah! The Changes was created by the sages, and was also used by the sages—is this not how the sages rendered great service to the Changes, and rendered great service to all under Heaven and to future generations!

Expositions on the Book of Documents (Shu yi)

"Utmost sincerity moves even the spirits—how much more so this ruler of Miao!" Yu bowed to the admirable words and said, "Yes!" He then led back the army and marshaled the troops.

Zheng Hong 鄭鴻

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭李批〔此篇作者多不能形容禹〕
〔益當時氣象此作得之所宜錄出〕
考試官教諭劉批〔禹謨一篇詞理俱優故表出之〕
考試官教諭吴批〔此作有雍容氣象可取〕
同列言誠能感神而遠人不足化大臣即敬然其言
而威武不復施夫至誠之道神且感格况於人乎大
禹聞益之賛遂從而弛其威武焉其一德一心可見
矣思昔苗民逆命益賛于禹而推言及此意謂真實
無妄曰誠誠能感物曰誠彼神至幽而莫測至誠則
===
可以感之神至隱而難度至誠則可以格之况有苗
亦人耳雖曰反道敗德而良心固在也豈有感之不
應而事於征伐乎雖曰侮慢自賢而善性猶存也豈
有綏之不來而煩於兵力乎伯益之賛如此禹也乃
拜以致其敬俞以然其言拜非貌恭也敬盛德之言
而屈已受善也俞非面從也契至誠之道而舍已從
人也不惟拜之而遂還師於有苗之國威不復施矣
不惟俞之而且整旅於京師之地武不復用矣其應
之之速也若江河之决其從之之易也如形影之隨
punctuated:
同考試官教諭李批：〔此篇作者，多不能形容禹益當時氣象，此作得之，所宜錄出。〕
考試官教諭劉批：〔《禹謨》一篇，詞理俱優，故表出之。〕
考試官教諭吴批：〔此作有雍容氣象，可取。〕

同列言誠能感神而遠人不足化，大臣即敬然其言而威武不復施。夫至誠之道，神且感格，况於人乎？大禹聞益之賛，遂從而弛其威武焉，其一德一心可見矣。思昔苗民逆命，益賛于禹而推言及此。意謂真實無妄曰誠，誠能感物曰誠。彼神至幽而莫測，至誠則可以感之；神至隱而難度，至誠則可以格之。况有苗亦人耳！雖曰反道敗德，而良心固在也，豈有感之不應，而事於征伐乎？雖曰侮慢自賢，而善性猶存也，豈有綏之不來，而煩於兵力乎？伯益之賛如此。禹也，乃拜以致其敬，俞以然其言。拜非貌恭也，敬盛德之言，而屈已受善也；俞非面從也，契至誠之道，而舍已從人也。不惟拜之，而遂還師於有苗之國，威不復施矣；不惟俞之，而且整旅於京師之地，武不復用矣。其應之之速也，若江河之决；其從之之易也，如形影之隨。
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Li: 〔Most authors writing on this passage cannot capture the spirit of Yu 禹 and Yi 益 at that time; this essay achieves it, and ought to be selected for publication.〕
Comment by Examiner Instructor Liu: 〔An essay on the "Counsels of Yu" (Yu mo), superior in both diction and reasoning; therefore it is singled out for publication.〕
Comment by Examiner Instructor Wu: 〔This essay has a poised and dignified spirit; it is worthy of selection.〕

When a colleague said that sincerity can move the spirits and that distant peoples are not hard to transform, the great minister immediately showed reverence and assented to his words, and martial force was no longer applied. Now, by the Way of utmost sincerity, even the spirits are moved and reached—how much more so human beings! When Great Yu heard Yi's counsel, he forthwith followed it and relaxed his martial force; their unity of virtue and unity of mind can thus be seen.

Recall how in antiquity, when the Miao people defied commands, Yi assisted Yu and extended his argument to this point. His meaning was that being true and free of falsehood is called sincerity, and that sincerity being able to move things is called sincerity. Those spirits are most obscure and unfathomable, yet utmost sincerity can move them; the spirits are most hidden and hard to gauge, yet utmost sincerity can reach them. How much more so the ruler of Miao, who is merely a human being! Although he is said to violate the Way and ruin virtue, his innate good mind certainly remains; how could it be that when moved he would not respond, so that one must resort to punitive expeditions? Although he is said to be insolent and self-righteous, his good nature still survives; how could it be that when pacified he would not come in submission, so that one must trouble with military force? Such was Boyi's 伯益 counsel.

As for Yu, he bowed to express his reverence and said "Yes!" to assent to his words. His bowing was not mere outward politeness; he revered words of abundant virtue and humbled himself to accept what is good. His saying "Yes!" was not mere compliance to someone's face; he tallied with the Way of utmost sincerity and set aside his own views to follow others. Not only did he bow to him, he forthwith withdrew his army from the state of Miao, and majesty was no longer applied; not only did he say "Yes!" to him, he moreover marshaled his troops in the region of the capital, and martial force was no longer used. The swiftness of his response was like the breaching of the Yangzi or Yellow River; the ease of his compliance was like shadow following form.

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
大禹樂善之誠夫豈有彼此之間哉嗟夫禹之征苗
奉辭伐罪欲示以威武也益之賛禹推極至理欲專
尚德化也禹遂從而班師自後世觀之益之言若迂
而不切禹之舉若懦而無勇卒之帝乃誕敷文德舞
干羽于兩階而苗自格焉是武不足以威苗而德誠
可以感人譬之春風流暢寒谷草木自皆發榮也非
有虞德教之盛惡可語此哉
越三日庚戌太保乃以庶殷攻位于洛汭越五
日甲寅位成若翼日乙卯周公朝至于洛則
===
達觀于新邑營越三日丁巳用牲于郊牛二
越翼日戊午乃社于新邑牛一羊一豕一
梁金
同考試官教諭李批召誥一題本史臣紀事之辭
作者貴切實條暢此作可嘉
考試官教諭劉批此篇於召公得民周公告
神處有發明
考試官教諭吳批行文典雅宜錄之
史臣既紀日以見大臣定都而得民成其位復紀日
punctuated:
大禹樂善之誠，夫豈有彼此之間哉？嗟夫！禹之征苗，奉辭伐罪，欲示以威武也；益之賛禹，推極至理，欲專尚德化也；禹遂從而班師。自後世觀之，益之言若迂而不切，禹之舉若懦而無勇。卒之帝乃誕敷文德，舞干羽于兩階，而苗自格焉。是武不足以威苗，而德誠可以感人，譬之春風流暢，寒谷草木自皆發榮也。非有虞德教之盛，惡可語此哉！

「越三日庚戌，太保乃以庶殷攻位于洛汭。越五日甲寅，位成。若翼日乙卯，周公朝至于洛，則達觀于新邑營。越三日丁巳，用牲于郊，牛二。越翼日戊午，乃社于新邑，牛一、羊一、豕一。」
梁金
同考試官教諭李批：《召誥》一題，本史臣紀事之辭，作者貴切實條暢，此作可嘉。

考試官教諭吳批：行文典雅，宜錄之。

史臣既紀日以見大臣定都而得民成其位，復紀日
translation_en:
… How could there be any barrier between self and others in the sincerity of Great Yu's delight in goodness? Alas! When Yu marched against the Miao, he carried out the mandate to punish the guilty, wishing to display martial might; when Yi assisted Yu with counsel, he reasoned to the ultimate principle, wishing to rely exclusively on moral transformation; and Yu thereupon followed his advice and withdrew the troops. Viewed from later ages, Yi's words might seem迂闊 (impractical and detached from reality), and Yu's action might seem timid and lacking in courage. Yet in the end, the Emperor widely diffused civil virtue, performing the shield and feather dance between the two staircases, and the Miao came to submit of their own accord. Thus martial force was insufficient to overawe the Miao, whereas virtue could truly move people—just as when the spring breeze flows freely, the grasses and trees in a cold valley naturally all burst into bloom. Without the flourishing moral instruction of the Yu (Shun) era, how could one even speak of such a thing!

"After three days, on the gengxu day, the Grand Guardian (Taibao) led the multitude of Yin to lay out the sites at the bend of the Luo River. After five days, on the jiayin day, the sites were completed. On the following day, yimao, the Duke of Zhou arrived at Luo in the morning and thoroughly inspected the layout of the new city. After three days, on the dingsi day, he offered victims at the suburban altar: two bulls. On the following day, wuwu, he sacrificed to the altar of the soil in the new city: one bull, one sheep, and one pig."
Liang Jin 梁金
Comment by Associate Examiner, Instructor (Jiaoyu) Li: This topic from the "Announcement of Shao" (Shao gao) is originally the narrative wording of the court historian. In writing on it, one values being concrete, precise, and fluent; this composition is commendable.
Comment by Examiner, Instructor Liu: This essay brings out the meaning well in the passages concerning the Duke of Shao winning the people and the Duke of Zhou announcing to the spirits.
Comment by Examiner, Instructor Wu: The style is classic and elegant; it ought to be selected for recording.

The court historian first records the days to show how the great minister established the capital and won the people's effort to complete its ritual sites, and again records the days…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
以見聖臣相都而告神備其禮盖召公之定都率民
以攻位而位成周公之觀洛舉祀以告神而禮備史
臣得不詳紀之哉昔周成王因武王之志成宅中之
業召公經理於先周公相成於後故史臣紀之曰越
三日庚戌大保乃以庶殷攻位于洛汭盖以畿內之
民不征其力四方之民又未至洛故用遷洛之殷民
闢荆棘平高下以定其城郭宗廟郊社朝市之位焉
越五日甲寅位成則庶殷之趨事咸勤召公之使民
咸悅而前朝後市左祖右社之位成焉此召公之定
===
都然也若翼日乙卯之朝周公以上相之尊行視洛
之事路車乗馬聿來新邑衮衣繡裳至止洛汭則凡
召公經營之位曰城郭曰宗廟無不徧而觀之曰郊
社曰朝市無不周而覽之尤以作洛重事不可不告
乎神故越三日丁巳用牲于郊而牲用牛二者於尊
以簡為誠也越翼日戊午乃社于新邑而牲用牛一
羊一豕一者於卑以豐為貴也郊社之祭皆告以營
洛之事此周公之相都然也噫召公之攻位位成有
以得乎民周公之至洛觀位有以告乎神神人協相
punctuated: 以見聖臣相都而告神備其禮。盖召公之定都，率民以攻位而位成；周公之觀洛，舉祀以告神而禮備，史臣得不詳紀之哉？昔周成王因武王之志，成宅中之業，召公經理於先，周公相成於後。故史臣紀之曰：「越三日庚戌，大保乃以庶殷攻位于洛汭。」盖以畿內之民不征其力，四方之民又未至洛，故用遷洛之殷民，闢荆棘，平高下，以定其城郭、宗廟、郊社、朝市之位焉。「越五日甲寅，位成。」則庶殷之趨事咸勤，召公之使民咸悅，而前朝後市、左祖右社之位成焉，此召公之定都然也。若翼日乙卯之朝，周公以上相之尊，行視洛之事，路車乗馬，聿來新邑，衮衣繡裳，至止洛汭。則凡召公經營之位，曰城郭、曰宗廟，無不徧而觀之；曰郊社、曰朝市，無不周而覽之。尤以作洛重事，不可不告乎神。故「越三日丁巳，用牲于郊」，而牲用牛二者，於尊以簡為誠也；「越翼日戊午，乃社于新邑」，而牲用牛一、羊一、豕一者，於卑以豐為貴也。郊社之祭，皆告以營洛之事，此周公之相都然也。噫！召公之攻位位成，有以得乎民；周公之至洛觀位，有以告乎神。神人協相，
translation_en:
…to show how the sage minister inspected the capital and announced it to the spirits, making the rites complete. For when the Duke of Shao (Shao Gong 召公) established the capital, he led the people to work on the sites and the sites were completed; when the Duke of Zhou (Zhou Gong 周公) inspected Luo, he performed sacrifices to announce it to the spirits and the rites were made complete—how could the court historian fail to record this in detail?

In antiquity, King Cheng of Zhou (Zhou Chengwang 周成王), carrying on the ambition of King Wu (Wuwang 武王) to accomplish the enterprise of dwelling at the center of the realm, had the Duke of Shao lay out and manage it beforehand, and the Duke of Zhou assist and bring it to completion afterward. Therefore the historian recorded it, saying: "After three days, on the gengxu day, the Grand Protector (Taibao 太保) then with the multitude of Yin worked on the sites at the bend of the Luo River (Luorui 洛汭)." For the labor of the people within the royal domain was not requisitioned, and the people from the four quarters had not yet arrived at Luo; therefore he employed the people of Yin who had been relocated to Luo to clear away brambles and thorns and level the high and low ground, so as to fix the sites for its inner and outer city walls, ancestral temple, suburban and state altars, court, and marketplace. "After five days, on the jiayin day, the sites were completed." Thus the multitude of Yin all hastened diligently to their tasks, and in the Duke of Shao's employment of the people all rejoiced, so that the sites—with the court in front and the marketplace behind, the ancestral temple on the left and the altar of the soil and grain on the right—were completed. Such was the Duke of Shao's establishing of the capital.

As for the morning of the next day, yimao, the Duke of Zhou, with the exalted dignity of Chief Minister, carried out the task of inspecting Luo. With state carriage and team of horses, he came to the new city; in dragon robe and embroidered skirt, he arrived at the bend of the Luo River. Then, of all the sites planned and laid out by the Duke of Shao—whether the inner and outer walls or the ancestral temple—there were none he did not inspect throughout; whether the suburban and state altars or the court and marketplace, there were none he did not survey completely. Moreover, considering that the building of Luo was a weighty affair that could not go unannounced to the spirits, therefore "after three days, on the dingsi day, he offered victims at the suburban altar," and the victims used were two bulls, because toward the exalted, simplicity is taken as sincerity. "On the next day, wuwu, he then sacrificed to the altar of the soil at the new city," and the victims used were one bull, one sheep, and one pig, because toward the lower, abundance is valued. The sacrifices at both the suburban altar and the altar of the soil announced the affair of constructing Luo. Such was the Duke of Zhou's inspection of the capital.

Alas! In working on the sites and bringing them to completion, the Duke of Shao had the means to win the hearts of the people; in coming to Luo and inspecting the sites, the Duke of Zhou had the means to announce it to the spirits. With spirits and men mutually assisting…

則定宅于洛，豈非萬億年敬天之休歟？抑考《洛誥》言：「予惟乙卯，朝至于洛，卜宅。」此不言者，召公於戊申已卜，周公之吉卜不殊乎召公之吉卜，周、召一心也。成王至豐告廟，此不言者，蓋成王於豐已告，成王之告祭無異乎周公之告祭，君臣一體也。有周君臣同心同德若是，其致雍熈泰和之治宜矣。

「鳳凰于飛，翽翽其羽，亦集爰止。藹藹王多吉士，維君子使，媚于天子。鳳凰于飛，翽翽其羽，亦傅于天。藹藹王多吉人，維君子命，媚于庶人。鳳凰鳴矣，于彼高岡。梧桐生矣，于彼朝陽。」
