title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
已高出百代而遠超舜湯矣當時侍從之臣莫
非臯陶伊尹下至庶民亦皆化於為善不見有
邪慝者而猶勤
聖慮作大誥三編
太宗文皇帝嗣大歷服復作為善陰隲孝順事實二
書
宣宗章皇帝用保乂民又作五倫一書固與周官時
邁所云同歸一揆欲求如舜湯之於臯陶伊尹
而詳舉其人則事存史冊考有未暇請以
===
三聖制作所及而條陳之以見我
朝教化有成而勸懲淑慝之明備焉執事所問剛
斷嫉惡不容奸偽者都御史詹徽也交不變色
德優於才者掌部事唐鐸也
大誥嘉之視
為善陰隲大理卿張文瓘之斷獄四百人無怨言
博陽侯丙吉之深厚不伐絕口舊恩者同一忠
也何可辨其優劣夙夜在公恪遵古道者左通
政茹瑺也超出羣職進膺嘉勞者知縣朱允恭
punctuated:
已高出百代而遠超舜、湯矣。當時侍從之臣，莫非臯陶、伊尹，下至庶民，亦皆化於為善，不見有邪慝者，而猶勤聖慮，作《大誥》三編。太宗文皇帝嗣大歷服，復作《為善陰隲》、《孝順事實》二書。宣宗章皇帝用保乂民，又作《五倫》一書，固與《周官》、《時邁》所云同歸一揆。欲求如舜、湯之於臯陶、伊尹而詳舉其人，則事存史冊，考有未暇；請以三聖制作所及而條陳之，以見我朝教化有成，而勸懲淑慝之明備焉。

執事所問，剛斷嫉惡、不容奸偽者，都御史詹徽也；交不變色、德優於才者，掌部事唐鐸也。《大誥》嘉之，視《為善陰隲》大理卿張文瓘之斷獄四百人無怨言、博陽侯丙吉之深厚不伐、絕口舊恩者，同一忠也，何可辨其優劣？夙夜在公、恪遵古道者，左通政茹瑺也；超出羣職、進膺嘉勞者，知縣朱允恭
translation_en:
… had already towered above a hundred generations and far surpassed Shun and Tang. At that time, the attendant officials were all the likes of Gao Yao and Yi Yin, and down to the common people, all were transformed toward doing good, with none seen to be wicked or evil. Yet He still exercised His Sacred Thought and composed the three parts of the Grand Pronouncements (Dagao 大誥). When Emperor Taizong Wen succeeded to the great hereditary mandate, He further composed the two books Unseen Retribution for Doing Good (Weishan yinzhi 為善陰隲) and True Records of Filial Piety (Xiaoshun shishi 孝順事實). Emperor Xuanzong Zhang, in order to protect and govern the people, also composed the single book Five Human Relationships (Wulun 五倫). These indeed share the exact same principle as what is said in the "Offices of Zhou" (Zhouguan 周官) and "Timely Progress" (Shimai 時邁). If one wished to seek out those like Gao Yao and Yi Yin under Shun and Tang and enumerate those men in detail, their deeds are preserved in the historical records and there is no leisure here to examine them all; I beg to set them forth item by item according to those mentioned in the works composed by the Three Sages, so as to show the success of our Dynasty's moral transformation and the clear completeness of its encouragement of the good and punishment of the evil.

As for what Your Excellency asked: the one who was resolute and decisive, hated evil, and tolerated no treachery or falsehood was Censor-in-chief Zhan Hui 詹徽; the one whose countenance never changed in his dealings with others and whose virtue surpassed his talent was Tang Duo 唐鐸, who was in charge of the affairs of a Ministry. The Grand Pronouncements praised them. Compared with Chief Minister of the Court of Judicial Review Zhang Wenguan 張文瓘 in Unseen Retribution for Doing Good, who decided four hundred criminal cases without a word of resentment, and Marquis of Boyang Bing Ji 丙吉, who was profound and generous without boasting and never spoke of his past kindnesses, they are of the exact same loyalty—how could one distinguish their superiority or inferiority? The one who was on public duty day and night and scrupulously followed the ancient way was Left Transmission Commissioner Ru Chang 茹瑺; the one who stood out above the multitude of officials and was advanced to receive praise and reward for his toil was District Magistrate Zhu Yungong 朱允恭…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
也
大誥美之與
為善陰隲開封府功曹陳泊之為政公忠注當貴
顯密令卓茂之教化大行中牟令魯恭之政有
三異者同一賢也何可議其得失他若大將軍
徐達之克元都禁戢士卒無敢侵暴人民安業
市肆不移知府費震之在漢中發廩賑飢民多
來歸立為保伍賴以存活此又我
朝將帥守令之卓卓者也
===
五倫書載之與曹彬之伐蜀申令戢下所至悅服
富弼之徒青救灾有法從者如歸見采於
為善陰隲者不同一心乎御史中丞章溢之念母
不置遂以成疾母歿居喪悲戚而卒韓太初妻
劉氏之姑疾體腐齧蛆號呼事達于
朝姑獲賜葬此亦我
朝孝子節婦之表表者也
五倫書載之與張九齡之求養累詔不許毀不勝
哀徐積之廬墓悲慟嘔血聞者泣下見采於
punctuated: 也。《大誥》美之，與《為善陰隲》開封府功曹陳泊之為政公忠、注當貴顯，密令卓茂之教化大行，中牟令魯恭之政有三異者，同一賢也，何可議其得失？他若大將軍徐達之克元都，禁戢士卒，無敢侵暴，人民安業，市肆不移；知府費震之在漢中，發廩賑飢，民多來歸，立為保伍，賴以存活。此又我朝將帥守令之卓卓者也，《五倫書》載之，與曹彬之伐蜀，申令戢下，所至悅服；富弼之徒青，救灾有法，從者如歸，見采於《為善陰隲》者，不同一心乎？御史中丞章溢之念母不置，遂以成疾，母歿居喪，悲戚而卒；韓太初妻劉氏之姑疾體腐，齧蛆號呼，事達于朝，姑獲賜葬。此亦我朝孝子節婦之表表者也，《五倫書》載之，與張九齡之求養，累詔不許，毀不勝哀；徐積之廬墓，悲慟嘔血，聞者泣下，見采於
translation_en: … [was Magistrate Zhu Yungong]. The Grand Pronouncements (Dagao) praise them. Together with those in the Secret Blessings for Doing Good (Weishan yinzhi)—Chen Bo 陳泊, Personnel Manager of Kaifeng Prefecture, who governed with fairness and loyalty and was destined in the register of fate for noble eminence; Zhuo Mao 卓茂, Magistrate of Mi, whose moral transformation was widely realized; and Lu Gong 魯恭, Magistrate of Zhongmou, whose administration produced three marvels—they share the very same worthiness; how could one debate their respective successes and failings? As for others: Generalissimo Xu Da 徐達, upon capturing the Yuan capital, restrained his soldiers so that none dared to plunder or abuse, the people remained peacefully in their occupations, and the market stalls did not shift; Prefect Fei Zhen 費震, while in Hanzhong, opened the granaries to relieve the starving, so that many people came to submit, and he organized them into mutual-security groups (baowu) by which they were able to survive. These, moreover, are outstanding examples among the generals, commanders, prefects, and magistrates of our Dynasty, recorded in the Book of the Five Human Relationships (Wulun shu). Compared with Cao Bin 曹彬, who in campaigning against Shu reiterated orders to restrain his subordinates so that wherever he went people gladly submitted, and Fu Bi 富弼, who upon being transferred [reading 徒 as 徙] to Qingzhou relieved the disaster with effective methods so that people followed him as if returning home—both selected for inclusion in the Secret Blessings for Doing Good—do they not share the very same mind? Vice Censor-in-Chief Zhang Yi 章溢 thought of his mother without ceasing until he fell ill from it, and when his mother died and he observed mourning, he passed away from grief; and the wife of Han Taichu 韓太初, née Liu 劉氏, whose mother-in-law fell ill with rotting flesh, bit the maggots and wailed aloud—when the matter reached the Court, her mother-in-law was granted an imperial burial. These too are preeminent examples among the filial sons and chaste wives of our Dynasty, recorded in the Book of the Five Human Relationships. Compared with Zhang Jiuling 張九齡, who begged to care for his parents, was repeatedly denied by imperial edict, and wasted away in unbearable grief, and Xu Ji 徐積, who dwelt in a hut by his parent's grave, grieving so bitterly that he vomited blood and moved those who heard of it to tears—both selected for inclusion in …

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
孝順事實者不同一誠乎夫勸懲旣至則邪慝者
皆化而為善猶舜湯選舉有法則不仁者皆化
而為仁於是進一賢者於衆人之中何患不賢
者之不勸拔一能者於庶民之列何患不能者
之不戒今
聖人在上監于
成憲而
列聖之制作日益敷布勤于治理而
列聖之教化日益申明敦勸懲別淑慝而野無遺賢
===
朝無幸位所以保萬萬年之
鴻業者實係於此矣愚也誦習講求出逢其盛敢
不以善自勗以惡自戒惟執事其進教之
第二問
梁儲
同考試官教諭張批小學家禮人所通習條目
意義宜無不知場中乃多泛泛直寫問目何哉
忽得此卷兼二書而條陳至終篇而益暢真莫
手也
punctuated:
《孝順事實》者，不同一誠乎？夫勸懲旣至，則邪慝者皆化而為善，猶舜、湯選舉有法，則不仁者皆化而為仁。於是進一賢者於衆人之中，何患不賢者之不勸？拔一能者於庶民之列，何患不能者之不戒？今聖人在上，監于成憲，而列聖之制作日益敷布；勤于治理，而列聖之教化日益申明。敦勸懲，別淑慝，而野無遺賢、朝無幸位，所以保萬萬年之鴻業者，實係於此矣。愚也誦習講求，出逢其盛，敢不以善自勗、以惡自戒？惟執事其進教之。

第二問
梁儲
同考試官教諭張批：《小學》、《家禮》，人所通習，條目意義，宜無不知，場中乃多泛泛，直寫問目，何哉？忽得此卷，兼二書而條陳，至終篇而益暢，真莫手也。
translation_en:
… Facts of Filial Piety (Xiaoshun shishi)—do they not share the very same sincerity? Now, once encouragement and admonition are fully carried out, the wicked and depraved are all transformed toward goodness, just as when Shun and Tang had proper methods for selecting the worthy, the unbenevolent were all transformed into the benevolent. Thus, when a single worthy person is advanced from among the multitude, what need is there to worry that the unworthy will not be encouraged? When a single capable person is elevated from the ranks of the common people, what need is there to worry that the incapable will not take warning? Today, the Sage is on the throne: taking the established statutes as his mirror, he causes the institutions of the successive Imperial Ancestors to be ever more widely disseminated; diligent in governance, he causes the moral teachings of the successive Imperial Ancestors to be ever more clearly proclaimed. Emphasizing encouragement and admonition, distinguishing the virtuous from the wicked, so that no worthy is left overlooked in the countryside and no post at court is held by undeserved favor—that whereby the grand enterprise of myriad upon myriad years is preserved truly hinges upon this. Though ignorant, I have recited, studied, and investigated these matters; coming forth in such a flourishing age, how could I dare not spur myself on with goodness and warn myself against evil? May Your Excellency offer further instruction.

Second Question
Liang Chu 梁儲
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Zhang: The Elementary Learning (Xiaoxue) and the Family Rituals (Jiali) are works universally studied by all, and there ought to be no one who does not know their articles and meanings. Yet in the examination compound most candidates wrote vaguely and superficially, or merely copied out the wording of the question—why is this? Suddenly coming upon this paper, which sets forth both books point by point and grows ever more fluent right to the end of the essay, one sees the work of a true master hand [? 莫手 for 高手/老手].

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭劉批條對無遺而辨析有理
昌黎低頭拜東野歐陽極口道聖俞正不能不
爾也
考試官教諭吴批扵小學家禮惟此甚悉其
嘗究心者歟
著垂法立教之典莫先於脩身齊家推脩身齊
家之道斯可以治國平天下此朱子小學家禮
二書所以大有功於世也即小學言之其大綱
不過立教明倫敬身三者而已教篇所載首言
===
胎教次言保傅之教次言學校君政之教又次
言師弟子之教蓋人始生則母主之既就外傅
則父主之雖不言父教而亦在其中矣至稽古
言父教乃孔子之所以教其子學詩學禮之事
為萬世立教之大法于此究極諸教之指歸故
不得不有先後之序也明倫自父子之親君臣
之義夫婦之別長幼之序至朋友之交其目有
五敬身自心術之要威儀之則衣服之制至飮
食之節其目有四然既立其大綱又舉古之聖
punctuated:
考試官教諭劉批：條對無遺，而辨析有理。「昌黎低頭拜東野，歐陽極口道聖俞」，正不能不爾也。
考試官教諭吴批：扵《小學》、《家禮》，惟此甚悉，其嘗究心者歟！
著垂法立教之典，莫先於脩身齊家；推脩身齊家之道，斯可以治國平天下。此朱子《小學》、《家禮》二書所以大有功於世也。即《小學》言之，其大綱不過「立教」、「明倫」、「敬身」三者而已。〈教〉篇所載，首言胎教，次言保傅之教，次言學校君政之教，又次言師弟子之教。蓋人始生則母主之，既就外傅則父主之，雖不言父教，而亦在其中矣。至〈稽古〉言父教，乃孔子之所以教其子學《詩》、學《禮》之事，為萬世立教之大法，于此究極諸教之指歸，故不得不有先後之序也。「明倫」自父子之親、君臣之義、夫婦之別、長幼之序，至朋友之交，其目有五；「敬身」自心術之要、威儀之則、衣服之制，至飮食之節，其目有四。然既立其大綱，又舉古之聖
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: Every point is answered without omission, and the analysis is well-reasoned. As the verse says, "Han Yu bowed his head in homage to Meng Jiao; Ouyang Xiu praised Mei Yaochen to the skies"—one truly cannot help doing just that here!

Comment by Examiner Wu, Instructor: Regarding the Elementary Learning (Xiaoxue) and the Family Rituals (Jiali), this paper alone is thoroughly conversant with them. Surely the candidate is one who has devoted deep study to them!

In composing canons that hand down models and establish instruction, nothing takes precedence over cultivating the person and regulating the family; by extending the Way of cultivating the person and regulating the family, one can then govern the state and bring peace to the world. This is why Master Zhu's two books, the Elementary Learning (Xiaoxue) and the Family Rituals (Jiali), have rendered such great service to the world. Speaking first of the Elementary Learning, its main outlines consist of nothing more than three parts: "Establishing Instruction" (Lijiao), "Clarifying Human Relations" (Minglun), and "Revering the Person" (Jingshen). What is recorded in the chapter on Instruction first speaks of prenatal instruction, next of instruction by wet nurses and governesses, next of instruction through schools and royal governance, and next again of instruction between master and disciple. For when a person is first born, the mother is in charge; once he goes out to an external tutor, the father is in charge. Thus although paternal instruction is not explicitly mentioned there, it is nonetheless implied within it. When it comes to the chapter "Examining Antiquity" (Jigu), where paternal instruction is spoken of, it cites the matter of how Confucius instructed his son to study the Odes and study the Rites, serving as the great standard for establishing instruction for ten thousand generations; here the ultimate aim of all forms of instruction is brought to its culmination, and therefore there could not but be this sequence of earlier and later. As for "Clarifying Human Relations," from the affection between father and son, the righteousness between ruler and minister, the distinction between husband and wife, and the precedence between old and young, down to trust between friends, its subheadings number five. As for "Revering the Person," from the essentials of mental disposition, the rules of dignified demeanor, and the regulations of dress, down to moderation in food and drink, its subheadings number four. Yet having established its main outlines, he further adduced the deeds of the ancient sages…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
賢立教明倫敬身之事以證之矣苟不取嘉言
以廣之則漢唐宋諸賢言及於立教明倫敬身
者無以知不取善行以實之則漢唐宋諸賢行
合於立教明倫敬身者無以見此內篇紀三代
之事迹以為小學之本源外篇具漢唐宋之言
行以為小學之支流也然又為通論一篇寓乎
其間莫非申明立教明倫敬身之畧而致意於
曰寵禄曰威儀者夫寵禄過則驕怠由以生左
傳所載公子州吁之事姑置勿論而威儀者敬
===
身之大節而立教明倫之所由以成者也諸家
釋小學者饒氏許氏而熊氏著為句解何氏纂
為集成黃氏輯為通義然皆不及括蒼于氏之
解為明備其於威儀惟西山真氏言人之動作
禮義威儀非可以强為也皆有自然之則能者
養之以福亦在敬而已矣今具載海虞吳氏之
集解此其說之最優者歟即家禮言之其大綱
不過冠昏喪祭四者而冠禮篇所載首言戒賓
次言宿賓次言迎賓又次言賓揖將冠者就席
punctuated:
賢立教、明倫、敬身之事以證之矣。苟不取《嘉言》以廣之，則漢、唐、宋諸賢言及於立教、明倫、敬身者無以知；不取《善行》以實之，則漢、唐、宋諸賢行合於立教、明倫、敬身者無以見。此《內篇》紀三代之事迹，以為小學之本源；《外篇》具漢、唐、宋之言行，以為小學之支流也。然又為「通論」一篇寓乎其間，莫非申明立教、明倫、敬身之畧，而致意於曰寵禄、曰威儀者。夫寵禄過則驕怠由以生，《左傳》所載公子州吁之事，姑置勿論；而威儀者，敬身之大節，而立教、明倫之所由以成者也。諸家釋《小學》者，饒氏、許氏，而熊氏著為《句解》，何氏纂為《集成》，黃氏輯為《通義》，然皆不及括蒼于氏之解為明備。其於威儀，惟西山真氏言：「人之動作禮義威儀，非可以强為也，皆有自然之則，能者養之以福，亦在敬而已矣。」今具載海虞吳氏之《集解》，此其說之最優者歟？

即《家禮》言之，其大綱不過冠、昏、喪、祭四者。而《冠禮》篇所載，首言戒賓，次言宿賓，次言迎賓，又次言賓揖將冠者就席，
translation_en:
… worthies in establishing instruction, clarifying human relationships, and revering the self in order to substantiate them. Yet if it had not selected "Fine Words" (Jiayan) to broaden them, there would be no way to know what the worthies of the Han, Tang, and Song spoke concerning establishing instruction, clarifying human relationships, and revering the self; and if it had not selected "Good Deeds" (Shanxing) to verify them, there would be no way to see how the conduct of the worthies of the Han, Tang, and Song accorded with establishing instruction, clarifying human relationships, and revering the self. Thus the "Inner Chapters" (Neipian) record the deeds of the Three Dynasties as the fountainhead of Elementary Learning (Xiaoxue), while the "Outer Chapters" (Waipian) set forth the words and deeds of the Han, Tang, and Song as the tributary streams of Elementary Learning. Moreover, a section of "Comprehensive Discussions" (Tonglun) is lodged within them, which does nothing other than reiterate the essentials of establishing instruction, clarifying human relationships, and revering the self, while paying special attention to what it calls "favor and emolument" and "dignified demeanor." Now, when favor and emolument are excessive, arrogance and indolence arise therefrom—the affair of Prince Zhouxu recorded in the Zuo Tradition (Zuozhuan) may be set aside without discussion for now—whereas dignified demeanor is a great principle of revering the self, and that whereby establishing instruction and clarifying human relationships are brought to completion. Among the various commentators who have explicated the Elementary Learning are Mr. Rao [Rao Lu 饒魯] and Mr. Xu [Xu Heng 許衡], while Mr. Xiong [Xiong He 熊禾] wrote the Explication by Sentences (Jujie), Mr. He [He Shixin 何士信] compiled the Collected Commentaries (Jicheng), and Mr. Huang [Huang Ze 黃澤 / Huang Chang 黃常] edited the Comprehensive Meaning (Tongyi); yet none of them is as clear and complete as the commentary by Mr. Yu [Yu Wenchuan 于文傳] of Guocang. Regarding dignified demeanor, only Mr. Zhen of Xishan [Zhen Dexiu 真德秀] said: "The rules of propriety and dignified demeanor in a person's movements cannot be forced; all have their natural principles. That the able cultivate them to attain fortune lies simply in reverence and nothing more." This is now fully recorded in the Collected Explications (Jijie) by Mr. Wu [Wu Ne 吳訥] of Haiyu; is this not the most excellent of the explanations?

Speaking of the Family Rituals (Jiali), its main outlines consist of no more than the four rites of capping, wedding, mourning, and sacrifice. What is recorded in the chapter on the "Capping Rite" (Guanli) first speaks of notifying the guests (jiebin), next of confirming the invitation to the principal guest (subin), next of welcoming the guest (yingbin), and next again of the guest bowing to the one about to be capped to take his mat, …

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
始加再加三加盖冠者成人之道始於正容體
終於正君臣親父子和長幼而禮不可以不重
故極於三加至笄禮亦有賓加笄而服背子乃
醮乃冠不用三加者以女將從陽履順故惟一
加而服背子之禮服以少致其謹始之意而示
以裁抑之道也婚禮自議婚納采納幣親迎婦
見舅姑廟見至壻見婦之父母其目有七喪禮
自初終沐浴襲奠為位飯含至小祥大祥禫其
目四十有六祭禮自時祭忌祭至墓祭其目有
===
三然既立其大綱又酌古之禮制而自附於孔
子從先進之意以準之矣苟不取雜儀以附之
則古今喪禮儀文之詳無以知不即祖禰以辨
之則宗支祭禮降殺之由無以見此古禮或不
宜於今務少加損益而不失謹名分崇愛敬之
本俗禮或不合於古亦詳加折衷而必得畧浮
文敦本實之意也然又為通禮一篇以列乎其
前莫非表明喪祭冠禮之畧而致意於曰祠堂
曰深衣者祠堂立則禮敬有所寓朱子所定四
punctuated: 始加、再加、三加。盖冠者，成人之道，始於正容體，終於正君臣、親父子、和長幼，而禮不可以不重，故極於三加。至笄禮，亦有賓加笄而服背子，乃醮、乃冠。不用三加者，以女將從陽履順，故惟一加，而服背子之禮服，以少致其謹始之意，而示以裁抑之道也。婚禮自議婚、納采、納幣、親迎、婦見舅姑、廟見，至壻見婦之父母，其目有七。喪禮自初終、沐浴、襲、奠、為位、飯含，至小祥、大祥、禫，其目四十有六。祭禮自時祭、忌祭至墓祭，其目有三。然既立其大綱，又酌古之禮制，而自附於孔子從先進之意以準之矣。苟不取雜儀以附之，則古今喪禮儀文之詳無以知；不即祖禰以辨之，則宗支祭禮降殺之由無以見。此古禮或不宜於今，務少加損益，而不失謹名分、崇愛敬之本；俗禮或不合於古，亦詳加折衷，而必得畧浮文、敦本實之意也。然又為《通禮》一篇以列乎其前，莫非表明喪、祭、冠禮之畧，而致意於曰祠堂、曰深衣者。祠堂立則禮敬有所寓，朱子所定四
translation_en: … for the first capping, second capping, and third capping. For capping is the way of becoming an adult: it begins with rectifying one's deportment and appearance, and ends with rectifying the relationship between ruler and minister, fostering affection between father and son, and harmonizing elder and younger. Because the rite must be treated with gravity, it culminates in three cappings. As for the hair-pinning ceremony for women, a guest likewise places the hairpin and the initiate puts on the sleeveless jacket (beizi), followed by the ceremonial toast and the conferring of the headdress [?]. That three placings are not used is because a woman is about to follow the yang principle and tread the path of compliance; therefore there is only a single placing, and she wears the ceremonial garment of the sleeveless jacket so as to express in some measure the meaning of care at the beginning while demonstrating the principle of restraint and modesty. In the wedding rites, from discussing the marriage, presenting the betrothal gift (nacai), presenting the bridal treasury gift (nabi), welcoming the bride in person (qinying), the bride's presentation to her parents-in-law, and her presentation at the ancestral temple, down to the groom's presentation to the bride's parents, there are seven items. In the mourning rites, from the initial death, bathing the corpse, dressing the corpse (xi), setting out offerings, establishing the mourning places, and placing rice and gems in the mouth (fanhan), down to the first-anniversary sacrifice (xiaoxiang), the second-anniversary sacrifice (daxiang), and the peace-offering sacrifice at the end of mourning (dan), there are forty-six items. In the sacrificial rites, from the seasonal sacrifices and death-day sacrifices down to the grave sacrifices, there are three items. Yet having established these main outlines, he also weighed the ritual institutions of antiquity and aligned himself with Confucius's intention of "following the men of former times" as his standard. Had he not selected miscellaneous ritual procedures to append to the work, there would be no way to know the detailed ceremonial forms of ancient and modern mourning rites; had he not distinguished them by immediate and more distant ancestors (zu and ni), there would be no way to see the reasons for the gradations and reductions in sacrificial rites between the main lineage and branch lineages. Thus, where ancient rites might not suit the present, he sought to make slight additions and reductions without losing the fundamental principles of carefully maintaining status obligations and exalting love and reverence; where popular customs might not accord with antiquity, he also carefully weighed and compromised among them so as surely to attain the intention of curtailing superficial ornament and emphasizing fundamental substance. Furthermore, he composed a chapter on "General Rites" (Tongli) to place at the front, which does nothing less than set forth the general outlines of the mourning, sacrificial, and capping rites, while devoting special attention to what are called the ancestral hall (citang) and the deep robe (shenyi). When the ancestral hall is established, ritual reverence has a place to reside—Master Zhu's regulation of four…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
龕一室之說姑置勿講而深衣平居之常服其
制度精密古服之僅存者也諸家釋家禮者蔡
氏黃氏劉氏而王氏著為深衣考朱氏復為深
衣刋誤然皆不如楊氏之說為精確其於深衣
之制惟慈谿黃氏言玉藻深衣制十有二幅深
長也深長被體故謂之深衣未甞言裳十有二
幅言裳者鄭註之誤也今具載古燕岳氏之纂
誤此其說之為得者歟愚甞考朱子小學書題
有曰皆所以為脩身齊家治國平天下之本又
===
考朱子家禮序有曰庶幾古人所以脩身齊家
之道於國家所以崇化導民之意或有小補故
知脩身齊家不可以不勉而垂法立教其功莫
大於朱子也敢舉其槩從下執事請教幸恕其
狂妄而正焉
第三問
黃廷圭
同考試官教諭李批以孔子信教二者為時政
之急可謂知本之論
punctuated:
龕一室之說，姑置勿講。而深衣，平居之常服，其制度精密，古服之僅存者也。諸家釋《家禮》者，蔡氏、黃氏、劉氏，而王氏著為《深衣考》，朱氏復為《深衣刋誤》，然皆不如楊氏之說為精確。其於深衣之制，惟慈谿黃氏言：「《玉藻》深衣制十有二幅。深，長也。深長被體，故謂之深衣。未甞言裳十有二幅，言裳者，鄭註之誤也。」今具載古燕岳氏之《纂誤》，此其說之為得者歟？愚甞考《朱子小學書題》有曰：「皆所以為脩身、齊家、治國、平天下之本。」又考《朱子家禮序》有曰：「庶幾古人所以脩身、齊家之道，於國家所以崇化導民之意，或有小補。」故知脩身、齊家不可以不勉，而垂法立教，其功莫大於朱子也。敢舉其槩，從下執事請教，幸恕其狂妄而正焉。

第三問
黃廷圭
同考試官教諭李批：以孔子信、教二者為時政之急，可謂知本之論。
translation_en:
…the theory of [four] niches in a single chamber, let us set it aside and not discuss it for now. As for the deep robe (shenyi), the ordinary attire for daily life, its system of construction is precise and detailed, and it is the only surviving example of ancient dress. Among the various scholars who have explicated the Family Rituals (Jiali) are Mr. Cai, Mr. Huang, and Mr. Liu; meanwhile, Mr. Wang wrote the Investigation of the Deep Robe (Shenyi kao), and Mr. Zhu in turn composed the Corrections of Errors on the Deep Robe (Shenyi kanwu), yet none of them is as precise and accurate as the explanation of Mr. Yang. Regarding the design of the deep robe, only Mr. Huang of Cixi stated: "In the 'Jade-Bead Pendants' (Yuzao) chapter [of the Record of Rites], the deep robe is made of twelve strips of cloth. 'Deep' means long; because it is long and covers the body, it is called the deep robe. It never says that the lower skirt has twelve strips; speaking of the lower skirt is an error in Zheng's commentary." Today this is fully recorded in the Compilation of Errors (Zuanwu) by Mr. Yue of Guyan—is this not the explanation that has grasped the truth? I have also examined Master Zhu's Note on the Elementary Learning (Zhuzi Xiaoxue shuti), which says: "All these serve as the foundation for cultivating the self, regulating the family, governing the state, and bringing peace to the world." And I have further examined the Preface to Master Zhu's Family Rituals (Zhuzi Jiali xu), which says: "Perhaps the way by which the ancients cultivated the self and regulated the family may be of some small assistance to the state's intention of exalting moral transformation and guiding the people." Thus we know that one cannot fail to exert oneself in cultivating the self and regulating the family, and in handing down models and establishing teachings, no one's merit is greater than Master Zhu's. I venture to present this general outline to ask for instruction from your clerks; I hope you will forgive my rashness and correct me.

Question Three
Huang Tinggui
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Li: Taking Confucius's two principles of trustworthiness and instruction as the urgent priorities of current governance—this can truly be called a discourse that understands the fundamentals.

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭劉批信以足兵食教以安富庶
孔子之格言也而舉以答時務盖王道之要儒
者豈真迂腐哉
考試官教諭吳批策有援據當是有識之士
足食足兵而守之以信既庶既富而加之以教
此先聖之格言而今日之急務也請因明問而
條陳之詩不云乎脩爾車馬弓矢戎兵用戒戎
作用遏蠻方此武衛之所以防禦寇亂也往者
蠻夷弗靖或遇戰而畏怯以守而弛惰誠有如
===
明問所云者今邊塵不驚而野草增綠亦已有
年矣然逸不忘勞而武事其可以不脩乎必欲
將皆智勇兵皆精銳則
朝廷具有
大法總府復有成規惟如孔子所云守之以信於
將帥也量能而後遣乘便而後用賞之必信賞
一人而莫不皆悅罰之必信罰一人而莫不皆
懼如是而使之各練習其兵士則何患戰之不
克而守之不固哉詩不云乎式遏寇虐無俾民
punctuated:
考試官教諭劉批：信以足兵食，教以安富庶，孔子之格言也，而舉以答時務，盖王道之要，儒者豈真迂腐哉！
考試官教諭吳批：策有援據，當是有識之士。
足食足兵而守之以信，既庶既富而加之以教，此先聖之格言，而今日之急務也。請因明問而條陳之。《詩》不云乎：「脩爾車馬，弓矢戎兵，用戒戎作，用遏蠻方。」此武衛之所以防禦寇亂也。往者蠻夷弗靖，或遇戰而畏怯，以守而弛惰，誠有如明問所云者。今邊塵不驚而野草增綠，亦已有年矣。然逸不忘勞，而武事其可以不脩乎？必欲將皆智勇、兵皆精銳，則朝廷具有大法，總府復有成規，惟如孔子所云「守之以信」。於將帥也，量能而後遣，乘便而後用；賞之必信，賞一人而莫不皆悅；罰之必信，罰一人而莫不皆懼。如是而使之各練習其兵士，則何患戰之不克而守之不固哉？《詩》不云乎：「式遏寇虐，無俾民…
translation_en:
Examiner and Instructor Liu comments: Using trustworthiness to make troops and food sufficient, and using instruction to secure wealth and a numerous populace, are the maxims of Confucius. To cite them in reply to current affairs captures the essence of the Kingly Way—how could Confucians truly be pedantic and impractical!
Examiner and Instructor Wu comments: The policy essay is well-supported with citations; he must be a man of insight.
To make food and troops sufficient and maintain them with trustworthiness, and once the people are numerous and wealthy to add instruction to them—these are the maxims of the Former Sage and the urgent tasks of today. Allow me to set them forth item by item in response to your perceptive inquiry. Does not the Classic of Poetry (Shijing) say: "Prepare your chariots and horses, your bows, arrows, and weapons of war, so as to be ready for military action, and to keep the southern borderlands in check"? This is how military defenses guard against and repel banditry and rebellion. In the past, when the southern tribes were restless, some were cowardly when encountering battle and lax when holding defenses, truly just as your perceptive inquiry describes. Now the border dust is undisturbed and the wild grasses grow ever greener, and it has been so for some years. Yet in ease we must not forget toil—how could military affairs not be kept in order? If we insist that commanders all be wise and brave, and soldiers all be elite and sharp, the Imperial Court already possesses great laws, and the general military command likewise has established regulations; it is simply a matter of doing as Confucius said, maintaining them with trustworthiness. With regard to commanders, gauge their abilities before dispatching them, and avail of opportune conditions before employing them. In rewarding them, be unfailingly trustworthy, so that when one man is rewarded, none fail to rejoice; in punishing them, be unfailingly trustworthy, so that when one man is punished, none fail to be struck with fear. If this is done and each is made to drill and train his troops, then what worry would there be of failing to prevail in battle or failing to hold fast in defense? Does not the Classic of Poetry say: "Repress the cruel and tyrannical, do not let the people…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
憂無棄爾勞以為王休此有司之所以牧養斯
民也往者軍旅屢興或供億而有費饋餉而致
勞亦有如明問所憂者今閭閻寧謐而禾稼登
隴亦既有年矣然安不忘危而治政其可以不
飭乎必欲吏皆循廉民皆安乂則
朝廷具有
成憲撫察亦有定法惟如孔子所云守之以信於
守令也獎勵其賢能懲戒其貪墨進之必信進
一人而莫不皆悅退之必信退一人而莫不皆
===
懼如是而使之各愛養其人民則何患賦不正
供力至重困哉流移之民許之附籍蓋
朝廷一視同仁之心也然爭奪田產以致興訟而
相攻殺此其見利而忘義也今欲絕夫意外之
虞亦惟如孔子所云教之而已誠能謹庠序之
教申之以孝弟之義則斑白者不負戴於道路
何況田產之微乎雖云流移附籍其必永建乃
家而各安生業矣頑梗之徒使之向化此
朝廷篤近舉遠之意也然田耕不賦以至丁壯而
punctuated: 憂。無棄爾勞，以為王休。」此有司之所以牧養斯民也。往者軍旅屢興，或供億而有費，饋餉而致勞，亦有如明問所憂者。今閭閻寧謐，而禾稼登隴，亦既有年矣。然安不忘危，而治政其可以不飭乎？必欲吏皆循廉，民皆安乂，則朝廷具有成憲，撫察亦有定法。惟如孔子所云，守之以信。於守令也，獎勵其賢能，懲戒其貪墨；進之必信，進一人而莫不皆悅；退之必信，退一人而莫不皆懼。如是而使之各愛養其人民，則何患賦不正供、力至重困哉？流移之民，許之附籍，蓋朝廷一視同仁之心也。然爭奪田產，以致興訟而相攻殺，此其見利而忘義也。今欲絕夫意外之虞，亦惟如孔子所云，教之而已。誠能謹庠序之教，申之以孝弟之義，則斑白者不負戴於道路，何況田產之微乎？雖云流移附籍，其必永建乃家，而各安生業矣。頑梗之徒，使之向化，此朝廷篤近舉遠之意也。然田耕不賦，以至丁壯而
translation_en:
…worry; do not abandon your services, in order to achieve praise for the King." As for how the authorities shepherd and nourish the people: in the past, when military campaigns were repeatedly launched, there were indeed expenses in supplying provisions and toil in transporting rations, just as the examiner's question worries. Today, the villages are peaceful and tranquil, and harvests have filled the fields for years now. Yet in peace one must not forget danger—how then could civil governance not be put in order? If we insist that officials all be law-abiding and incorruptible, and the people all be peaceful and well-governed, the Court possesses established statutes, and the Grand Coordinators and Investigating Censors also have fixed regulations. One need only, as Confucius said, uphold them with trustworthiness. Regarding Prefects and Magistrates, encourage the worthy and capable among them, and punish the greedy and corrupt. In promoting them, be unfailingly trustworthy—promote one person and all will be pleased; in demoting them, be unfailingly trustworthy—demote one person and all will be fearful. If by doing so we cause each of them to cherish and nourish their people, what worry will there be that taxes are not properly supplied or that corvée labor leads to severe exhaustion?

Allowing displaced migrants to attach themselves to the local household registers reflects the Court's heart of universal benevolence. Yet their contending for fields and property, to the point of instigating lawsuits and attacking and killing one another, comes from seeing profit and forgetting righteousness. If we now wish to eliminate such unexpected perils, we need only, as Confucius said, instruct them. If we can truly attend carefully to the education of the local schools and repeatedly expound the principles of filial piety and fraternal duty, then gray-haired elders will not carry loads on the roads—how much less would people fight over trifling fields and property! Even though they are displaced migrants newly attached to the registers, they will surely establish their homes permanently and each be content in their livelihoods.

Causing obstinate and unruly elements to turn toward civilization reflects the Court's intention of treating those near with generosity and uplifting those afar. Yet their cultivating fields without paying land tax, and even reaching able-bodied adulthood…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
不役于官此其見小而遺大也今欲固其率服
之志亦惟如孔子所云教之而已誠能使其壯
者以暇日脩其孝弟忠信入以事其父兄出以
事其長上則可使制挺以撻堅甲利兵何況力
役之微乎雖云頑梗向化其必畏威懷德而格
其非心矣愚也窮經固將以致用觀理亦欲以
應事故對明問不敢妄有所引以語小而遺大
語近而遺遠竊舉孔子之說足食足兵而守之
以信旣庶旣富而加之以教者如此以今觀于
===
將帥守令與流移附籍强梗向化者其所以操
縱之機設施之道在
朝廷則有
廟筭在大臣則有才畧區區愚生乃舉孔子之說雖
若迂闊不切然明問固云窮經以致用觀理以
應事經豈外孔子哉理豈舍孔子哉故始終言
之進退惟命
第四問
陳庸
punctuated:
不役于官，此其見小而遺大也。今欲固其率服之志，亦惟如孔子所云「教之」而已。誠能使其壯者以暇日脩其孝弟忠信，入以事其父兄，出以事其長上，則可使制挺以撻堅甲利兵，何況力役之微乎？雖云頑梗向化，其必畏威懷德，而格其非心矣。愚也窮經固將以致用，觀理亦欲以應事，故對明問不敢妄有所引，以語小而遺大，語近而遺遠。竊舉孔子之說，「足食足兵」而守之以「信」，「旣庶旣富」而加之以「教」者如此。以今觀于將帥、守令，與流移附籍、强梗向化者，其所以操縱之機、設施之道，在朝廷則有廟筭，在大臣則有才畧。區區愚生，乃舉孔子之說，雖若迂闊不切，然明問固云「窮經以致用，觀理以應事」，經豈外孔子哉？理豈舍孔子哉？故始終言之，進退惟命。

第四問
陳庸
translation_en:
…do not perform corvée labor for the authorities; this is a case of their seeing the small and neglecting the great. Now, if we wish to firm up their resolve to submit and obey, it lies simply in "educating them," just as Confucius said. If we can truly cause their able-bodied men, in their spare time, to cultivate filial piety, fraternal respect, loyalty, and trustworthiness—inside the home serving their fathers and elder brothers, and outside serving their elders and superiors—then they can be made to fashion wooden clubs to strike down strong armor and sharp weapons, how much more so a trifle like corvée labor? Even though they are described as obstinate and unruly people turning toward civilization, they will surely stand in awe of authority and cherish virtue, rectifying their errant hearts.

In thoroughly studying the Classics, I, an ignorant student, certainly intend to put them to practical use, and in observing principle, I likewise wish to respond to affairs. Therefore, in replying to your discerning question, I dare not recklessly cite things that speak of the small while neglecting the great, or speak of the near while neglecting the distant. Instead, I venture to bring forward the teachings of Confucius—namely, having "sufficient food and sufficient troops" while upholding them with "trustworthiness," and once the people are "numerous and enriched," adding "education" to them—in this manner. Looking today at generals and commanders, prefects and magistrates, as well as wandering migrants who have been entered into the household registers and the refractory who have turned toward civilization: as for the mechanisms for managing them and the methods for implementing policy, at court there are the strategic calculations of the imperial temple, and among the great ministers there are talent and strategy. When a mere ignorant student like myself brings forward the teachings of Confucius, although it may seem pedantic and impractical, the discerning question itself stated: "thoroughly study the Classics for practical application, and observe principle to respond to affairs." How could the Classics lie outside of Confucius? How could principle dispense with Confucius? Therefore, I have spoken of this from beginning to end, and await your command as to whether I am advanced or rejected.

Question Four
Chen Yong  陳庸

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭許批策發出三代漢唐宋諸賢
忠愛之實而歸宿於善名之重與心術之正亦是確論
考試官教諭劉批諫諍策場中皆善卷惟
此包羅無遺佳作也
考試官教諭吳批策有議論非泛泛者可比
慕士之虛名不可不重其善名愛士之學術不
可不察其心術斯言也先民固嘗及之今請以
為執事對夫諫諍者非徒然也孟子云非仁義
之道不陳又云不得其言則去此萬世諫諍之
===
法也自犯顏逆鱗叩頭流血者出而直諫之名
起自和容愉色微言婉辭者見而諷諫之名立
虛名之與善名學術之與心術判于此矣伯益
因禹之有言也而吁以致戒既曰罔失法度罔
遊于逸罔淫于樂而又曰罔違道以干譽罔咈
百姓以從欲其諫不直乎而直之名未起召康
公因王之遊歌也而詩以致警既曰有馮有翼
有孝有德以引以翼而又曰矢詩不多維以遂
歌其諫不諷乎而諷之名未立伊尹將告歸而
punctuated:
同考試官教諭許批：策發出三代、漢、唐、宋諸賢忠愛之實，而歸宿於善名之重與心術之正，亦是確論。
考試官教諭劉批：諫諍策場中皆善卷，惟此包羅無遺，佳作也。
考試官教諭吳批：策有議論，非泛泛者可比。
「慕士之虛名，不可不重其善名；愛士之學術，不可不察其心術。」斯言也，先民固嘗及之，今請以為執事對。夫諫諍者，非徒然也。孟子云：「非仁義之道不陳。」又云：「不得其言則去。」此萬世諫諍之法也。自犯顏逆鱗、叩頭流血者出，而直諫之名起；自和容愉色、微言婉辭者見，而諷諫之名立。虛名之與善名，學術之與心術，判于此矣。伯益因禹之有言也，而吁以致戒，既曰「罔失法度，罔遊于逸，罔淫于樂」，而又曰「罔違道以干譽，罔咈百姓以從欲」，其諫不直乎？而直之名未起。召康公因王之遊歌也，而詩以致警，既曰「有馮有翼，有孝有德，以引以翼」，而又曰「矢詩不多，維以遂歌」，其諫不諷乎？而諷之名未立。伊尹將告歸而…
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Instructor Xu comments: The policy essay brings out the substance of loyalty and devotion among the worthies of the Three Dynasties, Han, Tang, and Song, and concludes with the weight of a good reputation and the rectitude of the mind's intentions; this too is a sound argument.

Examiner Instructor Liu comments: On the policy question concerning remonstrance, there were many fine papers in the examination compound, but this one alone encompasses everything without omission; it is an excellent piece of work.

Examiner Instructor Wu comments: The policy essay possesses substantive discussion and is not comparable to superficial ones.

"When admiring a scholar's empty reputation, one cannot fail to value his good reputation; when cherishing a scholar's learning, one cannot fail to examine the intentions of his mind." These words were indeed touched upon by people of former times, and now I beg to offer them as my reply to Your Excellency.

Now, remonstrance is not something done in vain. Mencius (Mengzi) said: "I do not set forth anything other than the way of benevolence and righteousness." He also said: "When one's words are not heeded, one leaves." This is the standard for remonstrance for ten thousand generations. Ever since those who offended the ruler's countenance, brushed against his逆鱗 (inverted scales), and knocked their heads until blood flowed appeared, the reputation for "direct remonstrance" (zhijian) arose; ever since those who showed a harmonious countenance and pleasant expression and used subtle words and gentle phrases were seen, the reputation for "indirect remonstrance" (fengjian) was established. Empty reputation versus good reputation, and learning versus the intentions of the mind, diverged right here.

Because Yu had spoken, Boyi uttered an exclamation to deliver an admonition. Having said, "Do not fail to observe the laws and ordinances; do not wander in idleness; do not indulge to excess in pleasure," he further said, "Do not go against the Way to seek praise; do not oppose the common people to follow your own desires." Was his remonstrance not direct? Yet the reputation for directness had not yet arisen. Because the king was roaming and singing, Duke Kang of Shao (Shao Kanggong) composed an ode to deliver a warning. Having said, "You have those on whom to rely and those to assist you, men of filial piety and of virtue, to lead you on and to support you," he further said, "I haveset forth not many verses, only to accompany your own singing." Was his remonstrance not indirect? Yet the reputation for indirectness had not yet been established. When Yi Yin was about to ask leave to retire and…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
陳戒始言惟吉凶不僭在人惟天降灾祥在德
而終之以無自廣以狹人近於直矣傅說既作
相而受命始言木從繩則正后從諫則聖終之
以對揚天子之休近於諷矣董仲舒天人之策
諷也賈誼治安之疏直也而誼為絳灌所毁遂
至於見斥張蘊古大寶之箴直也張九齡金鑑
之錄諷也而蘊古為萬紀所劾遂至於見疑他
如婁敬諫漢高帝伐匈奴身受械繫而終見褒
美劉行本諫周宣帝不之顧投笏求退而上為
===
斂容此直而不慕虛名庶幾心術之正者歟谷
永之越職抗議似慷慨也而陰黨王氏劉栖楚
之叩墀死争若高亢也而欲附逢吉其與范仲
淹孔道輔之伏閤奏事叩環呼聲寇萊公之挽
衣苦諍叩榻抗論唐介寧為英州之行而必奪
寵臣之命蘇軾寧為雪堂之游而力沮新法之
行者不啻霄壤豈曰優劣而已哉善名之重心
術之正與務虛名而逞學術者不可同日語也
又如司馬相如之賦子虛鋪張景物諫絶奢侈
punctuated: 陳戒，始言「惟吉凶不僭在人，惟天降灾祥在德」，而終之以「無自廣以狹人」，近於直矣。傅說既作相而受命，始言「木從繩則正，后從諫則聖」，終之以「對揚天子之休」，近於諷矣。董仲舒天人之策，諷也；賈誼治安之疏，直也。而誼為絳、灌所毁，遂至於見斥。張蘊古大寶之箴，直也；張九齡金鑑之錄，諷也。而蘊古為萬紀所劾，遂至於見疑。他如婁敬諫漢高帝伐匈奴，身受械繫，而終見褒美；劉行本諫周宣帝，不之顧，投笏求退，而上為斂容。此直而不慕虛名，庶幾心術之正者歟！谷永之越職抗議，似慷慨也，而陰黨王氏；劉栖楚之叩墀死争，若高亢也，而欲附逢吉。其與范仲淹、孔道輔之伏閤奏事，叩環呼聲；寇萊公之挽衣苦諍，叩榻抗論；唐介寧為英州之行，而必奪寵臣之命；蘇軾寧為雪堂之游，而力沮新法之行者，不啻霄壤，豈曰優劣而已哉！善名之重、心術之正，與務虛名而逞學術者，不可同日語也。又如司馬相如之賦《子虛》，鋪張景物，諫絶奢侈；
translation_en:
…presented his admonitions, beginning with the words, "Good and ill fortune do not err in their visitations upon men; Heaven sends down calamity or blessing according to virtue," and concluding with, "Do not aggrandize yourself so as to belittle others"—this was close to direct remonstrance. When Fu Yue 傅說 became Chief Counselor and received his charge, he began by saying, "When wood follows the chalk-line it becomes straight; when the sovereign follows remonstrance he becomes sage," and ended with, "to respond to and extol the beneficence of the Son of Heaven"—this was close to indirect remonstrance.

Dong Zhongshu's 董仲舒 policy essays on Heaven and Man (Tianren zhi ce 天人之策) were indirect remonstrance; Jia Yi's 賈誼 memorial on public order and security (Zhi'an zhi shu 治安之疏) was direct remonstrance. Yet Jia Yi was slandered by Zhou Bo 周勃 (Marquis of Jiang 絳) and Guan Ying 灌嬰, and consequently was sidelined. Zhang Yungu's 張蘊古 Admonition on the Great Treasure (Dabao zhi zhen 大寶之箴) was direct remonstrance; Zhang Jiuling's 張九齡 Record of the Golden Mirror (Jinjian zhi lu 金鑑之錄) was indirect remonstrance. Yet Zhang Yungu was impeached by权萬紀 Quan Wanji, and consequently fell under suspicion.

As for others: Lou Jing 婁敬 remonstrated with Emperor Gaozu of Han 漢高帝 against campaigning against the Xiongnu 匈奴; though personally bound in fetters, he was ultimately praised and rewarded. Liu Xingben 劉行本 remonstrated with Emperor Xuan of Northern Zhou 周宣帝; when the Emperor paid him no heed, he threw down his court tablet and begged to retire, whereupon the sovereign composed his countenance. Were these not men who were forthright without coveting empty fame, coming close to rectitude of mind?

Gu Yong's 谷永 stepping beyond his office to submit defiant memorials seemed impassioned, yet he secretly sided with the Wang 王 clan; Liu Qichu's 劉栖楚 knocking his head against the palace steps in a life-or-death struggle seemed high-principled, yet he sought to attach himself to Li Fengji 李逢吉. Compared with Fan Zhongyan 范仲淹 and Kong Daofu 孔道輔 prostrating themselves at the palace gates to present memorials, knocking the door-rings and crying out aloud; or Kou準 Kou Zhun (Duke of Lai 寇萊公) pulling the Emperor's robes in bitter remonstrance and striking the couch in forthright argument; or Tang Jie 唐介 preferring banishment to Yingzhou 英州 so long as he could strip a favored minister of his appointment; or Su Shi 蘇軾 preferring exile at Snow Hall (Xuetang 雪堂) while strenuously opposing the enforcement of the New Policies—the difference is no less than that between heaven and earth! How could one speak of it merely in terms of superiority and inferiority? Cherishing a good name and possessing rectitude of mind cannot be spoken of on the same day as pursuing empty fame and parading one's scholarly skills.

Or take Sima Xiangru 司馬相如 composing the Rhapsody on Sir Fantasy (Zixu fu 子虛賦), lavishly describing scenes and objects in order to remonstrate against extravagance and put an end to luxury;…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
楊雄之賦羽獵盛言車騎諫去奢詐此諷而欲
重善名庶幾學術之美者歟相如再為通西南
之書盖喜功也而起帝窮兵之念吾丘壽王亦
有得寶鼎之對盖好大也而萌帝封禪之心其
視歐陽脩侍從規諫不諍口舌范淳夫經筵開
陳色溫氣和呂公著辨錫王勇智之語神宗聞
之而為戒范祖禹論酣酒嗜音之句哲宗聽之
而首肯者不啻天淵豈曰是非而已哉盖心術
之正善名之重與眩學術以求虛名者不可同
===
時而語也且名一也術亦一也有意於求名則
心術不正矣何取乎學術有意於眩術則善名
不重矣何取乎虛名故有伯益康公伊尹傅說
之忠愛則所以責難而順美者不訐不阿無求
於諷直之名而自得夫諫諍之道有董仲舒賈
誼張蘊古張九齡之忠愛則所以告戒而陳請
者不矯不媚無求於諷直之術而自得夫諫諍
之正忠愛者事
上之本也諫諍者忠愛之發也今欲臨大政决大計
punctuated: 楊雄之賦《羽獵》，盛言車騎，諫去奢詐，此諷而欲重善名，庶幾學術之美者歟？相如再為通西南之書，盖喜功也，而起帝窮兵之念；吾丘壽王亦有得寶鼎之對，盖好大也，而萌帝封禪之心。其視歐陽脩侍從規諫，不諍口舌；范淳夫經筵開陳，色溫氣和；呂公著辨「錫王勇智」之語，神宗聞之而為戒；范祖禹論「酣酒嗜音」之句，哲宗聽之而首肯者，不啻天淵，豈曰是非而已哉？盖心術之正、善名之重，與眩學術以求虛名者，不可同時而語也。且名一也，術亦一也。有意於求名，則心術不正矣，何取乎學術？有意於眩術，則善名不重矣，何取乎虛名？故有伯益、康公、伊尹、傅說之忠愛，則所以責難而順美者，不訐不阿，無求於諷直之名，而自得夫諫諍之道；有董仲舒、賈誼、張蘊古、張九齡之忠愛，則所以告戒而陳請者，不矯不媚，無求於諷直之術，而自得夫諫諍之正。忠愛者，事上之本也；諫諍者，忠愛之發也。今欲臨大政、决大計，
translation_en:
…and Yang Xiong 楊雄, in composing the Rhapsody on the Plume Hunt (Yulie fu), grandly described chariots and cavalry to remonstrate for the removal of extravagance and deceit—were these not instances of indirect remonstrance aimed at valuing a good name, coming close to the beauty of scholarly learning? Yet Xiangru later wrote his treatise on opening communication with the Southwest; this was out of a fondness for exploits, and it aroused the emperor's thoughts of exhausting his military forces. Wuqiu Shouwang 吾丘壽王 also presented his reply on obtaining the precious tripod; this was out of a fondness for grandiosity, and it sprouted the emperor's desire to perform the feng and shan sacrifices. Compared with Ouyang Xiu 歐陽脩 offering admonition as an imperial attendant without wrangling with tongue and lips; Fan Chunfu 范淳夫 (Fan Zuyu 范祖禹) setting forth his expositions at the Classics Colloquium with a gentle countenance and harmonious air; Lü Gongzhu 呂公著 analyzing the phrase "bestowing courage and wisdom upon the king," which Emperor Shenzong 神宗 heard and took as a warning; and Fan Zuyu discussing the line on "indulging in wine and being fond of music," to which Emperor Zhezong 哲宗 listened and nodded in approval—the difference is no less than that between heaven and the abyss; how could one merely call it a matter of right and wrong? Indeed, rectitude of mental disposition and the valuing of a good name cannot be spoken of at the same time as dazzling people with scholarly learning in order to seek an empty reputation.

Moreover, reputation is one, and technique is also one. If one has the intention to seek reputation, then the mental disposition is not upright—what is there to value in scholarly learning? If one has the intention to dazzle with technique, then a good name is not valued—what is there to value in an empty reputation? Therefore, when one possesses the loyalty and affection of Boyi 伯益, Duke Kang 康公, Yi Yin 伊尹, and Fu Yue 傅說, the way in which one urges difficult duties upon the ruler and complies with his virtues is neither abrasive nor flattering; without seeking a reputation for either indirect or forthright remonstrance, one naturally attains the Way of remonstrance. When one possesses the loyalty and affection of Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒, Jia Yi 賈誼, Zhang Yungu 張蘊古, and Zhang Jiuling 張九齡, the way in which one offers warnings and submits requests is neither affectedly defiant nor obsequious; without seeking the techniques of indirect or forthright remonstrance, one naturally attains the correctness of remonstrance. Loyalty and affection are the foundation of serving the Sovereign; remonstrance is the manifestation of loyalty and affection. Now, if one wishes to face great affairs of state, decide great plans,…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而一言之必如前數公與范仲淹寇準歐陽脩
蘇軾之當直而直非慕其名也當諷而諷非眩
其術也理有不得已也則何患
朝廷之不信而天下之不慕哉愚也學未能以及
古道未足以入官何敢出位而思但心術之正
善名之重則不可以不勉故以奉復惟垂教焉
第五問
李昕
同考試官訓導陳批禮樂一策詞不冗而事不遺
===
可美可羡
同考試官教諭張批禮樂辨析明白考據詳
備當冠策塲
考試官教諭劉批五策皆優魁選其在是矣
考試官教諭吳批五策詳贍而密皆竒宜奪元
本立而文從而禮樂之制以明功成而治定而
禮樂之制以備故歷代之制禮樂皆在功成治
定之日而用禮樂必極本立文從之美也請申
言之敬而將之以玉帛則為禮和而發之以鍾
punctuated:
而一言之，必如前數公與范仲淹、寇準、歐陽脩、蘇軾之當直而直，非慕其名也；當諷而諷，非眩其術也，理有不得已也。則何患朝廷之不信而天下之不慕哉？愚也學未能以及古，道未足以入官，何敢出位而思？但心術之正、善名之重，則不可以不勉，故以奉復，惟垂教焉。

第五問
李昕
同考試官訓導陳批：禮樂一策，詞不冗而事不遺，可美可羡。
同考試官教諭張批：禮樂辨析明白，考據詳備，當冠策塲。
考試官教諭劉批：五策皆優，魁選其在是矣。
考試官教諭吳批：五策詳贍而密，皆竒，宜奪元。

本立而文從，而禮樂之制以明；功成而治定，而禮樂之制以備。故歷代之制禮樂，皆在功成治定之日，而用禮樂，必極本立文從之美也。請申言之：敬而將之以玉帛則為禮，和而發之以鍾
translation_en:
… and to speak out once on them, one must be like those several worthies mentioned previously, as well as Fan Zhongyan 范仲淹, Kou Zhun 寇準, Ouyang Xiu 歐陽脩, and Su Shi 蘇軾—being forthright when one ought to be forthright, not out of a desire for fame; and offering indirect remonstrance when one ought to offer indirect remonstrance, not to show off one's skill, but because principle leaves no other choice. Why then worry that the Court would not trust one, or that the empire would not admire one? In my ignorance, my learning has not yet reached the level of the ancients, and my grasp of the Way is not yet sufficient to enter officialdom; how could I dare to let my thoughts overstep my station? Yet rectitude of mind and the weight of a good reputation are things I cannot fail to strive after. Therefore I respectfully submit this in reply, and only beg for your condescending instruction.

Fifth Question
Li Xin 李昕
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Chen 陳 comments: "In this policy essay on rites and music, the wording is not verbose and no historical facts are omitted; it is worthy of praise and admiration."
Associate Examiner and Instructor Zhang 張 comments: "Rites and music are analyzed and differentiated clearly, and the textual evidence is detailed and complete; it ought to top the policy essay session."
Examiner and Instructor Liu 劉 comments: "All five policy essays are excellent; the top selection surely lies right here."
Examiner and Instructor Wu 吳 comments: "The five policy essays are detailed, rich, and closely argued; all are extraordinary, and he ought to take first place."

When the fundamental is established and the outward form follows, the system of rites and music is thereby made clear; when meritorious achievements are accomplished and governance is settled, the system of rites and music is thereby made complete. Therefore, the instituting of rites and music in successive dynasties always took place on the day when meritorious achievements were accomplished and governance was settled, and in employing rites and music, they necessarily brought to perfection the beauty of the fundamental being established and the outward form following. Allow me to elaborate on this: reverence conveyed through jade and silk constitutes rites, and harmony expressed through bells …

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
鼓則爲樂敬者禮之本和者樂之本以禮之儀
文觀之經禮三百曲禮三千莫非言其經常之
禮委曲之節而禮文之重則玉帛是也以樂之
聲音觀之八音克諧無相奪倫莫非言其衆音
之備和諧之美而樂器之大則鍾鼓是也此書
所以有五玉三帛之文詩所以有賁鼓維鏞之
語孔子欲人因文以知其本故特舉而言之歟
古今禮不相襲樂不相沿伏羲制嫁娶正姓氏
以重人倫歌扶徠斲琴瑟以理情性而禮樂之
===
端肇于此矣繼之者黃帝堯舜也象天地而製
衣裳聽鳳凰而别律吕非黃帝極制作之大乎
薦玉以白繒而大章以奏頒瑞于羣后而大韶
以作非堯舜極制作之大乎至成王祭方明見
蕃服以著朝儀教樂舞序祭饗以文聲音而禮
樂之文盛于此矣前之者禹湯文武也以黑為
徽號而服収冠而黑衣作樂曰大夏而九成五
音以聽治非大禹盡參酌之妙乎服尋冠縞衣
而作大濩服冕旒玄衣而奏大武非湯武盡參
punctuated:
鼓則爲樂。敬者，禮之本；和者，樂之本。以禮之儀文觀之，「經禮三百，曲禮三千」，莫非言其經常之禮、委曲之節，而禮文之重則玉帛是也。以樂之聲音觀之，「八音克諧，無相奪倫」，莫非言其衆音之備、和諧之美，而樂器之大則鍾鼓是也。此《書》所以有「五玉三帛」之文，《詩》所以有「賁鼓維鏞」之語。孔子欲人因文以知其本，故特舉而言之歟？
古今禮不相襲，樂不相沿。伏羲制嫁娶、正姓氏以重人倫，歌《扶徠》、斲琴瑟以理情性，而禮樂之端肇于此矣。繼之者，黃帝、堯、舜也。象天地而製衣裳，聽鳳凰而别律吕，非黃帝極制作之大乎？薦玉以白繒而《大章》以奏，頒瑞于羣后而《大韶》以作，非堯、舜極制作之大乎？至成王祭方明、見蕃服以著朝儀，教樂舞、序祭饗以文聲音，而禮樂之文盛于此矣。前之者，禹、湯、文、武也。以黑為徽號，而服収冠而黑衣；作樂曰《大夏》，而九成五音以聽治，非大禹盡參酌之妙乎？服尋冠、縞衣而作《大濩》，服冕旒、玄衣而奏《大武》，非湯、武盡參
translation_en:
…and drums, it becomes music. Reverence is the foundation of ritual; harmony is the foundation of music. Viewed in terms of the ceremonial forms of ritual, the "three hundred cardinal rites and three thousand detailed rules of demeanor" speak of nothing other than its constant rites and intricate observances, while the weightiest expressions of ritual form are indeed jade and silk. Viewed in terms of the sounds and tones of music, "the eight timbres can be harmonized without encroaching upon one another's proper order" speaks of nothing other than the completeness of its many tones and the beauty of its harmony, while the greatest of musical instruments are indeed bells and drums. This is why the Book of Documents (Shu) has the passage on "the five jades and three silks," and why the Book of Odes (Shi) has the phrase "large drums and great bells." Was it not because Confucius wished people to understand the foundation by way of the outward form that he specifically singled these out to speak of them?

Across antiquity and the present, rites do not duplicate one another, and music does not simply carry on unchanged. Fuxi instituted marriage and rectified surnames to give weight to human relationships, and he sang the "Fulai" and fashioned the qin and se zithers to regulate emotions and nature; the beginnings of ritual and music originated here. Those who succeeded him were the Yellow Emperor (Huangdi), Yao, and Shun. Modeling on heaven and earth to fashion upper and lower garments, and listening to the phoenixes to distinguish the阳 (yang) and 陰 (yin) pitch-pipes (lülü)—was this not the Yellow Emperor carrying the greatness of institution-making to its utmost? Presenting jade upon white silk while performing the "Dazhang" music, and bestowingjade tallies of rank upon the various lords while composing the "Dashao" music—was this not Yao and Shun carrying the greatness of institution-making to its utmost? Down to King Cheng of Zhou, he sacrificed to the Fangming deity and gave audience to the tributary lords of the frontier domains in order to manifest court ceremonial, and he taught musical dances and ordered sacrifices and banquets in order to refine musical sounds; the cultural forms of ritual and music flourished at this point. Those who preceded him were Yu, Tang, King Wen, and King Wu. Taking black as his emblem of distinction, wearing the shou ceremonial cap and black robes, composing music called "Daxia" in nine movements, and using the five tones to attend to governance—was this not Great Yu exhausting the subtlety of deliberative adaptation? Wearing the xun ceremonial cap and white silk robes while composing the "Dahuo" music, and wearing the mian cap with pendant strings and dark robes while performing the "Dawu" music—was this not Tang and King Wu exhausting the subtlety of deliberative…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
酌之妙乎漢高帝用叔孫通朝儀與通因秦□
人所定樂制大抵皆秦舊焉武帝時河間獻王
以為治道非禮樂不成乃獻禮五百餘篇又獻
所集雅樂蓋漢去古未遠獻王所集多得古書
之遺豈無合於古者至明帝時博士曹充言漢
再受命宜興禮樂自是樂凡四品一曰大予樂
二曰周頌雅樂三曰黄門鼓吹樂四曰短簫鐃
歌樂又采百官詩頌以為登歌此其可考者也
太宗用房玄齡魏徵等所脩貞觀禮及祖孝
===
雅樂大槩皆隋舊焉玄宗時李銳與諸學士
刊定五禮蓋唐古書猶多有存諸學士所脩亦
豈無合於古者起居舍人王仲丘請依顯慶禮
脩明祀事遂以高祖配圜丘方丘太宗配雩祀
及神州地祇睿宗配明堂此其可言者也宋太
祖因博士聶崇義上所撰三禮圖詔集儒學之
士參議而閱定為十五卷者非竇儼乎儼又改
周樂章十二順為十二安者蓋取治世之音安
以樂之義也元世祖詔太保劉秉忠起朝儀徵
punctuated: 酌之妙乎？漢高帝用叔孫通朝儀，與通因秦□人所定樂制，大抵皆秦舊焉。武帝時，河間獻王以為治道非禮樂不成，乃獻禮五百餘篇，又獻所集雅樂。蓋漢去古未遠，獻王所集多得古書之遺，豈無合於古者？至明帝時，博士曹充言漢再受命，宜興禮樂，自是樂凡四品：一曰大予樂，二曰周頌雅樂，三曰黄門鼓吹樂，四曰短簫鐃歌樂；又采百官詩頌以為登歌，此其可考者也。太宗用房玄齡、魏徵等所脩《貞觀禮》及祖孝雅樂，大槩皆隋舊焉。玄宗時，李銳與諸學士刊定五禮，蓋唐古書猶多有存，諸學士所脩亦豈無合於古者？起居舍人王仲丘請依《顯慶禮》脩明祀事，遂以高祖配圜丘、方丘，太宗配雩祀及神州地祇，睿宗配明堂，此其可言者也。宋太祖因博士聶崇義上所撰《三禮圖》，詔集儒學之士參議，而閱定為十五卷者，非竇儼乎？儼又改周樂章十二順為十二安者，蓋取「治世之音安以樂」之義也。元世祖詔太保劉秉忠起朝儀，徵
translation_en:
… subtlety of deliberative adaptation? Emperor Gaozu of Han (漢高帝) adopted the court ritual of Shusun Tong (叔孫通), along with the musical institutions established by Tong on the basis of the Qin musicians [秦樂人], which were for the most part inherited from the Qin. In the time of Emperor Wu (武帝), King Xian of Hejian (河間獻王), holding that the way of governance cannot be perfected without rites and music, presented over five hundred chapters on ritual, and also presented the elegant music (雅樂) he had collected. Since the Han was not yet far removed from antiquity, what King Xian collected preserved much of the surviving legacy of ancient texts—how could there not have been parts that accorded with antiquity? By the time of Emperor Ming (明帝), the Erudite Cao Chong (曹充) argued that since the Han had received the Mandate anew, it ought to revive rites and music. From this point on, music was divided into four categories: the first was called Music of the Grand Predictor (大予樂), the second Elegant Music of the Hymns of Zhou (周頌雅樂), the third Piping and Drumming Music of the Yellow Gates (黄門鼓吹樂), and the fourth Short-Flute and Cymbal-Song Music (短簫鐃歌樂); in addition, poetic eulogies by the hundred officials were gathered to serve as the Songs of Ascent (登歌). These are the matters that can be verified.

Emperor Taizong [of Tang] (太宗) employed the Zhenguan Rites (貞觀禮) compiled by Fang Xuanling (房玄齡), Wei Zheng (魏徵), and others, as well as the elegant music of Zu Xiaosun [祖孝孫, transcribed 祖孝], which in general were mostly inherited from the Sui. In the time of Emperor Xuanzong (玄宗), Li Rui (李銳) and various Academicians edited and fixed the Five Rites (五禮). Since many ancient books still survived in the Tang, how could what the Academicians compiled not also have had parts that accorded with antiquity? Imperial Diarist Wang Zhongqiu (王仲丘) requested that the sacrificial services be revised and clarified in accordance with the Xianqing Rites (顯慶禮). Consequently, Emperor Gaozu (高祖) was associated as coadjutor at the Round Mound (圜丘) and Square Mound (方丘), Taizong at the Rain Sacrifice (雩祀) and the altar to the Spirits of Earth of the Sacred Continent (神州地祇), and Emperor Ruizong (睿宗) at the Hall of Light (明堂). These are the matters worth speaking of.

When Emperor Taizu of Song (宋太祖), prompted by the Erudite Nie Chongyi (聶崇義) presenting the Illustrations to the Three Ritual Classics (三禮圖) that he had composed, decreed that Confucian scholars be assembled to deliberate upon it, was it not Dou Yan (竇儼) who reviewed and finalized it into fifteen scrolls (卷)? That Yan also changed the twelve "Shun" (順, Harmony) musical suites of the Later Zhou into the twelve "An" (安, Peace) was because he took the meaning of the phrase "the tones of a well-governed age are peaceful and joyous." Emperor Shizu of Yuan (元世祖) ordered Grand Guardian Liu Bingzhong (劉秉忠) to institute court ritual, summoning …

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
儒生周鐸等議之而稽古典參時宜沿情而安
制者非許衡乎秉忠復奏無樂以相須則禮不
備乃製大成雅樂蓋依律運譜而成也及我
朝
太祖高皇帝功成治定制禮作樂
詔有司各行鄉飲命禮部取儀禮及唐宋之制又
采周官属民讀法之旨參定其儀府州縣每歲
孟春正月孟冬十月行之於學校民間里社以
百家為一會每季行之於里中大率皆本於正
===
齒位之說而賓興賢能春秋習射亦通行焉又
諭尚書牛諒曰定著禮儀宜與諸儒參詳考議令
百官常朝班次及奏事禮儀節目之文官僚所
通習有不待於言也且以前代樂章率用諛詞
以為容悅甚者鄙陋不稱
命尚書陶凱製宴享九奏之樂一曰本太初二曰
仰大明三曰民初生四曰品物亨五曰御六龍
六曰泰階平七曰君德成八曰聖道成九曰樂
清寧而流俗諠譁之樂悉屏去之又
punctuated: 儒生周鐸等議之，而稽古典、參時宜、沿情而定制者，非許衡乎？秉忠復奏無樂以相須則禮不備，乃製《大成》雅樂，蓋依律運譜而成也。及我朝太祖高皇帝功成治定，制禮作樂，詔有司各行鄉飲，命禮部取《儀禮》及唐、宋之制，又采《周官》属民讀法之旨，參定其儀：府、州、縣每歲孟春正月、孟冬十月行之於學校；民間里社以百家為一會，每季行之於里中。大率皆本於正齒位之說，而賓興賢能、春秋習射亦通行焉。又諭尚書牛諒曰：「定著禮儀，宜與諸儒參詳考議。」令百官常朝班次及奏事禮儀節目之文，官僚所通習，有不待於言也。且以前代樂章率用諛詞以為容悅，甚者鄙陋不稱，命尚書陶凱製宴享九奏之樂：一曰《本太初》，二曰《仰大明》，三曰《民初生》，四曰《品物亨》，五曰《御六龍》，六曰《泰階平》，七曰《君德成》，八曰《聖道成》，九曰《樂清寧》，而流俗諠譁之樂悉屏去之。又
translation_en:
…Confucian scholars such as Zhou Duo 周鐸 and others to deliberate on them, yet was it not Xu Heng 許衡 who examined ancient canons, consulted the needs of the times, and followed human feelings to establish the system [reading 定 for 安]? Liu Bingzhong 劉秉忠 further memorialized that without music to complement them, the rites would be incomplete; thus they created the Dacheng 大成 (Great Completion) court music, which was composed by applying musical notation in accordance with the pitch-pipes.

When the Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu Gaohuangdi 太祖高皇帝) of our dynasty had accomplished his achievements and stabilized the governance, he instituted rites and created music. He decreed that the authorities in each locality conduct the Community Wine-Drinking Rite (xiangyin 鄉飲), and ordered the Ministry of Rites (Libu 禮部) to take the Book of Etiquette and Ceremonial (Yili 儀禮) together with the institutions of the Tang and Song, and also to adopt the purport of assembling the people to read the laws in the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan 周官), so as to deliberate upon and determine the ceremonial: prefectures, subprefectures, and counties were to perform it in the schools each year in the first month of spring and the first month of winter; among the people, rural communities (lishe 里社) formed associations of one hundred families and performed it in their neighborhoods every season. In general, all of this was rooted in the principle of rectifying precedence by age, while honoring and recommending the worthy and able and practicing archery in spring and autumn were also universally carried out therein.

He further instructed Minister Niu Liang 牛諒, saying: "In fixing and setting down the ritual ceremonies, you should consult and deliberate carefully with the various Confucian scholars." The detailed regulations ordered for the ranking of all officials at regular court audiences and the ceremonies for presenting memorials are thoroughly practiced by the bureaucracy and need not be spoken of here. Moreover, because the musical pieces of previous dynasties generally used flattering words in order to curry favor, and at worst were vulgar and unbefitting, he ordered Minister Tao Kai 陶凱 to compose the music in nine performances for state banquets: the first is called "Rooted in the Grand Beginning" (Ben taichu 本太初); the second, "Looking Up to the Great Ming" (Yang Daming 仰大明); the third, "The First Birth of the People" (Min chusheng 民初生); the fourth, "All Things Flourish" (Pinwu heng 品物亨); the fifth, "Driving the Six Dragons" (Yu liulong 御六龍); the sixth, "The Grand Steps Are Level" (Taijie ping 泰階平); the seventh, "The Sovereign's Virtue Is Perfected" (Junde cheng 君德成); the eighth, "The Sagely Way Is Perfected" (Shengdao cheng 聖道成); and the ninth, "Rejoicing in Purity and Tranquility" (Le qingning 樂清寧). Popular and clamorous music was entirely banished. He also…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
諭禮部臣曰大成樂器以祀孔子此宜究心今登
歌樂舞酌獻迎送名義之詳學校所通肄亦不
待贅也惟禮樂之本所謂敬與和者則斯須不
可以去身而禮樂之制所謂明與備者必見聞
而後有所識愚也何幸生
今之世而得昌言其盛哉謹對
punctuated: 諭禮部臣曰：「大成樂器，以祀孔子，此宜究心。」今登歌樂舞、酌獻迎送名義之詳，學校所通肄，亦不待贅也。惟禮樂之本，所謂敬與和者，則斯須不可以去身；而禮樂之制，所謂明與備者，必見聞而後有所識。愚也何幸生今之世，而得昌言其盛哉！謹對。
translation_en: …instructed the officials of the Ministry of Rites, saying: "The musical instruments for the Great Completeness (Dacheng) rites are used to sacrifice to Confucius; to this you should devote thorough attention." Today, the detailed meanings and names of the terrace-platform songs, musical dances, libation offerings, and welcoming and sending off of the spirits are universally practiced in the schools, so there is no need to elaborate further on them either. Only the foundation of rites and music—what are called reverence and harmony—must not depart from one's person even for a moment; whereas the institutions of rites and music—what are called clarity and completeness—must first be seen and heard before they can be understood. How fortunate am I, in my ignorance, to be born in the present age and to be able to speak forthrightly of its magnificence! I respectfully reply.

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣東鄉試錄後序
皇朝設科取士逾百年每三年大比
上詔禮部申飭方岳祗舉
舊章方岳重臣預聘儒碩司考校憲
臣預汰冗濫嚴防範協恭萃和咸
勤罔怠而士之升自庠序舉于山
林拔于戎伍者亦奮志厲氣鼓勇
陳文藝寅敬罔肆上下胥
丕應同一寅畏奮庸之心
也抑何至哉廣東甲午鄉試璣等
叨職主司凡命題考校第貢士之
名錄中式之文刻為小錄一循其
舊而執事之敬求賢之誠恒若不
及罔敢斁思焉洪惟
天眷
聖明保佑申命純明不已故篤生賢俊
punctuated:
廣東鄉試錄後序
皇朝設科取士，逾百年。每三年大比，上詔禮部，申飭方岳，祗舉舊章。方岳重臣，預聘儒碩司考校；憲臣預汰冗濫，嚴防範。協恭萃和，咸勤罔怠。而士之升自庠序、舉于山林、拔于戎伍者，亦奮志厲氣，鼓勇陳文藝，寅敬罔肆。上下胥丕應，同一寅畏奮庸之心也，抑何至哉！廣東甲午鄉試，璣等叨職主司，凡命題、考校、第貢士之名、錄中式之文，刻為小錄，一循其舊。而執事之敬、求賢之誠，恒若不及，罔敢斁思焉。洪惟天眷聖明，保佑申命，純明不已，故篤生賢俊，
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

Our august dynasty has established the examination system to select scholars for over a hundred years. Every three years at the great triennial competition, the Emperor issues an edict to the Ministry of Rites to instruct the senior provincial officials to reverently carry out the established statutes. The senior provincial administrative officials in advance invite erudite Confucians to take charge of the examining and grading, while the provincial surveillance officials in advance weed out the superfluous and unqualified and strictly enforce the regulations and precautions. Working together in reverence and gathering in harmony, all are diligent and never remiss. Meanwhile, the scholars—whether promoted from the local schools, recommended from retirement in the mountains and forests, or selected from the military ranks—also rouse their ambitions and sharpen their spirits, summoning their courage to display their literary arts in reverent respect without negligence. Above and below mutually respond on a grand scale, sharing the same mind of reverent awe and striving for meritorious service—how supreme this is!

In the jiawu (1474) Provincial Examination of Guangdong, I, [Wang] Ji 璣, and my colleagues had the undeserved honor of serving as the chief examiners. In all matters of setting the questions, examining and grading, ranking the names of the tribute scholars, and recording the essays that met the standard to be engraved as this brief record, we followed the old precedents in every respect. Yet in our reverence in performing our duties and our sincerity in seeking out the worthy, we constantly felt as though we were falling short, never daring to grow weary in our thoughts.

Looking upon the grand scheme, Heaven favors the Sacred and Enlightened Ruler, protecting and repeatedly conferring its mandate upon him with unceasing purity and brilliance, and therefore it richly brings forth worthy andoutstanding talents…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
無間遐邇雖海隅嶺表譽髦勃興
惟
聖天子秉哲貴德克承
天休簡賢乂民慎終如始惟小大庶臣
欽若
德意進賢匡
國竭忠效職惟爾諸士子漸被
清□□□□侯頖藏脩丘壑詩書禮樂
□□□久仁義忠信存養宜深矧
茲英華之發言有章而文有則獲
登名鄉舉將循資以有祿位矣然
文之中式特進身入官之階耳若
夫潤身以德任官以事德脩于明
事成于畏明之則德無或昧畏之
則事無或隳德不昧而恒明則有
化事不隳而恒立則有功化行功
punctuated: 無間遐邇，雖海隅嶺表，譽髦勃興。惟聖天子秉哲貴德，克承天休，簡賢乂民，慎終如始。惟小大庶臣，欽若德意，進賢匡國，竭忠效職。惟爾諸士子，漸被清□□□□侯頖，藏脩丘壑，詩書禮樂，□□□久，仁義忠信，存養宜深。矧茲英華之發，言有章而文有則，獲登名鄉舉，將循資以有祿位矣。然文之中式，特進身入官之階耳。若夫潤身以德，任官以事；德脩于明，事成于畏。明之則德無或昧，畏之則事無或隳。德不昧而恒明則有化，事不隳而恒立則有功。化行功
translation_en: …without distinction between far and near; even along the coastal corners and beyond the Southern Ranges, renowned talents rise up flourishingly. The Sacred Son of Heaven holds fast to wisdom and prizes virtue, able to receive the blessings of Heaven, selecting the worthy to govern the people, as cautious at the end as at the beginning. All the various officials, great and small, reverently conform to His virtuous intent, advancing the worthy to assist the state, exhausting their loyalty in performing their duties. As for all you scholars, imbued with the pure [grace? …] in the local schools, or retiring to cultivate yourselves among hills and valleys, your [learning in?] the Odes, Documents, Rites, and Music has been long, and your preservation and nourishment of benevolence, righteousness, loyalty, and faithfulness ought to be deep. Moreover, with this blossoming of your brilliance, your words have pattern and your writings have standards; having succeeded in placing your names on the list of the provincial examination, you will follow the sequence of qualifications to hold salaried office. Yet for one's writing to meet the standard is merely the stepping-stone for advancing oneself and entering officialdom. As for enriching the person through virtue and fulfilling office through service, virtue is cultivated through clarity, and affairs are accomplished through reverent caution. When one is clear about it, virtue is never obscured; when one treats it with reverent caution, affairs are never ruined. When virtue is not obscured and remains constantly bright, there is moral transformation; when affairs are not ruined and remain constantly established, there is achievement. When transformation proceeds and achievement…

title: 成化十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣可以配天命賛
皇猷可以共天職理天民而天之付畀
於我者斯無愧焉天且不愧况怍
於人乎垂聲炳耀永世無窮諸士
子其以是自勉
成化十年秋八月旣望江西廣信
府鉛山縣儒學教諭劉璣謹序
punctuated:
廣，可以配天命、賛皇猷，可以共天職、理天民，而天之付畀於我者斯無愧焉。天且不愧，况怍於人乎？垂聲炳耀，永世無窮，諸士子其以是自勉。
成化十年秋八月旣望，江西廣信府鉛山縣儒學教諭劉璣謹序。
translation_en:
… extends widely, one can match the Mandate of Heaven and assist the Imperial plan; one can share in the duties of Heaven and govern the people of Heaven, and thus feel no shame before what Heaven has entrusted to us. If one feels no shame even before Heaven, how much less will one feel abashed before men? Leaving behind a brilliant reputation that will endure endlessly through the ages—may all you scholars strive for this!
Respectfully prefaced on the sixteenth day of the eighth month in the autumn of the tenth year of the Chenghua reign [1474] by Liu Ji 劉璣, Instructor in the Confucian School of Yanshan County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi.
